03Chapter 3 · Error Analysis

Error Analysis

Evaluation lifecycle ka Analyze step woh hai jahan hum dekhte hain ki system asal me kya kar raha hai aur figure out karte hain ki woh kahan fail hota hai. Ye chapter uske practical methods cover karta hai — traces systematically padhna, failure modes identify aur categorize karna, traces padh kar aur observations cluster karke failure taxonomy banana, aur testing ke liye synthetic data generate karna.

Evaluation ek iterative cycle hai

LLM applications ke liye robust evaluations develop karne ka process inherently iterative hai. Isme test cases banana, performance assess karna, aur un observations ke basis par system refine karna shamil hai. High-level guides aksar evaluation process ko test cases develop karne, prompts engineer aur refine karne, aur initial cases aur held-out evaluations dono ke against test karne ke cycle ke roop me depict karte hain. Ye cycle emphasize karta hai ki test cases develop karo, prompts ko engineer aur refine karo, aur test karo — phir wapas refine karo. Ye chapter hamare Analyze-Measure-Improve lifecycle ka Analyze step cover karta hai: initial dataset bootstrap karna, traces padhna, aur ek structured understanding banana ki hamara application kahan fail hota hai.

Running example — real estate CRM assistant

Discussion ko concrete banane ke liye, hum ek running example use karte hain: ek real estate CRM assistant. Ye assistant real estate agents ki everyday, aksar messy tasks handle karne me madad ke liye bana hai. Ek real estate professional help maang sakta hai buyer ke liye listings search karne me, warm leads par follow up karne me, ya quick market analysis taiyar karne me. Woh aksar in needs ko conversational, ambiguous language me express karte hain — kis tarah ka ghar buyer chahta hai describe karna, "something affordable near downtown" maangna, ya check karna ki koi open houses jald available hain ya nahi. Assistant ko in requests ko interpret karna hota hai, unhe sahi database queries ya tool calls me translate karna hota hai, aur kabhi multiple steps chain karne hote hain bina constraints khoye hue. Hum is example par poori book me wapas aayenge.

Ek typical multi-step request kuch aisa dikhta hai: "Find me 3-bedroom homes under $600k near downtown. Email the top two matches to my client. Figure out if there are showings available for this weekend." Ek chhoti request bhi assistant se mangti hai ki woh constraints samjhe, listing data search kare, message draft kare, calendars consult kare, aur ek coherent final response de. System "agentic" hai — LLM current state aur already gather ki gayi information ke basis par decide karta hai ki agla action kya lena hai. Model user ki request interpret karta hai aur ek structured action produce karta hai, jaise listings query karna, email draft karna, ya showings calendar check karna. Har action ek downstream tool trigger karta hai, aur tool ka output wapas LLM ko pass hota hai. Model phir ek aur action issue kar sakta hai, pehle wale ko refine kar sakta hai, ya agle step par ja sakta hai. Ye tab tak continue hota hai jab tak system ne task ke liye saare necessary operations complete na kar liye hon.

Terminology — query aur trace

Aage badhne se pehle, kuch terms define kar lete hain jo poore chapter me repeat honge. Jab ek user system se interact karta hai, to woh ek query deta hai — uski request ka raw text. Uske baad jo kuch bhi hota hai, pehle model response se lekar final output tak, woh ek trace banta hai. Trace ek complete, ordered record hai un sab steps ka jo system ne query ke response me liye. Isme har LLM message, har tool call, tool se return hui har value, aur user ko dikhaya gaya final response shamil hai.

Jab hum LLM outputs evaluate karte hain, to hum individual steps ke bajaye traces evaluate karte hain. Kyunki ek LLM agent ka behavior sirf end to end dekhne par samajh aata hai. Ek individual message isolation me reasonable lag sakta hai, phir bhi galat final output ki taraf le ja sakta hai. Poori trace padhne se hum identify kar sakte hain ki problems asal me kahan originate hoti hain, bajaye iske ki baad ke symptoms ko independent failures ke roop me mislabel karein. Is chapter me query ka matlab hai system ko diya gaya original input, aur trace ka matlab hai uske response me system ne jo actions ki poori sequence produce ki. Queries hamesha chat window me type karne wale human se nahi aati; woh automated pipelines, scheduled jobs, ya dusre systems se bhi aa sakti hain jo aapke agent ki API call karte hain.

Kyunki LLM outputs nondeterministic hote hain, wahi query do baar chalane se alag traces produce ho sakte hain. Ek single trace sirf ek possible execution path dikhata hai. Agar koi failure intermittent lagta hai, to wahi query kai baar chalao taaki dekho ki woh kitni baar hota hai.

Analyze ke steps — overview

Is chapter me hum error analysis ke steps se guzrenge, raw data se failure modes ki structured understanding tak: pehle traces ka starting dataset banana, phir traces padh kar open coding karna, phir axial coding se observations ko failure modes me cluster karna, phir traces ko structured failure modes se label karke prevalence ginna, aur aakhir me iterate aur refine karna — saath me common pitfalls se bachna. Ye steps Analyze stage ko operationalize karte hain.

Yaad rakho: Evaluate traces ko karo, individual steps ko nahi. Ek step sahi lag sakta hai aur phir bhi galat final output de sakta hai — asal problem kahan shuru hui, ye sirf poori trace padh kar pata chalta hai.

03.1Chapter 3 · Error Analysis

Traces ka Dataset banana — dimensions aur queries

Error analysis ka pehla step hai traces ka dataset assemble karna. Is dataset ka purpose hai hume concrete material dena taaki hum analyze kar sakein — real examples ki system user requests ke response me kaise behave karta hai. Bina traces ke hamare paas observe karne ko kuch nahi hai, aur error analysis shuru hi nahi ho sakti.

Kitne traces chahiye — saturation

Kitne traces chahiye? Koi fixed number nahi hai; sahi amount aapke application ki complexity par depend karta hai. Ek reasonable starting point lagbhag 100 traces hai, lekin asal signal hai saturation: woh point jahan additional traces analyze karne se errors ki nayi categories milna band ho jayein. Agar aapne 60 traces padhe hain aur aakhri 20 sab un failure modes me aate hain jo aap pehle se identify kar chuke hain, to aap likely saturated hain. Agar naye failure types aate rehte hain, to aage badhte raho. Agar aap bahut jaldi ruk jate hain, to aap aise failure modes miss karne ka risk lete hain jo zyada data ke saath surface hote. Agar aap saturation ke bahut baad tak continue karte hain, to aap effort waste karte hain un traces ko analyze karne me jo sirf wahi confirm karte hain jo aap pehle se jante hain. Simple applications jaldi saturate hoti hain; zyada complex agentic systems jin me kai tools aur multi-step flows hain, unhe zyada exploration chahiye ho sakta hai.

Dataset banane ke do tareeke

Traces ka starting dataset banane ke do tareeke hain. Production logs se (preferred, jab available hon): agar aapke paas pehle se production traces hain, to aap unhe directly sample kar sakte hain. Ye ensure karne ke liye ki aapka sample alag use cases cover kare, aise traces include karne ki koshish karo jo alag features ya user input ke types cover karte hon. Chhote datasets ke liye random sampling fine hai. Bade datasets ke liye aap clustering use kar sakte hain (jaise query text embeddings ya keyword matches par) taaki alag groups se queries select kar sakein. Un traces ko bhi sample karo jahan users ka experience kharab raha: thumbs-down signals, wahi request baar-baar rephrase karna, ya sessions jo user ke dusre channel par switch karne se end hue. Agar aapke paas domain experts hain (jaise hamare CRM example ke liye experienced real estate agents), to unse poochho ki kis tarah ki queries sabse challenging hoti hain; woh aksar hard cases data confirm karne se pehle hi jante hain.

Synthetic queries se: agar aapke paas abhi traces available nahi hain, to pehle synthetic queries ka dataset banao, phir apne application ko un queries par chala kar traces produce karo.

Synthetic queries generate karne ki common galti

Synthetic queries generate karte waqt ek common galti hai ki LLM ko simply prompt kar diya jata hai "generate user queries for my application." Ye approach generic, repetitive queries produce karta hai jo real usage patterns capture nahi karte. Example: LLM ko "Generate 50 queries for a real estate assistant" prompt karne se variations mil sakti hain jaise "Find me a house in San Francisco", "Show me homes in San Francisco", "I'm looking for a property in San Francisco", "Can you find houses in the San Francisco area?" Ye queries sab wahi basic capability test karti hain. Woh un dimensions par vary nahi karti jo aapke application ke liye matter karte hain — dimensions jo agar unexplored reh jayein to failure modes ki poori categories chhupa sakti hain. Example: agar aapki saari synthetic queries well-specified property searches hain, to aap kabhi discover nahi karenge ki aapka assistant tab fail karta hai jab users ambiguous requests karte hain. Repetitive queries par agent chalane se traces sab ek jaise dikhenge, aur aap un failures ko miss kar denge jo sirf alag conditions me surface hote hain.

Behtar approach — dimensions, phir tuples, phir queries

Synthetic queries generate karne ka behtar approach hai ek layer of indirection add karna: LLM se queries directly generate karne ke bajaye, pehle woh dimensions define karo jin par queries vary kar sakti hain, phir un dimensions ke structured combinations generate karo, aur aakhir me har combination ko natural-language query me convert karo. Ye separation diversity ko controlled tareeke se force karta hai aur LLM ko repetitive outputs me collapse hone se rokta hai.

Dimension simply variation ki ek category hai — ek axis jis par requests ek dusre se alag hoti hain. Real estate assistant ke liye useful dimensions ho sakti hain: Feature — user kaunsa task karwana chahta hai (jaise property search, scheduling, email drafting); Client persona — kis type ke client ko serve kiya ja raha hai (jaise first-time buyer, investor, luxury buyer); Scenario type — user apna intent kitni clearly express karta hai (jaise well-specified, ambiguous, out-of-scope). Achhi dimensions identify karne me aksar product ko behtar samajhne ki mehnat lagti hai. Product managers se baat karo, user feedback review karo, ya khud application ko use karke time spend karo. Ye keh kar bhi, shuru karne se pehle har possible dimension enumerate karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Jab aapke paas teen sufficiently diverse dimensions hon, to data generate karna shuru karo. Aap hamesha baad me aur dimensions add kar sakte hain jaise-jaise aapki understanding deepen hoti hai. Dimensions chunte waqt un par focus karo jo describe karte hain ki aapka application kahan fail hone wala hai. Agar aapko abhi nahi pata ki aapka product kahan fail ho sakta hai, to khud use karke intuition banao, ya kuch logon ko use karne ke liye recruit karo aur unki failures ko dimensions motivate karne do.

Tuples generate karna aur queries banana

Dimensions define karne ke baad aap synthetic queries generate karne ke liye LLM use kar sakte hain, lekin diversity ensure karne wali indirection ke saath. Pehle apne dimensions ke structured combinations banao. Ek tuple values ka ek specific combination hai, har dimension se ek, jo ek particular use case define karta hai. Example: Feature: property search; Client persona: investor; Scenario type: ambiguous. Ye tuple ek case describe karta hai jahan ek investor properties search kar raha hai, lekin request underspecified ya vague hai. Is tuple se aap ek query generate kar sakte hain jaise: "Look up showings for good properties in San Mateo County." Ek alag tuple — first-time buyer aur specific scenario — se mil sakta hai: "Find 3-bedroom homes under $600k near downtown that allow pets."

20 tuples haath se likhna problem space ko samajhne me madad karta hai. Agar aapko sure nahi hai ki kaunse tuples likhne hain, to domain experts se consult karo ya real user queries ko inspiration ke liye review karo. Jab aapke paas example tuples aur corresponding queries ka ek chhota set ho, to LLM use karke 100 ya zyada tak scale up karo. Kuch practitioners 10 se 20 carefully crafted queries ka chhota set prefer karte hain jin me woh deeply invest karte hain, bajaye ek bade synthetic set ke; ye bhi achha kaam kar sakta hai agar aap un queries ko time ke saath enrich karte rahein aur unhe one-time test ke bajaye iterative improvement ki foundation ke roop me use karein.

Key idea hai tuple generation ko query generation se alag rakhna. Pehle LLM ko prompt karo ki structured tuples generate kare. Phir har tuple ke liye LLM ko prompt karo ki natural-language query generate kare. Ye two-step process LLM se queries directly mangne se behtar kaam karta hai, kyunki tuples har query ko ek specific combination cover karne ke liye constrain karte hain. Tuple generation ke liye prompt kuch aisa dikhta hai: "Generate 10 random combinations of (feature, client persona, scenario) for a real estate CRM assistant. The dimensions are: Feature — property search, market analysis, scheduling, email drafting; Client persona — first-time homebuyer, investor, luxury buyer; Scenario — exact match (clearly specified and feasible), ambiguous request (unclear or underspecified), shouldn't be handled (invalid or out-of-scope). Output each tuple in the format: (feature, client persona, scenario). Avoid duplicates. Vary values across dimensions."

Phir har tuple ke liye query generation prompt kuch aisa hota hai: "We are generating synthetic user queries for a real estate CRM assistant. The assistant helps agents manage client requests by searching listings, analyzing markets, drafting emails, and reading calendars. Given: Feature: Scheduling; Client Persona: First-time homebuyer; Scenario: Ambiguous request. Write a realistic query that an agent might enter into the system to fulfill this client's request. The query should reflect the client's needs and the ambiguity of the scenario. Example: 'Find showings for affordable homes with short notice availability.' Now generate a new query."

Sampling, generating aur filtering ki is process ko continue karo jab tak aapke paas lagbhag 100 high-quality, diverse examples na ho jayein. Agar phrasing awkward ho ya content mark miss kare, to query ko throw out karke regenerate kar sakte hain. Is stage par quality control ke baare me aggressive raho, kyunki error analysis ke aage ke steps is par depend karte hain ki traces kitne representative aur realistic hain.

Queries chalane se pehle — predictions likho, phir traces export karo

Jab aapne apni queries curate kar li hon, to unhe chalane se pehle ek useful exercise hai apni predictions likhna: har query ke liye note karo ki aap expect karte hain ki system kya karega aur kahan fail hoga. Predictions ko actual behavior se compare karna un assumptions ko surface karta hai jinke baare me aapko pata hi nahi tha ki aap bana rahe hain. Phir har query ko apne application par end to end chalao aur poori trace export karo. Export me saare LLM steps, tool calls, inputs aur outputs shamil hone chahiye. Agar aap Braintrust, LangSmith ya Weave jaise observability platform use kar rahe hain, to aap traces ko directly unke interfaces se export kar sakte hain. Agar aapka setup simple hai, to aap har step ko agent execute hote waqt JSON file ya database me log kar sakte hain. Annotation ke liye kai teams ko traces ko spreadsheet me export karna sabse aasan lagta hai — ek row per trace, aur columns query, har intermediate step aur final output ke liye. Format matter kam karta hai; important ye hai ki aapke paas ek complete record ho jise aap padh aur annotate kar sakein. In traces ke saath, aap unhe padhne aur failure modes identify karne ke liye taiyar hain.

Yaad rakho: LLM se seedha "50 queries banao" kehna aapko 50 tareekon se wahi query dega. Pehle dimensions define karo, phir tuples banao, phir har tuple se query — diversity design se aati hai, prompt se nahi.

03.2Chapter 3 · Error Analysis

Open Coding aur Axial Coding

Traces haath me aane ke baad agla step hai unhe padhna aur annotate karna — pehle free-form observations ke saath (open coding), phir un observations ko structured failure categories me cluster karke (axial coding). Idea hai ki categories ko wahi se emerge karne diya jaye jo aap asal me data me dekhte hain, bajaye ek predefined list se shuru karne ke.

Open coding — traces padhna aur label karna

Hamari labeling process qualitative research methods se adapted two-step approach use karti hai: pehle traces padho aur free-form observations likho (open coding); phir un observations ko structured failure categories me cluster karo (axial coding). Is context me coding ka matlab hai data ke un parts ko short descriptive labels assign karna jo important lagte hain. Har trace ke liye aap carefully padhte hain aur brief notes likhte hain jo aap observe karte hain. Aap note kar sakte hain ki outputs kahan incorrect hain, actions kahan surprising hain, ya behavior kahan galat feel hota hai. Har note ek failure mode ka potential signal hai. Ye annotations chhoti ho sakti hain — ek phrase ya ek-do sentences — aur kisi particular format follow karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Goal hai apne observations ko jaldi capture karna. Baad ke steps me hum inhe zyada rigorously categorize aur structure karenge.

Open coding karte waqt khud ko user ke perspective me rakho. Kya user ko asal me achha experience mil raha hai? Kya response unki request address karta hai? Is stage par focus ye notice karne aur record karne par hai ki kya galat feel hota hai, causes diagnose karne ya fixes ke baare me sochne par nahi.

Pehli failure ya saari failures?

Ek common sawaal hai: kya aapko ek trace me saari failures note karni chahiye, ya sirf pehli wali? Hum recommend karte hain ki pehle pehli failure se shuru karo jo aap observe karte hain — jo usually sabse upstream point hai jahan kuch galat hua. Traces complex ho sakte hain, aur ek single upstream error aksar downstream issues ka cascade cause karta hai. Pehli failure par focus karna zyada efficient hai aur aapko har symptom catalog karne se rokta hai jab kai symptoms sirf ek root cause ke consequences hain. Kai cases me pehli error fix karne se poori chain resolve ho jati hai.

Aap har trace aur uski corresponding annotation ko ek simple table ya spreadsheet me record kar sakte hain — ek column trace identifier ke liye, dusri trace ya uske summary ke liye, aur teesri free-form notes ke liye jo pehli failure describe karte hain. Practically, open codes chhote, lowercase notes hote hain jo aap padhte waqt jot karte hain. Unhe polished ya grammatical hone ki zaroorat nahi hai, lekin unme kaafi context hona chahiye taaki ek teammate baad me padh kar samajh sake ki kya galat hua, bina poori trace dobara padhe.

Realistic open codes — examples

Real estate assistant ki traces padhte waqt aap aise notes likh sakte hain: User ne "3-bedroom homes under $600k near downtown that allow pets" manga; assistant ne SQL generate kiya jis me pet-friendly filter drop ho gaya, halanki user ne explicitly manga tha — downstream listings aur email sab constraint miss karte hain. User ne "set up showings for these two homes this weekend" kaha; calendar API ne bataya ki agent Saturday afternoon unavailable hai; assistant ne phir bhi Saturday 2 p.m. aur Sunday 11 a.m. showings propose kar diye — calendar result ko hard constraint ke bajaye advisory treat kiya. User ne investor client ke liye property list mangi; assistant ne high-ROI properties search ki lekin casual, emoji-heavy email draft kiya jo first-time buyer ke liye likha lagta tha — tone aur framing investor persona se match nahi karti, halanki search investor-appropriate thi. Listing record kehta hai "2 bed, 1 bath"; assistant ki draft email ghar ko "spacious 3-bedroom with a renovated second bath" describe karti hai — hallucinated bedroom count aur bathroom upgrade, details plausible lagti hain lekin listing data se contradict karti hain. User ne kaha "send the shortlist to my client"; assistant ne email ek aise contact ko bhej diya jo conversation history me pehle mention hua tha, active shortlist se tied client ke bajaye — wrong recipient. User ne "Springfield" listings poochhi; agent ka location context Massachusetts hai; assistant ne bina poochhe Springfield, IL se results return kar diye — ambiguous city name galat state me silently resolve ho gaya, halanki multiple Springfields exist karte hain. User ne poocha "what's a good offer price for 142 Oak St?"; assistant ne bina comps lookup ya market analysis tool call ke "$585k" answer kar diya — confidently stated lekin kisi retrieved data par grounded nahi hai. Multi-step request ke dauraan listings search tool ne error payload return kiya; assistant ne error ignore kiya aur "the homes I found" summarize karte hue email draft karna continue kiya — tool error bina surface ya retry kiye ignore hua aur results fabricate kar diye gaye. User ne "a quick summary of this week's leads" manga; reply six paragraphs ka tha section headers ke saath — response "quick summary" ke implication se bahut lamba tha, user ki wording me brevity hint ignore hui. User ne assistant se kaha "draft an email" to a client; assistant ne email draft kiya aur turant send_email call kar diya bina draft review ke liye dikhaye — irreversible action tab liya jab user ne sirf draft karne ko kaha tha; implicit confirmation step skip ho gaya.

Notice karo ki ye notes abhi categories nahi hain. Ye raw observations hain, jo bhi phrasing padhte waqt dimaag me aayi, usme likhe gaye. Kuch same underlying failure mode ke instances nikalenge, aur kuch akele khade rahenge. Woh sorting baad me hoti hai, axial coding me. Open coding ke dauraan errors ko group ya formalize karne ki koshish mat karo. Rich set of raw observations collect karne par focus karo. Aap har trace ko ek holistic binary judgment bhi de sakte hain — acceptable ya unacceptable — ek fourth column ke roop me. Clear yes-or-no decision lena vague scores se zyada sharp thinking force karta hai, aur jab judgment borderline bhi lage, to ek side pick karna ye clarify karne me madad karta hai ki aap kya failure mante hain.

Kabhi-kabhi ye articulate karna mushkil hota hai ki trace me kya exactly galat feel ho raha hai. Agar aap stuck hain, to ek strategy hai temporarily zyada "top-down" approach adopt karna: failure modes ke data se emerge hone ka wait karne ke bajaye, common LLM failure categories consider karo aur actively unki manifestations dhoondho. Example: ye jaan kar ki hallucination (jab model aisi information generate karta hai jo uske input me grounded nahi hai aur use factual jaise present karta hai) ek common issue hai, aap har trace ko specifically check kar sakte hain ki kya assistant facts invent karta hai ya information misrepresent karta hai. Aap un failure modes par bhi bharosa kar sakte hain jo aapne apne application ke liye specific sune hain. Agar aap text-to-SQL system bana rahe hain, to aap malformed queries ya incorrect joins dhoondh sakte hain. Agar aap customer service bot bana rahe hain, to aap aise responses dhoondh sakte hain jo company policy contradict karte hain. Goal traces ko predefined categories me force karna nahi hai, balki known failure types ko "lenses" ke roop me use karna hai jo un problems ko identify karne me madad karte hain jo warna pin down karna mushkil hota.

Open coding kitni der tak continue karni chahiye? Ek useful heuristic hai ki tab tak aage badho jab tak aapne kam se kam 20 problematic traces label na kar liye hon aur naye failure modes aana band na ho gaye hon. Us point par aapke paas apne observations structure karne ke liye kaafi raw material likely hai.

Axial coding — failure modes ko structure karna

Open coding ek valuable lekin unstructured collection of observations produce karta hai. Har trace ke apne raw notes hain — missing constraints, invalid actions, inappropriate tones, ya hallucinated facts. In observations ko samajhne aur ye quantify karne ke liye ki alag problems kitni baar hoti hain, aapko unhe failure modes ke structured set me organize karna hota hai. Axial coding dusra step hai: open coding ke dauraan likhe gaye notes ke beech relationships identify karna aur unhe higher-order categories me group karna. Ye aapko isolated observations se distinct, recurring failure types ke coherent set tak le jata hai.

Axial code karne ke liye, apne open-coded traces ko padho aur similar annotations ko saath cluster karo. Kuch patterns obvious hote hain. Example: traces jahan assistant buyer ke budget ko ignore karta hai ya number of bedrooms jaisi requirement omit karta hai, woh naturally ek broader failure mode me cluster hote hain: violation of user constraints. Dusre patterns me deeper distinctions kai traces padhne ke baad hi dikhti hain. Example: property features ki hallucinations (claim karna ki ghar me solar panels hain jab nahi hain) aur client activity ki hallucinations (ek tour schedule karna jo user ne kabhi request hi nahi kiya) pehle wahi problem lag sakti hain. Lekin in failures ke alag causes hain aur alag fixes chahiye. Hallucinated property features likely isliye hain kyunki model listing data me present nahi details invent kar raha hai, jabki hallucinated user activity suggest karta hai ki model user intent ko misinterpret ya fabricate kar raha hai. Aap unhe hallucinated listing metadata aur hallucinated user actions me split karenge, kyunki diagnose aur address karne ke liye alag strategies chahiye. Ye keh kar bhi, ye sirf pehla pass hai. Agar aap baad me categories split ya merge karte hain to theek hai, jaise-jaise failure modes ki aapki understanding deepen hoti hai.

Jabki early clustering aksar manually hoti hai, aap notes organize karne me madad ke liye language model bhi use kar sakte hain. Lekin ek warning yaad rakhni hai: LLM ko apni failure taxonomy scratch se generate karne ke liye use mat karo. LLMs ke generic failure categories (jaise "hallucination", "instruction following", "tone") ki taraf strong priors hote hain aur application-specific issues ki taraf weak priors, jo sirf real traces padh kar visible hote hain. Jo teams open coding skip karke LLM se failure modes propose karne ko kehti hain, woh aksar months ki evaluation infrastructure ek aisi taxonomy par build kar leti hain jo unke actual failure distribution se match nahi karti. Hum open coding ke liye LLM use karna recommend nahi karte, kyunki us step me aapka judgment aur taste chahiye ki kya failure banta hai. Lekin axial coding ke liye LLM useful ho sakta hai: uska kaam aapka taste apply karna nahi hai, balki aapke already banaye gaye observations ko analyze karke unhe organize karne ka tareeka propose karna hai.

Traces ko open code karne ke baad, aap raw open codes ko LLM me paste kar sakte hain, traces ke saath, aur LLM se preliminary groupings propose karne ko keh sakte hain: "Below is a list of open-ended annotations describing failures in an LLM-driven real estate CRM assistant. Please group them into a small set of coherent failure categories, where each category captures similar types of mistakes. Each group should have a short descriptive title and a brief one-line definition. Do not invent new failure types; only cluster based on what is present in the notes." LLM-generated groupings initial ideas organize karne me madad kar sakti hain, lekin unhe blindly accept nahi karna chahiye. LLM nahi janta ki aapka system kaise kaam karta hai ya aap alag tarah ke failures ko fix karne ke liye kya karenge, isliye uski proposed categories aise issues merge kar sakti hain jo alag rakhne chahiye, ya aise issues split kar sakti hain jo saath belong karte hain. Aapko taxonomy ko review karke edits karne hi padenge: categories rename karna, bahut similar ones merge karna, ya unhe split karna jo alag root causes wale failures ko lump karte hain. Axial coding ke end par aapke paas distinct failure modes ki list hoti hai, har ek ke saath representative examples jo use illustrate karte hain. Ye examples reference points ka kaam karte hain jab aap error analysis ke agle stage me jate hain: failures ko saare traces par systematically label aur quantify karna.

Traces ko structured failure modes se label karna

Is point par aapke paas do artifacts hain: traces ka collection, har ek ke saath open coding se initial free-form annotation; aur axial coding se defined structured failure modes ki list. Agla step hai apne traces par wapas jana aur har ek ko un failure modes se label karna jo apply hote hain. Ye qualitative observation se quantitative data tak ka gap bridge karta hai. Har trace ke liye, uske open codes ko apne failure modes ki list se compare karo aur determine karo kaunse apply hote hain. Agar aapne failure modes manually derive kiye hain axial coding ke dauraan, to ye straightforward hai: aap wahi mapping apply karte hain jo aapne develop kiya tha. Agar ek LLM ne categories generate karne me madad ki hai, to aapko ensure karna hai ki woh categories consistently har trace par wapas apply hon. Aap ye manually kar sakte hain, ya aap LLM ko har trace ki annotation aur apne failure modes ki list ke saath prompt karke appropriate labels assign karne ko keh sakte hain. Jab is step ke liye LLM use karte hain, to uski assignments review karna sure karo taaki mistakes pakad sakein aur definitions refine kar sakein jahan zaroorat ho.

Apne spreadsheet me har failure mode ke liye ek naya column add karo. Har trace ke liye, 1 mark karo agar woh failure present hai aur 0 agar absent hai. Example table me har row ek trace hai aur har column ek failure mode — Missing Constraint, Inappropriate Tone, Wrong Action, aur aise hi. Ek 1 ka matlab hai woh failure present hai. Example: tr-041 "SQL query missed the budget cap" — Missing Constraint 1, baaki 0. tr-042 "Email tone too aggressive for luxury buyer" — Inappropriate Tone 1. tr-043 "Called send_email before checking calendar" — Wrong Action 1. tr-044 "Budget missed AND tone too casual" — Missing Constraint 1 aur Inappropriate Tone 1. tr-045 "Said property has pool, it does not" — saare 0 is chhoti table ke columns me, kyunki woh ek alag failure mode (hallucination) hai.

Jab columns populate ho jayein, to aap har failure mode ki occurrences gin sakte hain aur total traces se divide karke prevalence rate nikaal sakte hain. Is chhote example me, Missing Constraint paanch me se do traces me dikhta hai (40%) aur Inappropriate Tone bhi paanch me se do me (40%). Is process se guzarte waqt aapko likely edge cases milenge. Kuch traces kisi defined failure mode se cleanly match nahi karenge. Dusre nuances point karenge jo suggest karte hain ki ek category refine ya split karni chahiye. Apne failure mode definitions ko jaate-jaate adjust karna theek hai. Aap prevalence rates spreadsheet me simple formula se compute kar sakte hain, ya pandas ya pivot tables jaise tools se agar aap data ko alag dimensions se slice karna chahte hain. Ye batata hai ki kaunsi failures sabse common hain, jo improvement efforts kahan focus karne hain ye decide karne me useful hai.

Iteration aur refinement

Error analysis ek baar ka process nahi hai. Traces review karne aur failure mode taxonomy refine karne ke do ya teen rounds se guzarna common hai. Early rounds aksar un failure modes ko uncover karte hain jo initially miss hue the, ya clear karte hain ki definitions adjust karni hain. Jaise-jaise aap zyada traces analyze karte hain — chahe pehle skip ki gayi ones ko label karke ya naye queries sample karke — aapki understanding deepen hoti hai aur taxonomy zyada precise hoti jati hai. Refinement alag forms leta hai. Kabhi aap categories merge karte hain jo reliably distinguish karne ke liye bahut similar nikli. Kabhi aap ek category split karte hain jo alag root causes wale failures ko lump kar rahi thi. Aur kabhi aap simply ek definition clarify karte hain taaki use consistently apply karna aasan ho. Example: real estate CRM assistant par analysis ka dusra round ek nayi error expose kar sakta hai jo pehle batch me apparent nahi thi: assistant kabhi location names ko misinterpret karta hai — bina clarification maange local city par default kar deta hai. Springfield listings maangne wale user ko poori tarah galat state ke results mil sakte hain. Isse aap location ambiguity errors ko ek distinct failure mode ke roop me add karenge.

Iteration endless nahi hai. Practically, open coding aur reannotation ke do serious rounds aksar theoretical saturation ke kareeb pahunchne ke liye kaafi hote hain. Uske baad, wahi dataset par additional error analysis typically diminishing returns deti hai. Ye keh kar bhi, error analysis woh cheez hai jis par hum hamesha periodically wapas aate hain. Errors fix karne ke baad, zyada users ko ship karne ke baad, ya user behavior ke naye patterns observe karne ke baad, fresh data ke saath process se dobara cycle karo. Error analysis ki value is se aati hai ki aapka system abhi asal me kya kar raha hai, us se engage karna — ek static dataset ko baar-baar analyze karne se nahi.

Exhaustive labeling par ek note: pehle humne recommend kiya tha ki har trace ke liye sirf pehli failure label karo. Ye initial annotation process ko fast aur focused rakhta hai. Lekin first-failure labeling ki ek limitation hai: ye un failure modes ko undercount karta hai jo traces me baad me hote hain. Example: agar Inappropriate Tone aksar Missing Constraint jaisi pehli error ke baad aata hai, to aapke first-failure labels use rarely capture karenge. Isse fix ka impact precisely measure karna mushkil ho jata hai. Agar aap Inappropriate Tone fix karte hain lekin use sirf handful traces me record kiya tha, to aap bata nahi payenge ki aapka fix asal me kaam kiya ya nahi. Agar aap kisi fix ka impact measure karna chahte hain, to wapas jao aur us failure mode ke saare instances annotate karo — har failure mode ke nahi, sirf unke jinhe aap actively fix ya track kar rahe hain. Jaise-jaise aapko error analysis me zyada experience hota hai, process bahut fast ho jata hai. Aapko intuition develop hoti hai ki kya dhoondhna hai, aapki taxonomy stabilize hoti hai, aur labeling routine ban jati hai. Aap ye bhi pa sakte hain ki aap open coding me saari failures label karte hain — pehli failure par focus ek starting discipline hai, aakhri rule nahi.

Yaad rakho: Open coding me categories mat banao — sirf observe karo. Axial coding me cluster karo — aur LLM se grouping me madad lo, taxonomy generate karne me nahi. Phir binary 1/0 labeling se prevalence gino: jo common hai, use pehle fix karo.

03.3Chapter 3 · Error Analysis

Common Pitfalls aur Putting It Together

Error analysis karne ka koi single correct tareeka nahi hai. Aap pa sakte hain ki aap kuch stages par zyada time spend karna chahte hain, dusron par kam — ye aapki team ke working style aur aapke application ko evaluate karna kitna mushkil hai, is par depend karta hai. Lekin error analysis karne ke kai bad tareeke hain. Is section me kuch common pitfalls hain jin se bachna chahiye.

Pitfall 1 — Representative data par test na karna

Early error analysis me sabse common galti hai representative data par test na karna. Agar aapka initial query set real user behavior ki diversity aur difficulty reflect nahi karta, to aapke produce kiye gaye traces uninformative honge. Ya to koi serious failures hote hi nahi, ya jo failures dikhte hain woh woh nahi hote jo production me aayenge. Isi liye dimensions wala synthetic-data approach aur production logs ki careful sampling itni important hai — aapka dataset hi aapki analysis ki ceiling tay karta hai.

Pitfall 2 — Open coding skip kar dena

Dusri common galti hai open coding ko poori tarah skip kar dena. Real traces padhne aur ye observe karne ke bajaye ki system asal me kaise fail hota hai, teams aksar LLM research se uthayi gayi generic categories par default kar deti hain, jaise "hallucination", "instruction following" aur "verbosity". Ye labels reasonable sound kar sakte hain, lekin real examples me grounded hue bina, woh aksar application-specific issues miss kar dete hain. Real estate CRM assistant me, example ke liye, unavailable showings propose karna ya client personas misidentify karna jaise errors generic verbosity se kahin zyada damaging hain. Kai evaluation vendors off-the-shelf metrics promote karte hain, jo engineers ko aise metrics ki taraf le ja sakte hain jo useful sound karte hain lekin woh capture nahi karte jo aapke application ke liye asal me matter karta hai.

Pitfall 3 — Likert scales ka inappropriate use

Early annotation ke dauraan Likert scales ka inappropriate use ek aur frequent pitfall hai. Likert scale annotators se kehta hai ki relevance ya helpfulness jaisi qualities ko numeric scale par rate karein, typically 1 se 5. Widely use hone ke bawjood, Likert scales substantial noise introduce karte hain jab detailed rubric ke bina apply kiye jayein. Jab rubrics underspecified hote hain, to rating scales annotators ke beech kam agreement aur zyada subjective variance le aate hain. Iske contrast me, specific failure modes ke baare me binary decisions force karna (ki problem hui ya nahi) zyada reproducible annotations produce karta hai. Isi liye book binary Pass/Fail aur binary 1/0 labeling prefer karti hai — kam se kam early stages me.

Pitfall 4 — Initial annotations ko fixed treat karna

Initial annotations aur failure modes ko fixed treat karna ek galti hai. Annotation schemas ka zyada data review karne ke baad evolve karna normal hai. Naye examples edge cases expose kar sakte hain jin ke liye definitions refine karni padti hain. Schema ko bahut jaldi freeze karna aapke evaluation infrastructure ko system behavior ki incomplete understanding ke aas-paas lock kar deta hai.

Pitfall 5 — Domain experts ko labeling se bahar rakhna

Relatedly, domain experts ko labeling process se exclude karna ek misstep hai, khaas taur par un applications ke liye jin me deep subject matter knowledge chahiye hoti hai. Bina domain expertise wale logon ko annotation outsource karna aksar superficial ya incorrect labels ki taraf le jata hai. Agar domain experts ko aapke annotation tools cumbersome lagte hain, to simpler interfaces me invest karo jo unki participation aasan banayein.

Error analysis achhe se karna ek skill hai jise practice chahiye hoti hai. Har round ke saath aap faster hote hain, aapki taxonomy stable hoti hai, aur aapko pata hota hai ki kahan dekhna hai.

Putting it together — Analyze phase ke outputs

Analyze phase ke end par aapke paas teen concrete outputs hone chahiye:

  • Traces ka dataset — har ek free-form observations ke saath annotate kiya gaya ki kya galat hua.
  • Failure modes ki taxonomy — un observations ko cluster karke derive ki gayi. Ye sabse important output hai. Ye aapko aur aapki team ko ek shared vocabulary deti hai system ke fail hone ke tareekon ko describe karne ke liye, jo Measure aur Improve phases me har decision ko drive karti hai. Agar aapki taxonomy un failures se match nahi karti jo aapke users asal me experience karte hain, to uske upar bane evaluators galat cheezein measure karenge.
  • Initial counts — har failure mode aapke dataset me kitni baar dikhta hai.

Chapter 4 cover karta hai ki team ko annotation criteria par align kaise karaya jaye aur collaborative processes kaise banayein jo taxonomy ko accurate rakhte hain jab system evolve karta hai. Analyze se aapko pata chalta hai ki system kaise fail hota hai; Chapter 4 ensure karta hai ki team is baat par agree kare ki failure hai kya.

Yaad rakho: Sabse badi galti hai generic categories se shuru karna aur real traces kabhi na padhna. Aapki taxonomy aapke data se aani chahiye — aur woh living document hai, pehle draft ke baad frozen nahi.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Error Analysis

04Chapter 4 · Collaborative Evaluation Practices

Collaborative Evaluation Practices

Error analysis hume failure modes ki list deti hai. Agla sawaal hai ki kya team ke alag log is baat par agree karte hain ki failure kya qualify karta hai. Ye chapter human judgment align karne ke baare me hai — collaborative evaluation practices, jo multiple logon ko is baat par agree karwate hain ki pass ya fail kya hai.

Human judgment par sab kuch depend karta hai

Error analysis har step par human judgment par depend karti hai. Aap decide karte hain ki kya failure qualify karta hai, aur errors ko kaise categorize karna hai. Lekin evaluation criteria aksar subjective hote hain — jo ek vyakti "helpful" manta hai, dusra use verbose pa sakta hai — aur individual judgment inconsistent hota hai (wahi vyakti wahi trace ko alag dinon me alag tareeke se rate kar sakta hai). Agar labels unreliable hain, to unke upar bani har cheez (failure mode counts, automated evaluators, improvement decisions) wahi noise inherit karti hai.

Criteria drift — "good" badalta rehta hai

Ek motivating example hai ek badi notes-product company, jo lagbhag 70 engineers ke saath evaluations chalati hai aur usne ek dedicated team banayi hai jiska kaam hai define karna ki har AI feature ke liye "good" kaisa dikhta hai aur use rubric ke roop me likhna. Unka framework criteria drift ko account karta hai — ye fact ki "good" kya qualify karta hai, woh time ke saath shift hota hai, jaise-jaise team ki users aur edge cases ki understanding deepen hoti hai. Controlled setting me kiye gaye ek study me bhi wahi phenomenon mila: developers routinely apne past labels revise karte the, jaise-jaise woh zyada examples dekhte the. Evaluation criteria fixed nahi hote. Woh evolve karte hain jaise-jaise team zyada data dekhti hai, aur rubrics ko unke saath evolve karna hota hai.

Is chapter me kya seekhenge

  • Kab ek single "benevolent dictator" expert evaluation ke liye kaafi hota hai, aur kab aapko multiple annotators chahiye hote hain.
  • Consistent rubrics produce karne ke liye ek nine-step collaborative annotation workflow.
  • Inter-annotator agreement kaise measure karein — Cohen's Kappa ke saath (aur kab Fleiss's Kappa ya Krippendorff's Alpha jaise alternatives use karne hain).
  • Alignment sessions kaise chalani hain jo disagreements resolve karte hain aur rubrics improve karte hain.
  • Collaborative evaluation me common pitfalls aur unse kaise bachein.

Ye chapter Analyze phase ko team sport banata hai. Chapter 3 me aapne akele traces padh kar failure modes nikale; ab aap seekhenge ki team ko ek hi page par kaise laayein taaki woh failure modes reliable labels ban sakein — aur wahi labels aage automated evaluators ki ground truth banenge.

Yaad rakho: Agar labels unreliable hain, to un par bani har cheez unreliable hai. Pehle logon ko agree karwao ki "sahi" kya hai — phir automation ki baat karo.

04.1Chapter 4 · Collaborative Evaluation Practices

Collaborative Annotation Workflow

Jab ek single expert kaafi nahi hota, to aap evaluation me multiple logon ko involve karne ke liye ek structured process use kar sakte hain. Is section me ek workflow hai jo evaluation criteria ko collaboratively define aur refine karta hai. Goal hai clear, consistent rubrics banana jinhe multiple log (aur eventually automated evaluators) reliably apply kar sakein.

Ek criterion ya kai — aur agreement kaise measure karein

Kya aapki team ek baar me ek criterion tackle kare ya kai? Practically, zyadaatar teams ek hi pass me multiple criteria annotate karti hain. Agar aap pehle se ek trace review kar rahe hain, to use trace ko factual correctness, tone, completeness aur baaki criteria jo matter karte hain, sab ke liye ek saath label karna efficient hai. Lekin jab aap agreement measure karte hain aur alignment sessions chalate hain, to har criterion ko alag treat karo. Do annotators dono recognize kar sakte hain ki response me factual errors hain, lekin "too formal" ya "too casual" tone ke baare me unki intuitions poori tarah alag ho sakti hain. Agar aap saare criteria par ek single agreement score compute karte hain, to aapko pata nahi chalega ki kaunsi rubrics kaam kar rahi hain aur kaunsi need refinement. Agreement per criterion measure karo, aur alignment sessions ek baar me ek criterion par focused rakho.

Nine-step workflow

Collaborative evaluation workflow ke nine steps hain:

  1. Step 1 — Annotation team assemble karo. Relevant domain expertise ya stakeholder perspective wale do ya zyada annotators select karo. Roles aur annotation task ka scope shuru se clarify karo. Badi organizations me aap engineering, product, legal aur customer support se representatives involve kar sakte hain.
  2. Step 2 — Initial rubrics draft karo. Har evaluation criterion ke liye rubrics ke pehle versions banao. Har rubric me ek working definition honi chahiye (jaise "Is the response factually accurate with respect to the source document?") aur kuch illustrative Pass/Fail examples. Ye drafts aksar pehle ki error analysis se emerge hote hain — aap un failure modes ko formalize kar rahe hote hain jo aapne traces padhte waqt khud identify kiye the.
  3. Step 3 — Shared annotation set select karo. 20–50 representative traces ka ek common set curate karo jinhe saare annotators label karenge. Aise examples chuno jo criteria se directly relevant hon, aur deliberately borderline ya ambiguous cases include karo. Ye edge cases woh jagah hain jahan rubrics test hote hain. Agar sab easy cases par agree karte hain lekin hard ones par disagree karte hain, to aapko pata hai ki rubrics ko kaam chahiye.
  4. Step 4 — Independently label karo. Har annotator draft rubrics use karke saare examples ko khud label karta hai. Is phase me koi discussion allowed nahi hai. Goal hai rubrics ko interpret karne me differences surface karna, abhi consensus tak pahunchna nahi. Agar annotators is phase me baat karte hain, to unke judgments correlated ho jate hain, aur aap ambiguities detect karne ki ability kho dete hain.
  5. Step 5 — Inter-annotator agreement measure karo. Labeling ke baad, har criterion ke liye alag se inter-annotator agreement (IAA) scores compute karo — Cohen's Kappa jaise metrics use karke. Kisi particular criterion par kam agreement flag karta hai ki uski rubric vague hai ya annotators use alag tareeke se interpret kar rahe hain. High agreement wala criterion aage badhne ke liye taiyar hai. Kam agreement wale ko aur kaam chahiye.
  6. Step 6 — Alignment sessions facilitate karo. Annotators ko saath laao taaki woh cases discuss kar sakein jahan woh disagree hue. Ek baar me ek criterion par focus karo. Factual accuracy aur tone ki discussions ek hi conversation me mix karna confusion create karta hai. Goal hai disagreement ka source samajhna aur rubric improve karna, past labels par argue karna nahi.
  7. Step 7 — Rubrics revise karo. Alignment discussion se mile insights ke basis par har rubric update karo. Definitions clarify karo, examples refine karo, aur labeling criteria adjust karo jahan zaroorat ho. Rubrics ko har iteration ke saath zyada precise hona chahiye.
  8. Step 8 — Iterate karo. Process repeat karo: naye examples select karo, independently label karo, per criterion IAA measure karo, aur revise karo. Tab tak continue karo jab tak agreement acceptable levels tak na pahunch jaye — typically har criterion ke liye Cohen's Kappa 0.6 ya usse upar.
  9. Step 9 — Rubrics aur labels finalize karo. Jab agreement consistently high ho, to final rubrics document karo aur ek consensus-labeled dataset generate karo. Ye "gold standard" set do purposes serve karta hai: ye validate karta hai ki humans rubrics ko consistently apply kar sakte hain, aur ye automated LLM-as-judge evaluators ko evaluate karne ke liye ground truth deta hai (jo Chapter 5 me cover hote hain).

Is workflow me effort lagta hai, lekin ye pay off karta hai. Jo rubric aap produce karte hain, woh kisi ek vyakti ke akele banaye gaye rubric se zyada clear aur consistently applicable hogi. Aur jo gold-standard labels aap generate karte hain, woh automated evaluators train karne, system performance measure karne aur time ke saath improvement track karne ke liye reliable foundation denge.

Yaad rakho: Annotate karte waqt kai criteria ek saath label karo (efficient hai), lekin agreement measure karte waqt har criterion ko alag rakho — warna aapko kabhi pata nahi chalega ki kaunsi rubric tooti hui hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Collaborative Evaluation Practices
← Previous04 · Collaborative Evaluation Practices→ Next04.2 · Inter-Annotator Agreement — Cohen's Kappa aur alternatives
04.2Chapter 4 · Collaborative Evaluation Practices

Inter-Annotator Agreement — Cohen's Kappa aur alternatives

Aap kaise jaante hain ki aapke annotators rubric ko consistently apply kar rahe hain? Aap unka agreement measure karte hain. Ye section batata hai ki percent agreement kyun misleading hota hai, Cohen's Kappa chance ke liye kaise adjust karta hai, aur kab dusre metrics use karne chahiye.

Percent agreement — simple lekin misleading

Sabse simple measure hai percent agreement: items ka proportion jahan dono annotators ne wahi label assign kiya. Agar do annotators ne 100 traces label kiye aur 85 par agree kiye, to percent agreement 85% hai. Mathematically, percent agreement (jise observed agreement, Po bhi kehte hain) hai: (number of items where both annotators agree) / (total number of items).

Percent agreement compute karne me aasan hai aur interpret karne me aasan hai. Lekin isme ek serious flaw hai: ye us agreement ko account nahi karta jo chance se ho sakta tha. Ek scenario consider karo jahan aapke traces me 95% Pass hain aur sirf 5% Fail. Agar dono annotators simply har cheez ko Pass label kar dein, to woh 95% traces par agree karenge, chahe unme se koi bhi traces ko carefully padh hi na raha ho. High agreement label distribution ke skew ka artifact hoga, is baat ka evidence nahi ki rubric clear hai.

Label skew tab aur severe ho jata hai jab aapka system improve hota hai. Development ke shuru me aapke paas Pass aur Fail traces ka lagbhag even mix ho sakta hai, isliye chance agreement lagbhag 50% hoti hai. Lekin jaise-jaise aap bugs fix karte hain aur system behtar hota hai, zyada traces Pass ban jate hain. Agar 90% traces Pass hain, to chance agreement lagbhag 82% tak badh jata hai (0.9 × 0.9 + 0.1 × 0.1 = 0.82). 85% ka percent agreement achha sound karega, lekin woh random labeling se expected agreement se barely upar hai.

Cohen's Kappa — chance ke liye adjust karna

Cohen's Kappa (κ) is problem ko address karta hai — observed agreement ko expected chance agreement se compare karke. Formula hai: κ = (Po − Pe) / (1 − Pe). Yahan Po observed percent agreement hai, aur Pe expected agreement hai agar dono annotators randomly label kar rahe hote (lekin apni actual label distributions ke saath). Pe compute karne ke liye aap calculate karte hain ki har annotator har label ko kitni baar use karta hai, phir probability nikalte hain ki woh chance se agree karenge. Binary labels (Pass/Fail) ke liye: Pe = (PPass,1 × PPass,2) + (PFail,1 × PFail,2).

Kappa 1 ka matlab hai perfect agreement. Annotators har cheez par agree hue, aur us agreement me se kuch bhi chance ko attribute nahi kiya ja sakta. Kappa 0 ka matlab hai annotators exactly utni baar agree hue jitni chance predict karta, isliye unka agreement meaningless hai. Negative Kappa ka matlab hai woh chance se bhi kam baar agree hue, jo systematic disagreement suggest karta hai (shayad woh rubric ki opposite interpretations use kar rahe hain).

Worked example — 85% agreement, Kappa sirf 0.48

Calculation ko ek concrete set of labels par try karte hain. Do annotators ne "informativeness" ke liye 100 email summaries label kiye. Results: Annotator A Pass aur Annotator B Pass — 75; A Pass, B Fail — 10; A Fail, B Pass — 5; A Fail, B Fail — 10. Totals: A ne 85 Pass aur 15 Fail diye; B ne 80 Pass aur 20 Fail diye.

Step 1 — Observed agreement (Po): annotators 75 + 10 = 85 items par agree hue: Po = 85 / 100 = 0.85. Step 2 — Expected agreement (Pe): A ne 85% Pass aur 15% Fail label kiye; B ne 80% Pass aur 20% Fail: Pe = (0.85 × 0.80) + (0.15 × 0.20) = 0.68 + 0.03 = 0.71. Step 3 — Kappa: κ = (0.85 − 0.71) / (1 − 0.71) = 0.14 / 0.29 ≈ 0.48. 85% raw agreement ke bawjood, Kappa sirf 0.48 hai (moderate agreement). Apparent agreement ka bada hissa isliye tha kyunki dono annotators Pass favour kar rahe the.

Kappa scores interpret karna

Kappa values ki ek standard interpretation hai: < 0 — Poor (chance se bhi bura); 0.00–0.20 — Slight; 0.21–0.40 — Fair; 0.41–0.60 — Moderate; 0.61–0.80 — Substantial; 0.81–1.00 — Almost perfect. Practically, apne labels ko reliable treat karne se pehle κ ≥ 0.6 ka aim rakho. Us threshold se neeche, rubric ko likely refinement chahiye, kyunki annotators use bahut alag tareeke se interpret kar rahe hain aur consistent labels produce nahi kar sakte.

Kitna strict hona hai, ye is par depend karta hai ki aap labels ko kis liye use kar rahe hain. Rubric iteration ke liye (matlab decide karna ki aapki failure categories ko split ya merge karna hai), κ lagbhag 0.5 workable hai. LLM judge ko human labels ke against validate karne ke liye kam se kam 0.6 ka aim rakho. Un labels ke liye jo model training ya regulatory reporting me jate hain, 0.7 ya usse upar ka aim rakho. Note karo ki subjective tasks ke liye κ ≥ 0.6 bahut challenging hai; kai real-world annotation projects me κ lagbhag 0.4 bhi meaningful progress represent karta hai.

IAA ko, kuch had tak, apne automated evaluators ki ceiling ke roop me dekha ja sakta hai. Agar human annotators κ = 0.7 par agree karte hain, to hum expect nahi kar sakte ki ek LLM judge reliably us level ki accuracy se exceed karega, kyunki jin labels se use compare kiya ja raha hai, woh khud noisy hain. Chapter 5 me judge performance evaluate karte waqt agreement level ko dhyaan me rakho.

Agar aapka Kappa 0.6 se significantly neeche hai, to blindly aur traces label karna continue mat karo. Aap sirf inconsistent data produce karenge. Un specific traces ko dekho jahan annotators disagree hue. Alignment session wale example me, do annotators ne ek hi response padha jahan ek duplex ko "popular with families" kaha gaya tha — ek ne use persona mismatch dekha, dusre ne use relevant tenant-demand context dekha. Us disagreement ne highlight kiya ki rubric ne kabhi specify hi nahi kiya tha ki family-oriented language investor-appropriate qualify karti hai ya nahi, jab woh rental appeal describe karti hai. Is ek trace par quick discussion se ek explicit decision rule bana aur rubric improve hui. Us calibration ke bina team inconsistently label karna continue karti.

Kuch failure modes inherently agree karne me mushkil bhi hote hain. Factual errors high agreement produce karte hain, kyunki ya to response kehta hai ki property me teen bedrooms hain ya nahi kehta. Lekin tone, persona fit ya "appropriateness" ke judgments aksar aisa nahi karte. Us example me, "client persona match" ne pehle pass par sirf 0.3 ya 0.4 ka Kappa hit kiya. Team ne alignment improve kiya — "client persona match" ko do alag criteria me split karke: ek ye ki response me client ke goals ke liye relevant information hai ya nahi (jaise investors ke liye cap rates), aur dusra ye ki woh aisi language avoid karta hai ya nahi jo alag audience ko address karne jaisi lage. Annotators pehle sawaal par agree kar rahe the lekin dusre par disagree kar rahe the, isliye unhe alag karne se pata chala ki rubric ko asal me kahan kaam chahiye tha.

Python implementation

Cohen's Kappa ka Python implementation straightforward hai: do lists of labels lo, observed agreement gino (kitne items par dono raters match karte hain, total se divide karo), phir har label ki frequency se expected agreement compute karo (har label ke liye dono raters ki proportions multiply karke sum karo), aur phir κ = (Po − Pe) / (1 − Pe) apply karo. Edge cases handle karne hote hain: agar koi items hi nahi hain to convention ke hisaab se 1.0 return karo (perfect agreement); agar expected agreement 1.0 hai aur observed bhi 1.0 hai to 1.0 return karo, lekin agar expected 1.0 hai aur observed nahi hai to error raise karo, kyunki input labels me kuch galat hai. Example usage: annotations_a = ['Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Fail'] aur annotations_b = ['Pass', 'Fail', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Pass'] par function chalane se Kappa print hota hai. (Poora code book ke code ke roop me SPA ke code section me milta hai.)

Kab dusre metrics use karein

Cohen's Kappa ek specific situation ke liye design hua hai: do annotators, wahi items, categorical labels. Jab aapka setup alag ho, to dusre metrics zyada appropriate ho sakte hain.

  • Do se zyada annotators — Fleiss's Kappa: agar teen ya zyada log wahi traces label kar rahe hain, to Fleiss's Kappa use karo, jo Cohen's Kappa ko multiple raters tak generalize karta hai. Jahan Cohen's Kappa ek pair compare karta hai, Fleiss's Kappa saare items par average agreement measure karta hai, chance ke liye adjust karke. Formula wahi hai — κ = (Po − Pe) / (1 − Pe) — lekin Po yahan saare items par average observed agreement hai (har item par annotators ne kitni baar wahi label assign kiya, use dekh kar compute hota hai) aur Pe chance se expected agreement hai (saare annotators par labels ki overall distribution se compute hota hai). Interpretation Cohen's Kappa jaisi hi hai (0.6 se upar substantial agreement), lekin calculation ek se zyada pair compare karna account karta hai.
  • Ordinal ratings — Weighted Kappa: agar aapke labels ki natural order hai (jaise 1–5 quality scale), to standard Kappa saare disagreements ko equally bad treat karta hai: kisi cheez ko 4 versus 5 rate karna, 1 versus 5 rate karne jaisa hi gina jata hai. Aksar aap ye nahi chahte, kyunki ek point off hona chaar points off hone se kam serious hai. Weighted Kappa isko address karta hai — alag levels ke disagreement ko alag weights assign karke. Formula hai κw = (Po(w) − Pe(w)) / (1 − Pe(w)), jahan weighted observed aur expected agreement ek weight matrix use karke compute hote hain jo specify karta hai ki har type ka disagreement kitna "bad" hai. Ek common choice hai quadratic weights, jahan disagreement ki penalty labels ke beech distance ke square ke saath badhti hai: 1 versus 5 disagreement ko 1 versus 2 disagreement se 16 guna zyada penalize kiya jata hai. Ye keh kar bhi, hum generally ordinal scales ke bajaye binary Pass/Fail labels recommend karte hain. 5-point scale ke saath aapko define karna hota hai ki 3 ko 4 se kya distinguish karta hai, aur annotators ki in boundaries ke baare me aksar alag intuitions hoti hain. Binary labels aapko ek clear decision lene ke liye force karte hain: kya ye trace bar meet karta hai ya nahi? Agar aapka application itna mature hai ki aap finer-grained quality distinctions chahte hain (jaise prioritize karna ki kaunse acceptable responses ko aur improve karna hai), to ordinal scales useful ho sakte hain. Lekin binary labels se shuru karo, jab tak aapke paas zyada granularity ki specific wajah na ho.
  • Missing data — Krippendorff's Alpha: practically, har annotator har trace label nahi karta. Koi beemar ho jata hai, ya aap deliberately kaam split karte hain taaki har item ko annotators ka sirf ek subset dekhe. Cohen's Kappa complete overlap assume karta hai — dono annotators ne saare wahi items label kiye hon. Krippendorff's Alpha missing data ko gracefully handle karta hai. Formula hai: α = 1 − (Do / De), jahan Do observed disagreement hai (actual labels se compute hota hai) aur De chance se expected disagreement hai. Kappa ke opposite, jo agreement compute karta hai, Alpha disagreement compute karta hai aur use 1 se subtract karta hai. Ye formulation naturally missing data handle karti hai kyunki ye sirf un label pairs ko consider karti hai jo asal me exist karte hain. Alpha kisi bhi number ke annotators aur kisi bhi measurement scale (binary, ordinal, interval, ya ratio) ke saath bhi kaam karta hai, jo use flexible default banata hai jab aapka annotation setup complex ho. Alpha values Kappa jaise hi interpret hote hain: 1 ka matlab perfect agreement, 0 ka matlab chance se behtar agreement nahi, aur negative values ka matlab systematic disagreement. Krippendorff α ≥ 0.8 ko reliable data ke liye recommend karte hain aur α 0.67 se 0.8 ke beech ko tentative conclusions ke liye acceptable mante hain. Ye thresholds typical Kappa guidance se strict hain, isliye ghabrao mat agar data jo κ ≥ 0.6 clear karta hai, woh phir bhi α ≥ 0.8 se short padta hai.

Zyadaatar binary ya categorical labeling tasks ke liye jin me do raters hon aur complete coverage ho, Cohen's Kappa sahi choice hai. Ye compute karne me simple hai aur widely samjha jata hai. Jab aapki situation zyada complex ho, to Krippendorff's Alpha ek flexible alternative hai jo multiple raters, ordinal scales aur missing data ko ek hi framework me handle karta hai.

Ek common galti — Kappa se LLM judge ko evaluate karna

LLM-as-judge evaluators Chapter 5 ka focus hain, lekin agreement metrics discuss karte waqt ek common mistake note karni hai: Cohen's Kappa use karke measure karna ki ek LLM judge human-generated "ground truth" labels se kitna match karta hai. Cohen's Kappa do peers ke beech agreement measure karta hai. Kisi ko bhi "correct" assume nahi kiya jata. Ye appropriate hai jab do humans ek saath rubric develop kar rahe hon. Aap jaanna chahte hain ki woh rubric ko wahi tareeke se interpret karte hain ya nahi, kaun sahi hai ye nahi.

Jab aapke paas gold-standard human labels establish ho jayein, to aapke paas ek source of truth hai. Agar aap jaanna chahte hain ki ek LLM judge un labels se match karta hai ya nahi, to aap ye nahi poochh rahe ki "kya ye do raters agree karte hain?" — aap ye poochh rahe hain ki "kya ye judge sahi answer deta hai?" Ye ek classification problem hai, aur aapko jaanna hai ki judge kis tareeke se galat hai. Kya judge ne Pass kaha jab human ne Fail kaha (ek false positive)? Ya Fail kaha jab human ne Pass kaha (ek false negative)? Ek judge jo bahut lenient hai, bure outputs miss karega. Ek judge jo bahut strict hai, achhe outputs ko unnecessary review ke liye flag karega. Precision, recall aur true/false positive rates jaise classification metrics se aap in failure modes ko alag-alag diagnose kar sakte hain. Cohen's Kappa se aapko sirf ye pata chalta hai ki humans aur LLM judges disagree karte hain — isliye judge evaluation ke liye Kappa use karne ki galti mat karo.

Yaad rakho: 85% agreement impressive lag sakta hai, lekin agar 90% traces Pass hain to chance se bhi 82% agreement mil jata. Kappa = (Po − Pe) / (1 − Pe) — aur κ ≥ 0.6 se pehle labels par bharosa mat karo. Aur judge ko human labels se compare karna ho to precision/recall use karo, Kappa nahi.
Cohen's Kappa — Python implementation + example usage — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 4)
from collections import Counter

def cohens_kappa(rater1, rater2):
  """
  Compute Cohen's Kappa for two lists of categorical ratings.

     Args:
         rater1: List of labels from first annotator
         rater2: List of labels from second annotator

  Returns:
      float: Cohen's Kappa score
  """
  assert len(rater1) == len(rater2), "Rating lists must have
same length"
  n_items = len(rater1)

     if n_items == 0:
         return 1.0 # Convention: perfect agreement if nothing to
rate

  # Observed agreement
  agreements = sum(1 for i in range(n_items) if rater1[i] ==
rater2[i])
  p_observed = agreements / n_items

     # Expected agreement by chance
     labels = set(rater1) | set(rater2)
     count1 = Counter(rater1)
     count2 = Counter(rater2)

  p_expected = sum(
      (count1.get(label, 0) / n_items) * (count2.get(label, 0)
/ n_items)
      for label in labels
  )

  # Handle edge case where expected agreement is 1
  # (all items have the same label from both raters)
  if p_expected == 1.0:
      if p_observed == 1.0:
          return 1.0
      raise ValueError(
          "Expected agreement is 1.0 but observed agreement is
not; "
          "check that the input labels are correct."
      )
    return (p_observed - p_expected) / (1 - p_expected)


# Example usage
annotations_a = ['Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass',
'Fail']
annotations_b = ['Pass', 'Fail', 'Fail', 'Pass', 'Fail', 'Pass',
'Pass']
print(f"Cohen's Kappa: {cohens_kappa(annotations_a,
annotations_b):.3f}")
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 4 — Collaborative Evaluation Practices
