04.3Chapter 4 · Collaborative Evaluation Practices

Rubrics, Golden Datasets aur Benevolent Dictator

Collaborative workflow tabhi kaam karta hai jab aapko pata ho ki kab collaboration chahiye hi nahi. Kai cases me ek single trusted expert — ek "benevolent dictator" — multiple annotators se zyada effective hota hai. Aur jab collaboration zaroori ho, to alignment sessions aur achhi rubrics hi woh jagah hain jahan agreement banta hai. Ye section dono ko cover karta hai, aur batata hai ki final gold-standard dataset ko kaise save karna hai.

Benevolent dictator — kab ek expert kaafi hai

Collaborative workflows me dive karne se pehle consider karo: kya aapko asal me multiple annotators chahiye? Kai cases me answer nahi hai. Chhoti se medium-sized companies me, ek single principal domain expert appoint karna (koi aisa vyakti jiska judgment evaluation ke liye definitive standard ho) aksar zyada effective hota hai. Hum ise "benevolent dictator" model kehte hain, open source software governance se liya gaya term. Jaise kuch successful open source projects me ek single maintainer hota hai jiska judgment final hota hai, waise hi kuch evaluation efforts ko ek vyakti se fayda hota hai jiska word "ground truth" hota hai.

Benevolent dictator model tab achha kaam karta hai jab kuch conditions hold karti hain: pehle, ek clear authority figure ho jiska judgment team trust karti ho. Ye vyakti define karta hai ki technically kya acceptable hai aur team ko samajhne me madad karta hai ki product users ki asal chah se match karta hai ya nahi. Jab ek vyakti ka judgment standard ho, to resolve karne ke liye annotation conflicts hi nahi hote. Dusre, evaluation criteria us vyakti ki expertise ke andar hon. Evaluation process me unhe throughout involve karke, aap un preferences aur expectations ko uncover karte hain jo woh upfront articulate nahi kar pate. Traces review karne ki process unhe clarify karne me madad karti hai ki ek "passable" AI interaction kaisa dikhta hai. Teesre, labeling work ka volume ek vyakti ke liye manageable ho. Isse process fast aur simple rehta hai, aur expert ko AI ke development me ek stake milta hai. Woh invested feel karte hain kyunki unhone use shape karne me haath lagaya hai, jo unhe product champion karne ke liye zyada likely banata hai.

Benevolent dictator kaun ho sakta hai? Kuch examples: mental health AI assistant ke liye ek psychologist; legal documents analyze karne wale AI ke liye ek lawyer; support chatbot ke liye ek customer service director; educational AI tool ke liye ek lead teacher ya curriculum developer; chhoti startup me CEO ya founder. Agar aap independent developer hain, to aap default se domain expert hain. Apni expertise ke baare me honest raho, aur apni assumptions ko regularly real user feedback ke against validate karo. Agar aapko leadership par domain expert ke roop me bharosa karna hai, to ensure karo ki unke judgments actual user needs reflect karte hon, personal preferences nahi.

Kai developers khud domain expert banne ki koshish karte hain, ya koi convenient proxy (jaise apne manager) dhoondh lete hain. Ye disaster ka recipe ho sakta hai. Organization bhar me logon ki alag opinions hongi ki kya acceptable hai, aur sab ko khush karna impossible hai. Benevolent dictator model precisely isliye kaam karta hai kyunki woh ek single source of truth designate karke is ambiguity ko kaat deta hai. Lekin is model ki limits bhi hain. Agar domain ek vyakti ke liye comprehensively evaluate karne ke liye bahut complex hai, agar criteria stakeholders ke beech contested hain, ya agar aapko demonstrate karna hai ki aapka evaluation process rigorous aur unbiased hai, to aapko multiple annotators involve karne padenge. Baaki chapter batata hai ki ye effectively kaise karein.

Alignment sessions — disagreements ko rubric improvement me badalna

Jab annotators disagree karte hain, to aapko samajhna hai kyun. Alignment sessions structured discussions hain jahan annotators apne disagreements review karte hain aur rubric improve karne ke liye saath kaam karte hain.

Session ki taiyari

Annotators ko saath lane se pehle aapko teen cheezein karni hain: IAA scores calculate aur share karo; specific disagreements identify karo; ek neutral moderator appoint karo. IAA scores calculate aur share karne ka matlab hai ki sab ko overall agreement level dikhao taaki woh problem ka scope samajh sakein. Example: aap report kar sakte hain — "Factual accuracy criterion par humne 0.74 ka Kappa achieve kiya (substantial agreement). Client persona ke liye appropriate tone par humne 0.38 ka Kappa achieve kiya (fair agreement). Hum alignment session ko tone par focus karenge." Specific disagreements identify karne ka matlab hai un traces ko nikaalo jahan annotators ne alag labels diye. Har disputed trace, har annotator ke labels aur unke notes list karne wala ek summary document taiyar karo.

Is concrete banane ke liye, pichhle chapter wale real estate CRM assistant ko lo, jo agents ko listings search karne, showings schedule karne aur client emails draft karne me madad karta hai. Maan lo aapki team evaluate kar rahi hai ki assistant ke responses "appropriate for the client persona" hain ya nahi. Initial rubric kuch aisi dikh sakti hai: Criterion: Client Persona Match. Pass: Response client ki background aur goals ke hisaab se tailored hai. Ek investor ko investment decisions ke liye relevant information milni chahiye. Ek first-time homebuyer ko aisi information milni chahiye jo use buying process samajhne me madad kare. Fail: Response client ki background aur goals ko ignore ya mismatch karta hai. Examples: [Pass] Investor client property ke baare me poochhta hai; response me rental income potential aur cap rate shamil hai. [Fail] Investor client property ke baare me poochhta hai; response poori tarah school districts aur family amenities par focus karta hai.

Ye rubric reasonable lagti hai. Ye criterion define karti hai, intent explain karti hai aur examples deti hai. Lekin ye important sawal unanswered chhod deti hai. Agar ek response me investment metrics aur family-oriented language dono hain to kya hoga? "Tailored" kya count hota hai? Kya ek relevant detail mention karna kaafi hai, ya poori response match karni chahiye? Neutral aur generic responses ko kaise handle karna chahiye, bajaye actively mismatched ones ke?

Independent labeling ke baad, aapka disagreement summary kuch aisa dikh sakta hai: Trace #23: Investor client ne ek duplex ke baare me poocha. Assistant ne respond kiya: "This duplex is in a growing neighborhood with a strong rental market. The 3-bed/2-bath layout is popular with families, and the backyard is a nice bonus. Current tenant pays $2,400/month." Annotator A: Pass (rental income aur market strength mention karta hai). Annotator B: Fail ("popular with families" aur "backyard" language investor ke liye inappropriate hai). Annotator C: Pass (family language tenant appeal describe karti hai, jo rental investment ke liye relevant hai).

Teeno annotators ne rubric ko good faith me apply kiya, lekin alag conclusions par pahunche. Annotator A ne focus kiya ki investment-relevant information present hai ya nahi. Annotator B ne family-oriented language ko mismatch flag kiya. Annotator C ne wahi language ko relevant investment context interpret kiya (ye explain karna ki property tenants ko kyun attract karti hai). Rubric ne specify nahi kiya tha ki in competing considerations ko kaise weigh karna hai, isliye har annotator ne apna judgment call banaya. Kisi ko discussion ko rubric improve karne par focused rakhna hai, bajaye specific labels par arguments jeetne ke. Ideally, aap ek neutral moderator appoint karenge jo annotators me se ek na ho. Ek project lead ya adjacent team se koi jo product samajhta ho lekin labeling me participate na kiya ho, achha kaam kar sakta hai.

Session chalana — teen sawaal

Alignment session ka goal past labels par agreement force karna nahi hai. Goal hai ye samajhna ki annotators ne rubric ko alag tareeke se kyun interpret kiya, aur rubric ko fix karna taaki future annotations consistent hon. Har disagreement ke liye in sawalon se guzro:

  • Har annotator ne kya socha? Har vyakti ko apni reasoning bina interruption ke explain karne do. Trace #23 example me, Annotator C keh sakta hai: "Maine Pass label kiya kyunki family-oriented language tenant appeal explain kar rahi thi, jo investor ke liye useful information hai jo decide kar raha hai ki property rented rahegi ya nahi." Annotator B counter kar sakta hai: "Lekin rubric kehta hai ki response client ke hisaab se tailored hona chahiye. Popular with families aur nice backyard homebuyer ko bechne jaisa sound karta hai, investor ko nahi." Dono interpretations defensible hain, jiska matlab hai rubric ko is ambiguity ko address karna hai.
  • Rubric kahan fail hoti hai? Rubric me woh specific word, phrase ya gap identify karo jisne alag interpretations allow ki. Trace #23 me, rubric kehti thi ki response "tailored to the client's background and goals" hona chahiye, lekin specify nahi kiya tha ki kya language jo secondary purpose serve karti hai (tenant demographics describe karna) tailored qualify karti hai ya mismatched. Rubric me ye guidance bhi nahi thi ki mixed responses ko kaise handle karein jin me investor-relevant aur family-oriented content dono hon.
  • Future annotators ko agree karne ke liye kya chahiye? Retrospective blame ke bajaye forward-looking changes par focus karo. Trace #23 ke liye team decide kar sakti hai ki ye add kare: "Family-oriented language acceptable hai agar woh explicitly investment value se connect karti ho (jaise popular with families, which keeps vacancy rates low). Investment framing ke bina family-oriented language ko Fail mark karna chahiye."

Har disagreement ko timebox karo taaki session drag na kare. Har case ke liye paanch minutes usually kaafi hote hain. Agar aap use jaldi resolve nahi kar sakte, to follow-up ke liye flag karo aur aage badho.

Rubric improve karne ki techniques

Un disagreements ke basis par jo aap uncover karte hain, aap rubric ko kai tareekon se improve kar sakte hain:

  • Wording clarify karo: Vague ya overloaded terms zyadaatar disagreements cause karte hain. Real estate assistant example me, "tailored to the client's background and goals" ambiguous nikla. Annotators disagree hue ki tenant demographics describe karna investor-tailored content qualify karta hai ya nahi. Revised rubric ko boundaries explicit banani chahiye: Pass — response client ke goals ke liye relevant information par focus karta hai: Investors — financial metrics (cap rate, rental income, appreciation), market conditions, tenant stability aur property condition; tenant demographics ki descriptions sirf tab acceptable hain jab explicitly investment value se connected hon. First-time buyers — affordability, financing options, neighborhood livability aur process guidance. Fail — response me client ke goals se mismatched content hai, bina use unki actual needs se connect kiye.
  • Examples add karo: Concrete Pass/Fail examples aksar abstract definitions se zyada clear hote hain. Jab ek disagreement ek edge case surface karta hai, to use rubric me illustrative example ke roop me add karo. Trace #23 discussion ke baad aap add kar sakte hain: [Pass] Client investor hai. Response: "This duplex offers a 6.2% cap rate with stable rental history. The 3-bed layout is popular with long-term family tenants, which keeps turnover low." [Fail] Client investor hai. Response: "This duplex is in a great neighborhood. The 3-bed layout is popular with families, and the backyard is a nice bonus." (Investment value se koi connection nahi.) [Pass] Client first-time buyer hai. Response: "This home qualifies for FHA loans, which means you could put down as little as 3.5%." [Fail] Client first-time buyer hai. Response: "The cap rate is suboptimal but the IRR looks promising if you refi in year three."
  • Decision rules add karo: Tricky situations ke liye explicit rules do. Example: "Agar response investor client ko family-oriented features (backyard, school district, kid-friendly) mention karta hai, to Pass tabhi label karo jab response explicitly un features ko rental demand, tenant stability ya property value se connect kare. Warna Fail label karo."
  • Criterion split karo: Kabhi disagreements point karte hain ki ek single rubric multiple distinct concepts capture karne ki koshish kar rahi hai. Agar annotators consistently agree karte hain ki financial metrics present hain ya nahi, lekin disagree karte hain ki lifestyle language acceptable hai ya nahi, to "client persona match" ko do alag criteria me split karne par consider karo: "includes relevant information" aur "avoids mismatched framing". Har criterion ke liye agreement alag measure karna batayega ki kis ko zyada kaam chahiye.
  • Irreducible ambiguity acknowledge karo: Kuch cases genuinely borderline hote hain. Ek response jo investor ko "good schools nearby" mention karta hai, bina elaboration ke, use rental-demand signal ya mismatched homebuyer language, dono tareeke se interpret kiya ja sakta hai. Agar reasonable log legitimately disagree kar sakte hain, to ambiguity document karo aur ek tiebreaker rule establish karo (jaise "agar investment value se connection implied hai lekin explicit nahi hai, to Pass label karo").

Kya avoid karna hai

Rubric fix karne ke liye majority voting par bharosa mat karo. Voting individual label disagreements resolve kar sakti hai, lekin voting rubric improve nahi karti. Agar teen annotators ek trace par 2-1 vote karte hain, to aapne woh trace resolve kar liya hai lekin ye nahi seekha ki woh disagree kyun hue. Voting ko sirf last resort ke roop me use karo, rubric stable hone ke baad final labels finalize karne ke liye. Discussions ko adversarial mat bano. Goal rubric improve karna hai, ye prove karna nahi ki ek annotator "sahi" tha. Disagreements ko is roop me frame karo ki woh information hain ki rubric ko kahan kaam chahiye. Documentation skip mat karo. Har rubric change aur uske peeche ki reasoning likh lo. Future annotators (aur future aap) ko ye context chahiye hoga.

Escalation

Kabhi annotators discussion ke baad bhi agreement tak nahi pahunch pate. Jab aisa hota hai, to project lead ya senior domain expert tak escalate karo jo binding decision le sake. Ruling ko document karo aur rubric me add karo. Persistent disagreement aksar indicate karta hai ki criterion khud poorly defined hai ya annotators ke fundamentally alag values hain — dono hi surface karna important hai.

Sab kuch save karo — golden dataset

Automated evaluator train ya prompt karne ke baad bhi, apna gold-standard dataset aur documentation rakho. Aapko unki baad me zaroorat pad sakti hai: automated evaluators validate karna — jab aap LLM-as-judge ya dusra automated evaluator banate hain (Chapter 5 me cover hota hai), to aapko ground truth labels chahiye hote hain taaki measure kar sakein ki evaluator accurate hai ya nahi; gold-standard dataset woh ground truth deta hai. Fine-tuning — agar aap decide karte hain ki ek specialized LLM train karna hai, to labeled data training data ban jata hai. Auditing — agar stakeholders aapki evaluation methodology par sawaal uthate hain, to aapke paas documented rubrics, agreement scores aur consensus labels hain jo dikhate hain ki process rigorous tha. Ye dataset aur documentation woh foundation hai jis par Measure phase banta hai — iske bina aapke automated evaluators ke paas compare karne ke liye kuch nahi hota.

Yaad rakho: Alignment session ka goal past labels jeetna nahi hai — goal hai rubric ko itna clear banana ki agle annotator ko guess na karna pade. Har disagreement rubric me ek kami hai, kisi vyakti ki galti nahi.

05Chapter 5 · Implementing Automated Evaluators

Implementing Automated Evaluators

Chapter 3 me tumne traces padh kar failure modes pehchane, Chapter 4 me team ke saath tay kiya ki failure ka matlab kya hai — ab baari hai us measurement ko automate karne ki, taaki har trace ko haath se padhe bina, scale par failure rate track kar sako. Ye chapter batata hai ki failure modes ko precise, automatable metrics me kaise badlo, code-based checks kab use karo aur LLM-as-judge kab, judge ko human labels ke against kaise validate karo, aur production me agent ki asli success rate kaise estimate karo.

Measure phase ka matlab kya hai?

Poora evaluation loop hai Analyze-Measure-Improve. Analyze phase me tumne samjha ki system kahan fail ho raha hai. Measure phase me tum us samajh ko numbers me badalte ho — har failure mode ke liye ek metric, har metric ke liye ek automated evaluator. Manual labeling is scale par bahut slow aur mehenga hai, isliye automation zaroori hai. Lekin ek shart hai: har evaluator human-defined failure criteria se tightly grounded hona chahiye, warna metrics ka koi matlab nahi — tum kuch bhi measure kar loge, lekin woh woh cheez nahi hogi jo asal me matter karti hai.

Running example wahi hai jo Chapter 3 se chal raha hai: ek real estate chat-based CRM assistant jo real estate agents ke natural language queries samajhta hai, SQL chalata hai, client emails draft karta hai, calendar padhta hai aur internet search karta hai. Isi example se saare failure modes samjhaye gaye hain.

Pehle ambiguity fix karo, phir measure karo

Failure modes ki list banane ke baad, pehla kaam ye decide karna hai ki kaunsi failure asal me measure karne layak hai. Yahan Three Gulfs model kaam aata hai — Gulf of Comprehension (apna data samajhna), Gulf of Specification (achhe prompts aur agents likhna) aur Gulf of Generalization (clear instructions se sahi generalize karna). Specification ki galtiyan, matlab ambiguous ya incomplete instructions jo tumne LLM ko di, aksar sirf prompt edit karke fix ho jati hain. Aise failure mode ke liye automated evaluator banana wasted effort hai — evals banane aur maintain karne me time aur effort lagta hai, isliye unhe un issues ke liye bachao jo prompt clear karne ke baad bhi bachte hain.

Do reasons hain. Pehla, efficiency: bahut si specification failures prompt me clarity ya detail add karte hi fix ho jati hain. Doosra, aur zyada fundamental: tumhari evaluation ko LLM ki generalization ability reflect karni chahiye, ye nahi ki woh tumhare ambiguous intent ko kitna achha "mind-read" kar leta hai. Poorly specified task ke liye evaluator banana basically ye measure karta hai ki LLM tumhara dimaag kitna padh sakta hai — ye scalable ya reliable indicator nahi hai robust performance ka.

Kaunsi failure kis Gulf ki hai?

Real estate assistant ke failure modes ko hi dekho. Incomplete email content — agar email generation prompt me mandatory fields (budget, location, client name) include karne ki clear instruction hi nahi thi, to ye specification failure hai; prompt sudhaaro, evaluator mat banao. Lekin agar prompt me constraint clearly likha tha — jaise "max_price: $600k" — aur LLM ne phir bhi SQL me woh constraint chhod diya, to ye generalization failure hai, aur iske liye automated evaluator banta hai. Persona-tone mismatch bhi generalization failure hai, agar client persona clearly diya gaya tha. Invalid tool usage — aisa tool call karna jo exist hi nahi karta, jaise book_showings — lagbhag hamesha generalization failure hai, agar available tools LLM ko achhe se define kiye gaye the. Incorrect SQL aggregation (day ke bajay week se group karna, ambiguous phrasing ki wajah se), incorrect tool sequencing (listing data retrieve kiye bina email likhne lagna), unjustified tool calls (bina request ke scheduling ya messaging karna), aur location ambiguity ("Springfield" jaisi common jagah ko galat region samajhna) — in sabko isi lens se dekho: pehle prompt ki ambiguity fix karo, jo bache use measure karo.

Har failure mode ke liye do tarah ke metrics

Refined list milne ke baad, har significant failure mode ke liye specific, automatable metrics design karo — ideally dono tarah ke: reference-based aur reference-free. Reference-based metric me tumhare paas golden reference hota hai, matlab ideal output jo failure exhibit nahi karta. Evaluator measure karta hai ki agent ka actual output is golden reference se kitna closely align karta hai. Missing SQL constraints ke liye reference data hoga user queries aur unke corresponding ideal SQL, jinme saare necessary constraints hain; evaluator check karta hai ki generated SQL reference ke constraints ko correctly incorporate karta hai ya nahi. Reference-based metrics iterative development (prompt engineering ya model fine-tuning) ke dauran invaluable hain, aur continuous integration (CI) checks ka key component bhi hain, jo Chapter 9 me aate hain.

Reference-free metric me koi golden answer nahi chahiye — evaluator intrinsic properties ya rules check karta hai jo failure mode se related hain. Missing SQL constraints ke liye reference-free check generated SQL ko parse karke dekhega ki expected constraints se associated keywords present hain ya nahi — jaise input me price mention hua to SQL me price-related column ka reference hai ya nahi — ya general SQL validity check karega. Persona-tone mismatch ke liye reference-free approach generated email ki tone classify karke (formal, casual, data-driven) target persona ki known preferences se match karega, ya specific jargon ya phrases ki presence ya absence check karega. Reference-free metrics khaas taur par powerful hain kyunki ye aksar naye, unlabeled data par efficiently scale par chal sakte hain — broader monitoring, potentially online settings me bhi.

Executability checks — sirf text nahi, kaam bhi

Dono tarah ke metrics ke saath executability checks bhi add kar sakte ho. Ye functional correctness assess karte hain, sirf text ko nahi. Agar LLM ne SQL query generate ki, to evaluator use test database ke against execute karke dekhega ki woh bina error ke chalti hai aur plausible results deti hai ya nahi. Agar LLM ne tool calls generate kiye, to evaluator unhe simulate karke verify karega ki woh logically consistent hain aur intended outcome achieve kar sakte hain ya nahi. Ye checks confirm karte hain ki output asal me kaam karta hai, sirf dikhne me sahi nahi lagta.

Code se measure karo ya LLM judge se?

Har failure mode ka apna dedicated evaluator hota hai. Nature pe depend karta hai ki use code se implement karo ya LLM se. Code-based evaluators ideal hain jab failure definition objective ho aur rules se check ho sake — jaise JSON validity ya SQL syntax parse karna, regex ya string matching se required ya forbidden phrases detect karna, structural constraints count ya verify karna (jaise summary me exactly teen bullet points hain), LLM ke generate kiye tool call ko execute karke dekhna ki error aaya ya nahi, aur logical checks (jaise query dog-friendly apartment ki hai to output me "pets allowed" mention hai ya nahi). Code evaluators fast, cheap, deterministic aur interpretable hote hain, aur reference-free checks (length limits) aur reference-based checks (gold set se value extraction compare karna) dono support karte hain.

LLM-as-judge evaluators tab use hote hain jab failure mode me interpretation ya nuance ho jo code capture nahi kar sakta — jaise tone appropriate thi ya nahi, summary faithful thi ya nahi, response helpful thi ya nahi. In cases me ek alag LLM (main application wale se distinct) ko judge bana kar outputs ko ek single failure mode ke liye judge karwate ho. Har metric ke liye alag LLM-as-judge evaluator chahiye ho sakta hai, jo uski specific failure definition ke liye tailored ho — ye expected hai, aur desirable bhi, jab quality ke multiple aspects evaluate kar rahe ho. LLM judges narrowly defined, binary tasks (Pass ya Fail) ke liye best kaam karte hain. Open-ended ratings ya feedback supervise aur align karna mushkil hota hai. Aur LLM se evaluation karne me bias, inconsistency aur inference cost bhi aati hai — isliye prompt design, clear criteria aur human judgments ke against calibration, teeno important hain. Is chapter ke aage ke sections inhi cheezon ko detail me kholte hain: judge prompts kaise likhein, metrics kaise implement karein, judge ko statistically kaise calibrate karein, aur poori evaluator pipeline kaise banayein.

Yaad rakho: Pehle prompt ki ambiguity fix karo, phir jo failure bache use measure karo. Specification failure ke liye evaluator banana ye measure karta hai ki LLM tumhara dimaag kitna padh sakta hai — generalization failure ke liye evaluator banana ye measure karta hai ki woh clear instructions se kitna sahi kaam karta hai. Dono me farak samajhna hi sahi measurement ki shuruaat hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Implementing Automated Evaluators
← Previous04.3 · Rubrics, Golden Datasets aur Benevolent Dictator→ Next05.1 · LLM-as-Judge — design aur validation
05.1Chapter 5 · Implementing Automated Evaluators

LLM-as-Judge — design aur validation

Jab failure mode me nuance ho — tone, faithfulness, helpfulness — to code kaam nahi karta, aur ek LLM ko judge bana kar output ko check karwana padta hai. Lekin LLM judge ko aise hi prompt de dena kaafi nahi: judges me systematic biases hote hain, aur bina careful design aur validation ke unke scores par bharosa nahi kar sakte. Ye section batata hai ki reliable LLM-as-judge evaluator kaise design karein.

LLM-as-judge kahan se aaya?

Ye term ek research paper se aaya jisne human preference data par specialized LLM judges train kiye the. Fine-tuning se judge ka behaviour human expectations se align hota hai aur benchmark settings me strong performance milti hai. Lekin practice me aisi fine-tuning rarely feasible hoti hai — zyada tar applications ke paas kaafi labeled preference data nahi hota, khaas taur par development ke early stages me. Isliye hum off-the-shelf LLMs ko judge banate hain aur prompt engineering se unke outputs ko apni intended failure definitions se align karte hain.

Judge ke teen systematic biases

Usi research me LLM judges ki reliability problems bhi document ki gayi thi. Ek popular leaderboard chalane wali research group ne test kiya ki LLM judge ki ratings human reviewers ki ratings se match karti hain ya nahi, aur teen systematic biases mile:

  • Position bias: Jab do responses ko side by side compare karne ko kaha jaye, to judge us response ko favour karta hai jo pehle aati hai (ya kuch models ke liye jo doosri aati hai), chahe dono responses equal quality ki hon. Study me ek leading model ne apne lagbhag 26% judgments me ye bias dikhaya.
  • Verbosity bias: Lambi responses ko higher quality rate kiya jata hai, chahe chhoti response equally correct ho. Aise bias wala judge agent ko outputs pad karne ke liye reward dega.
  • Self-enhancement bias: Jab judge aur judge kiya ja raha agent same model ho (jaise ek hi model apne outputs ko judge kar raha ho), to judge agent ke outputs ko neutral judge se zyada favourably rate karta hai.

Ye biases LLM judges ko useless nahi banate, lekin raw judge scores par akele bharosa nahi kar sakte. Prompts aur validation procedures aise design karne padte hain jo inhe control karein — aur wahi is chapter ka baaki hissa karta hai.

Ek achhe judge prompt ke chaar components

Har evaluator ek single metric se correspond karta hai, jo error analysis me identify kiye gaye ek specific failure mode ko target karta hai. Task ko binary outputs tak restrict karte hain — Pass/Fail ya Yes/No. Ek well-structured LLM-as-judge prompt me chaar essential components hote hain:

  1. Clear task aur evaluation criterion: Har prompt ek well-scoped failure mode par focus karta hai. Vague tasks unreliable judgments dete hain. Ye poochhne ke bajay ki email "achha" hai ya nahi, poochho ki "tone luxury buyer persona ke liye appropriate hai ya nahi."
  2. Precise Pass/Fail definitions: Pass ka matlab kya hai (failure absent) aur Fail ka matlab kya hai (failure present), seedha error analysis me develop ki gayi failure descriptions se define karo.
  3. Few-shot examples: Examples judge ki decision boundary calibrate karne me help karte hain. Clearly Pass aur clearly Fail karne wale labeled outputs include karo. Ye best hain human-labeled traces se liye gaye — jo data splits wale section me aate hain.
  4. Structured output format: Judge consistent, machine-readable format me respond kare — typically ek JSON object jisme do fields hon: reasoning (ek-do sentence ki explanation) aur answer ("Pass" ya "Fail"). Ye structure accuracy aur interpretability dono improve karta hai.

Example: tone appropriateness ka judge prompt

Real estate CRM assistant ke liye tone ka prompt template is structure ko dikhata hai. Prompt kehta hai: tum ek expert evaluator ho, tumhara task hai determine karna ki assistant-generated email client persona ke liye appropriate tone use karta hai ya nahi. Phir Pass/Fail definitions: Fail matlab email ki tone, language ya formality described client persona ke saath inconsistent ya unsuitable hai; Pass matlab tone, language aur formality persona ki expectations se achhe se align karte hain.

Phir client personas ka overview: Luxury Buyers polished, highly professional aur deferential language expect karte hain — slang ya excessive casualness avoid karo. First-Time Homebuyers ko friendly, reassuring aur patient tone se fayda hota hai — overly complex jargon avoid karo. Investors concise, data-driven aur direct communication prefer karte hain — effusiveness avoid karo. Phir output format (JSON, reasoning + answer) aur do examples: ek Luxury Buyer ko "Hey there! Got some truly awesome listings..." jaisa slang-filled email — Fail, kyunki excessive slang aur overly casual tone luxury persona ke liye unsuitable hai. Doosra, First-Time Homebuyer ko "Good morning! I've found a few properties that seem like a great fit for getting started in the market..." — Pass, kyunki friendly, reassuring tone suitable hai aur next steps clearly offer karta hai. Har evaluator isi structure ko follow karta hai, lekin apne specific failure mode ke liye tailored hota hai.

Judge ko kab LLM se aur kab code se?

Table ke hisaab se, persona-tone mismatch ke liye programmatic evaluator N/A hai (subjective hai) — wahan few-shot LLM prompt chahiye jisme definitions aur examples ke saath tone alignment judge ho. Unjustified tool calls ke liye dono kaam karte hain: regex-based filter koi bhi action flag kar sakta hai jo input context me grounded nahi hai, aur LLM prompt assess kar sakta hai ki har tool call requested thi ya prior steps se justified thi. Rule ye hai: definition objective ho to code, nuance ho to judge — aur aksar dono ko combine karo.

Yaad rakho: Judge prompt me chaar cheezein honi chahiye — ek clear criterion, precise Pass/Fail definitions, human-labeled few-shot examples, aur JSON jaisa structured output. Aur judge ke biases (position, verbosity, self-enhancement) ko yaad rakho: raw judge score kabhi bhi apne aap me sach nahi hota, use validate karna padta hai — jo agle sections me aata hai.
Example 5-1 — LLM-as-judge prompt template (tone appropriateness) — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 5)
You are an expert evaluator assessing outputs from a real estate
assistant chatbot.

Your Task: Determine if the assistant-generated email to a client
uses a tone appropriate for the specified client persona.

Evaluation Criterion: Tone Appropriateness

Definition of Pass/Fail:
- Fail: The email's tone, language, or level of formality is
inconsistent with or unsuitable for the described client persona.
- Pass: The email's tone, language, and formality align well with
the client persona's expectations.

Client Personas Overview:
- Luxury Buyers: Expect polished, highly professional, and
deferential language. Avoid slang or excessive casualness.
- First-Time Homebuyers: Benefit from a friendly, reassuring, and
patient tone. Avoid overly complex jargon.
- Investors: Prefer concise, data-driven, and direct communication.
Avoid effusiveness.

Output Format:
Return your evaluation as a JSON object with two keys:
1. "reasoning": A brief explanation (1-2 sentences) for your
 decision.
2. "answer": Either "Pass" or "Fail".

Examples:
-----

Input 1:
Client Persona: Luxury Buyer
Generated Email: "Hey there! Got some truly awesome listings for
you in the high-end district. Super views, totally posh. Wanna
check 'em out ASAP?"

Evaluation 1:
{
"reasoning": "The email uses excessive slang ('Hey there',
  'awesome', 'totally posh', 'ASAP') and an overly casual tone,
  which is unsuitable for a Luxury Buyer persona.",
"answer": "Fail"
}


-----

Input 2:
Client Persona: First-Time Homebuyer
Generated Email: "Good morning! I've found a few properties that
seem like a great fit for getting started in the market, keeping
your budget in mind. They offer good value and are in nice,
welcoming neighborhoods. Would you be interested in learning more
or perhaps scheduling a visit?"

Evaluation 2:
{
"reasoning": "The email adopts a friendly, reassuring tone
  ('great fit for getting started', 'nice, welcoming
  neighborhoods') suitable for a First-Time Homebuyer, and
  clearly offers next steps.",
"answer": "Pass"
}

-----

Now, evaluate the following:

Client Persona: {{CLIENT_PERSONA_HERE}}
Generated Email: {{GENERATED_EMAIL_HERE}}

Your JSON Evaluation:
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Implementing Automated Evaluators

05.2Chapter 5 · Implementing Automated Evaluators

Metrics — exact, similarity aur task-specific

Metric woh precise, quantifiable definition hai jo batati hai ki failure mode present hai ya nahi. Is section me alag-alag tarah ke metrics hain — exact checks jo code se hote hain, similarity-based checks jo meaning compare karte hain, aur task-specific group metrics jo multiple outputs ko ek saath evaluate karte hain. Sahi metric chunna hi sahi measurement hai; galat metric chunoge to galat cheez optimize karoge.

Exact aur code-based metrics

Sabse straightforward metrics woh hain jo exact matching ya rules se check hote hain. Reference-based exact checks me generated output ko golden reference se compare karte hain — jaise generated SQL ki abstract syntax tree (AST) ko golden AST se compare karke verify karna ki saare expected WHERE clauses present hain. Reference-free exact checks me rules directly apply hote hain — jaise regex ya AST traversal se mandatory filter keywords (pets_allowed, max_price) detect karna, static schema check se ensure karna ki har invoked tool name registered tool registry me exist karta hai, ya keyword presence check se mandatory sections (budget, location, client name) verify karna.

Code evaluators structure parse karte hain (JSON validity, SQL syntax), regex ya string matching se required ya forbidden phrases detect karte hain, structural constraints count ya verify karte hain, tool call execute karke dekhte hain ki error aaya ya nahi, aur logical checks karte hain. Ye fast, cheap, deterministic aur interpretable hote hain — aur isiliye jahan bhi definition objective ho, wahan pehli pasand hone chahiye. LLM judge ko sirf wahan lao jahan code se kaam na chale.

Similarity metrics — wording alag, meaning same?

Kai baar exact match bahut strict hota hai: output sahi ho sakta hai lekin wording golden reference se alag ho. Wahan semantic similarity kaam aati hai. Text ko embeddings (vector representations) me convert karke, candidate output ke embedding aur reference (jaise input ya ideal answer) ke embedding ke beech cosine similarity compute karte hain. Ye score batata hai ki meaning kitna closely match karta hai, chahe wording differ kare. Ye binary Pass/Fail se aage ja kar batata hai ki outputs desired response se semantically kitne close hain — ek continuous score, jo ranking ya comparison ke liye useful hai.

Group metrics: Success@k, Precision@k, Recall@k

LLM agents aksar ek input ke liye multiple candidates generate karte hain — multiple completions, retrieved documents, ya answer options. In cases me group ki quality evaluate karni hoti hai, har output ko isolation me nahi. Success@k (code generation me Pass@k bhi kehte hain) woh fraction hai evaluation problems ka jinme top k outputs me se kam se kam ek correct ho (jaise saare unit tests pass kare). Example: code generator har problem ke liye paanch candidate completions banaye, to Pass@5 woh fraction hai problems ka jinme kam se kam ek candidate saare tests pass karta hai.

Precision@k measure karta hai ki top k outputs me se kitne correct hain — top k me relevant items ka fraction. Agar LLM paanch API calls propose kare aur teen valid hon, to Precision@5 = 0.6. Ye batata hai ki top ke outputs kitne achhe hain. Recall@k coverage measure karta hai: total relevant items me se kitne top k me mil gaye. Agar 10 correct answers me se 3 top 3 suggestions me aayein, to Recall@3 = 0.3. High precision aur low recall ka matlab hai system jab guess karta hai to sahi hota hai, lekin bahut kuch miss kar deta hai. Ye teeno metrics alag-alag sawaal poochte hain — kam se kam ek sahi hai ya nahi, top ke kitne sahi hain, aur kul kitna coverage mila — isliye apne task ke hisaab se chuno, teeno ko ek saath confuse mat karo.

Diversity metric — same cheez baar-baar to nahi?

Generative settings me diversity bhi matter karti hai — similar outputs undesirable hote hain. Example: fashion recommender har din lagbhag identical outfits suggest na kare. Ek common diversity metric hai average pairwise semantic similarity. Outputs ka set O = {o1, …, oN} lo, har output oi ka embedding ei lo, aur compare karne wale index pairs ka set P define karo. Phir har pair (i, j) ke liye cosine similarity cossim(ei, ej) = (ei·ej) / (||ei|| ||ej||) compute karke average nikalo. Lower average similarity ka matlab hai higher diversity.

Kaunse pairs P me include karne hain, ye matter karta hai. Fashion stylist application me shayad sirf aaj ki suggestion (oi) aur pichle hafte ki suggestions (oj, jahan j recent days ko index karta hai) ke beech similarity se matlab ho. Tab P me woh pairs honge jahan j pichle saat outputs tak ho — lagbhag saat comparisons per day, short-term repetition ko target karte hue. Saare pairs par average karne se ye focus dilute ho jayega aur near-duplicate suggestions miss ho jayenge. Implementation simple hai: sklearn ke cosine_similarity se pairwise similarity matrix banao, upper triangle (diagonal exclude karke) ka mean lo — wahi average pairwise similarity hai.

Task-specific metrics kaise chunein?

Har failure mode ka metric uske nature se tay hota hai. Missing SQL constraints: AST comparison (reference-based) ya regex/AST traversal (reference-free). Invalid tool usage: reference trace se tool call sequence match karna, ya static schema check. Incomplete email content: LLM-as-judge check ki generated email me context se saare required fields hain ya nahi, ya regex se mandatory sections check karna. Persona-tone mismatch: judge ki tone label ko human-labeled references se compare karna, ya persona definitions par based binary tone classification. Location ambiguity: disambiguated location entity IDs ko ground truth region codes se compare karna, ya geocoding-based check — mentioned place ko coordinates me map karke verify karna ki woh user-specified region se consistent hai ya nahi. Pattern ye hai: pehle failure ko precisely define karo, phir socho ki use code se check kar sakte ho ya judge chahiye, reference hai ya reference-free rule kaafi hai — aur metric ko usi hisaab se banao.

Yaad rakho: Exact metrics (AST, regex, schema) jahan possible ho wahan use karo — fast aur deterministic hain. Similarity metrics meaning compare karte hain jab wording alag ho. Group metrics (Success@k, Precision@k, Recall@k) multiple candidates ke liye hain, aur diversity ke liye average pairwise similarity dekho. Metric ka chunav hi tay karta hai ki tum kya optimize karoge, isliye use failure mode se jod kar chuno, convenience se nahi.
Average pairwise semantic similarity (cosine) — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 5)
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
import numpy as np

# Example: 5 embeddings, each 384-dim
embeddings = np.random.rand(5, 384)

# Pairwise similarity matrix
sim_matrix = cosine_similarity(embeddings)

# Average of unique pairs (exclude diagonal)
triu_indices = np.triu_indices_from(sim_matrix, k=1)
avg_similarity = sim_matrix[triu_indices].mean()

print(f"Average pairwise similarity: {avg_similarity:.4f}")
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Implementing Automated Evaluators

05.3Chapter 5 · Implementing Automated Evaluators

Judge Calibration aur Statistical Correction

Judge prompt likh lena sirf aadha kaam hai. Asli sawaal ye hai: judge human experts se kitna agree karta hai, aur uske imperfect hone ke bawjood production me agent ki asli success rate kaise estimate karein? Ye section usi calibration ka hai — data splits, TPR/TNR, iterative refinement, aur Rogan-Gladen correction ke saath bootstrap confidence intervals.

Data splits: train, dev, test

LLM-as-judge design karna classifier train karne jaisa hai, farak sirf itna hai ki "training" prompt engineering se hoti hai, parameter tuning se nahi. Gradient descent ke bajay hum manually examples select karte hain aur instructions likhte hain jo model ka behaviour in-context guide karte hain. Judge generalize kare aur overfit na ho, isliye labeled traces (Chapters 3 aur 4 se) ko teen disjoint sets me divide karte hain:

  • Training set: Labeled examples ka pool jinse prompt banate time few-shot demonstrations draw kar sakte ho — typically clear-cut Pass aur Fail cases jo failure mode ki boundaries illustrate karte hain.
  • Development (dev) set: Alag, bada set jisse prompt refine karte ho. Har edit ke baad (instructions badalna, criteria reword karna, few-shot examples swap karna) judge ke outputs ko dev set par human labels se compare karte ho. Dev set ke examples kabhi prompt me nahi aane chahiye — isse measure kar sakte ho ki judge training examples se aage kitna generalize karta hai.
  • Test set: Held-out set jise sirf judge ki alignment compute karne ke liye use karte ho, prompt finalize karne ke baad. Development ke dauran is set ko kabhi dekhte bhi nahi. Ye judge ki real-world accuracy ka unbiased estimate deta hai (jaise true positive rate aur true negative rate), jise baad me production traces me estimated success rates adjust karne ke liye use karte hain.

Splits ke beech examples reuse karna (khaas taur par dev ya test ke examples prompt me dalna) data leakage hai aur accuracy estimates inflate kar deta hai. Traditional supervised learning se alag, yahan bade training sets nahi chahiye — in-context learning typically chhoti sankhya me well-chosen examples ke baad saturate ho jati hai. Isliye zyada data evaluation ko allocate karte hain. Typical split: 10%-20% labeled traces training set ko, aur 40%-45% har ek dev aur test ko. Judge performance reliably estimate karne ke liye dev aur test dono me kaafi Pass aur Fail examples hone chahiye (ideally 30-50 har ek ke). Ye proportions real-world prevalence reflect nahi karte, khaas taur par jab failures rare hon — ye imbalance acceptable hai, aur deliberate hai, jaisa correction wale section me samjhaya gaya hai.

Iterative prompt refinement — TPR aur TNR

Loop aise chalta hai: pehle baseline prompt likho (task description, clear definitions, structured output, training set se few-shot examples). Phir judge ko poore dev set par chalao aur har judgment ko human ground truth se compare karo. Phir agreement measure karo: P ho total dev examples jo Pass label kiye gaye, jinme se p correctly Pass judge kiye gaye; F ho total Fail label wale, jinme se f correctly Fail judge kiye gaye. To TPR (true positive rate) = p / P aur TNR (true negative rate) = f / F. Yahan positive ka matlab Pass hai, negative ka matlab Fail.

TPR aur TNR hi kyun, precision aur recall kyun nahi? Kyunki end goal hai application ki true pass rate estimate karna. Judge us pass rate ko sirf do tareekon se misestimate kar sakta hai: (1) real Passes miss karke, ya (2) real Fails ko pass karke. TPR aur TNR in dono error modes ko seedha capture karte hain. Precision aur recall galat nahi hain, lekin is goal se utne cleanly align nahi karte.

Phir disagreements inspect karo: false passes (judge ne Pass kaha, human ne Fail) aur false fails (judge ne Fail kaha, human ne Pass) dekh kar ambiguous criteria ya missing edge cases pehchano. Phir prompt refine karo — Pass/Fail criteria ki wording clarify karo, training set se zyada illustrative few-shot examples swap karo, aur agar dev set me aise failure modes hain jo training set me nahi hain, to unke representative traces training set me add karo aur agle round me prompt me use karne par consider karo. Phir revised prompt ko same dev set par dobara evaluate karo aur metrics recalculate karo — jab tak performance stabilize na ho ya acceptably improve na ho.

Kab rukna hai, aur agar alignment atak jaye to kya karein?

Rukte hain jab TPR aur TNR satisfactory levels tak pahunch jayein (jaise 90% se upar). Thresholds application ki needs par depend karte hain — real failure miss karna false flag se zyada costly ho sakta hai. DSPy jaise tools is loop ko dev set par prompts optimize karke automate kar sakte hain, lekin pehle manual iteration recommend ki jati hai — isse failure mode aur judge ke behaviour dono ki intuition banti hai. Agar judge phir bhi poorly perform kare (low TPR aur TNR), to teen strategies hain: zyada capable LLM use karo (bada ya naya model subtle ya context-sensitive errors resolve kar sakta hai), criterion ko decompose karo (complex failure mode ko chhote, atomic checks me todo, har ek ka apna judge), ya labeled data improve karo (training set me zyada diverse, high-quality examples add karo, khaas taur par edge cases ke liye).

True success rate estimate karna — Rogan-Gladen correction

Jab dev set par consistent high TPR aur TNR mil jayein, to judge prompt freeze karke test set par chalate hain. Isse do cheezein milti hain: test set par estimated pass rate (judge ne kitne fraction ko Pass label kiya) aur judge ke TPR/TNR ke estimates. Lekin ye sirf test split ke baare me batata hai. Practice me hum ye estimate karna chahte hain ki ek bade (aksar unlabeled) dataset me, jaise production agent ke naye traces me, failure mode kitni baar aata hai. Problem ye hai ki judge imperfect hai — hazaaron naye outputs par use chala kar sirf Pass predictions count karoge to biased estimate milega, kyunki judge kabhi failures miss karta hai aur kabhi passes ko galat flag karta hai.

Correction ka procedure chaar steps me hai. Step 1: held-out test set par judge accuracy measure karo (TPR aur TNR). Step 2: judge ko m naye, unlabeled traces par chalao; k ho jinhe Pass label kiya gaya; raw success rate p_obs = k / m. Step 3: observed rate ko correct karo — Rogan-Gladen formula: theta_hat = (p_obs + TNR - 1) / (TPR + TNR - 1), aur result ko [0, 1] me clip karo. Do edge cases hain: agar TPR + TNR - 1 near zero ho (jaise dono lagbhag 50%), to correction blow up ho jata hai aur judge random chance se behtar nahi hai — is case me correction unreliable hai aur use nahi karna chahiye. Aur numerical noise se theta_hat thoda 0 se neeche ya 1 se upar ja sakta hai — clipping use handle karta hai. Code me denominator ke liye 0.05 ka threshold use hota hai.

TPR/TNR combinations ka effect aisa hota hai: dono high (0.85 se upar) hon to accurate estimate aur tight confidence interval milta hai. TPR high aur TNR low (0.7 se neeche) ho to estimate neeche shift hota hai (false positives observed success count inflate karte hain) aur interval widen hota hai. TPR low aur TNR high ho to estimate upar shift hota hai (false negatives observed failure count inflate karte hain) aur interval widen hota hai. Dono low hon to estimate unreliable hai aur confidence interval bahut wide — conclusions nikalne se pehle judge improve karo.

Bootstrap confidence interval

Corrected estimate ek single test set se aaya hai; agar alag test set draw karte to number thoda alag hota. Is variation ko measure karne ke liye bootstrap use karte hain: existing test set ko baar-baar resample karo (replacement ke saath, matlab same example ek resample me multiple baar aa sakta hai) aur har resampled set par estimate recompute karo. Un estimates ka spread batata hai ki original number par kitna bharosa kar sakte ho. Concretely, har bootstrap iteration me (human label, judge prediction) pairs ka full set resample karo, us par TPR aur TNR recompute karo, correction apply karke naya theta_hat-star nikalo, aur record karo. B iterations ke baad, in theta_hat-star values ke 2.5th aur 97.5th percentiles 95% confidence interval banate hain.

Python code me ye function estimate_success_rate(test_labels, test_preds, unlabeled_preds, B=20000) implement kiya gaya hai — numpy par based, ek chhoti open source library judgy me bhi available hai. Steps: P aur F count karo, TPR/TNR nikalo, p_obs nikalo, denominator 0.05 se kam ho to error raise karo, theta_hat compute karke clip karo, phir B baar bootstrap karo (har baar P_boot ya F_boot zero ho ya denominator 0.05 se kam ho to woh sample skip karo), aur aakhir me samples ke 2.5th aur 97.5th percentile se L aur U nikalo.

Intuition: TPR improve karna sabse zyada fayda deta hai

Ek illustrative thought experiment me fixed 50 successes aur 50 failures wale human-labeled set aur 80% ki ground truth success rate assume ki gayi. Jab judge bahut si real successes miss karta hai, to raw success rate true 80% se bahut neeche start hoti hai aur uncertainty (shaded area) huge hoti hai. Jaise-jaise woh zyada successes catch karna seekhta hai, raw rate 80% ki taraf badhti hai aur interval narrow hota hai, jabki corrected line 80% par fixed rehti hai. Isi tarah, jab judge bahut si real failures ko success classify karta hai, to raw rate true 80% se upar baithti hai; jaise-jaise woh failures reject karna seekhta hai, raw rate wapas 80% par aa jati hai aur interval shrink hota hai.

Teen takeaways: bias correction dono extreme error modes me reliably bias remove karta hai; judge ki errors corrected estimate ko shift karne ke bajay mainly uncertainty badhati hain (wider intervals); aur TPR improve karna confidence interval ko sabse zyada narrow karta hai. Jab TNR = 1 ho, to formula simplify ho kar theta_hat = p_obs / TPR ban jata hai — TPR chhota ho to p_obs ko correspondingly bade factor se "boost" milta hai, aur TPR ke bootstrapped estimate me chhoti absolute variations bhi bade relative changes la sakti hain, jisse wider interval milta hai.

Confidence interval se shipping decision

Maan lo corrected estimate theta_hat = 0.87 hai, 95% confidence interval [0.81, 0.93] ke saath, aur team ne minimum acceptable success rate 0.85 set ki hai. Point estimate (0.87) threshold se upar hai, lekin interval ka lower bound (0.81) neeche hai. Practice me decision galat hone ki cost par depend karta hai. Agar 81% success rate wala feature ship karna serious user harm cause karega, to interval bahut wide hai confidently ship karne ke liye — zyada test data collect karo ya judge improve karke interval tighten karo. Agar feature low-stakes hai aur 81% bhi acceptable hai, to ship karke monitor kar sakte ho. [0.85, 0.89] jaisa narrow interval zyada confidence deta hai, kyunki worst case bhi threshold meet karta hai. Interval ki width, sirf point estimate nahi, tay karti hai ki action lene ke liye kaafi evidence hai ya nahi.

Yaad rakho: Judge ko test set par TPR/TNR se validate karo, phir Rogan-Gladen correction se raw pass rate ko adjust karo, aur bootstrap se 95% confidence interval nikalo. Point estimate akele ship/no-ship decide nahi karta — interval ka lower bound dekho, aur yaad rakho ki TPR improve karna interval ko sabse zyada tighten karta hai.
Bias correction + bootstrap 95% CI (estimate_success_rate) — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 5)
import numpy as np

def estimate_success_rate(
    test_labels,
    test_preds,
    unlabeled_preds,
    B=20000
):
    """
    Args:
      test_labels: array-like of 0/1, human labels on test set
                   (1 = Pass).
      test_preds: array-like of 0/1, judge predictions on test set
                  (1 = Pass).
      unlabeled_preds: array-like of 0/1, judge predictions on
                       unlabeled data (1 = Pass).
      B: number of bootstrap iterations.
Returns:
theta_hat: point estimate of true success rate.
L, U: lower and upper bounds of a 95% bootstrap CI.
"""
test_labels     = np.asarray(test_labels, dtype=int)
test_preds      = np.asarray(test_preds, dtype=int)
unlabeled_preds = np.asarray(unlabeled_preds, dtype=int)

# Step 1: Judge accuracy on test set
P = test_labels.sum()
F = len(test_labels) - P
TPR = ((test_labels == 1) & (test_preds == 1)).sum() / P
TNR = ((test_labels == 0) & (test_preds == 0)).sum() / F

# Step 2: Raw observed success rate
p_obs = unlabeled_preds.sum() / len(unlabeled_preds)

# Step 3: Correct estimate
denom = TPR + TNR - 1
if denom < 0.05:
  raise ValueError("Judge accuracy too low for correction")
theta_hat = (p_obs + TNR - 1) / denom
theta_hat = np.clip(theta_hat, 0, 1)

# Step 4: Bootstrap CI
N = len(test_labels)
idx = np.arange(N)
samples = []
for _ in range(B):
  boot_idx = np.random.choice(idx, size=N, replace=True)
  lbl_boot = test_labels[boot_idx]
  pred_boot = test_preds[boot_idx]
  P_boot = lbl_boot.sum()
  F_boot = N - P_boot
  if P_boot == 0 or F_boot == 0:
      continue
  TPR_star = (
      (lbl_boot == 1) & (pred_boot == 1)
  ).sum() / P_boot
  TNR_star = (
      (lbl_boot == 0) & (pred_boot == 0)
  ).sum() / F_boot
  denom_star = TPR_star + TNR_star - 1 # Rogan-Gladen denominator
  if denom_star < 0.05:
      continue # denominator near zero makes the estimate unreliable
  theta_star = (p_obs + TNR_star - 1) / denom_star
  samples.append(np.clip(theta_star, 0, 1))

if not samples:
  raise RuntimeError(
      "No valid bootstrap samples; check inputs"
  )
    L, U = np.percentile(samples, [2.5, 97.5])
    return theta_hat, L, U
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Implementing Automated Evaluators

05.4Chapter 5 · Implementing Automated Evaluators

Evaluator Pipeline banana

Individual evaluators samajh lena ek baat hai, unhe ek poori pipeline me jodna doosri. Evaluator pipeline woh workflow hai jo har failure mode ke liye metric define karne se le kar production me true success rate estimate karne tak jata hai — aur use maintain bhi karna padta hai, kyunki data drift hota hai, naye failure modes aate hain, aur model updates judge ka behaviour badal dete hain.

Pipeline ke paanch steps

Chapter ke end me diya gaya practical workflow ye hai: pehle, taxonomy ke har failure mode ke liye ek metric define karo jo automatically compute ho sake. Doosra, jahan criterion precise ho wahan code-based checks use karo — SQL AST matching, required fields ke liye regex, schema validation. Teesra, jahan judgment chahiye wahan LLM-as-judge evaluators use karo — tone, completeness, relevance jaise criteria ke liye. Chautha, har judge ko human-labeled ground truth ke against validate karo, held-out test set par TPR/TNR use karke. Paanchva, Rogan-Gladen correction se true success rate estimate karo aur bootstrap confidence intervals se apni uncertainty quantify karo.

Is sequence ka order matter karta hai. Metric define kiye bina evaluator banana matlab bina target ke shoot karna hai. Code checks ko pehle rakhna cost bachata hai — deterministic checks saste hain, judge calls mehnge. Aur validation ke bina judge chalana matlab numbers par bharosa karna jinka koi grounding nahi hai. Pipeline ka har step agle step ki credibility banata hai.

Common pitfalls — pipeline kahan toot-ti hai?

Sabse common galti hai prompt me examples bilkul na dalna. Concrete examples ke bina model ke paas grounding nahi hoti ki is task me failure ka matlab kya hai — task definition clear hone ke bawjood behaviour vague ya inconsistent ho jata hai. Doosri pitfall hai ek hi prompt me bahut kuch karne ki koshish: kuch teams tone, content correctness aur next steps — teeno ko ek hi Pass/Fail decision me evaluate karne ki koshish karti hain. Isse ambiguity aati hai aur errors diagnose karna mushkil ho jata hai. Complex metrics ko narrow, specific metrics aur prompts me todna behtar alignment aur zyada reliable judges deta hai.

Teesri pitfall hai alignment step ko skip kar dena. Teams aksar assume kar leti hain ki LLM-as-judge out of the box "just work" karega. Kabhi-kabhi ye sach hota hai, khaas taur par simple ya broadly familiar metrics jaise sentiment polarity (positive ya negative) ke liye. Lekin bahut se evaluation metrics domain-specific hote hain ya product ki unique "vibe" se tied hote hain — luxury clients ke liye tone alignment, listing summary ki completeness, tool call ka justification. Ye pretrain nahi hote judge me; humein sikhana padta hai. Prompt refinement aur human-labeled validation essential hain taaki evaluators asal me woh reflect karein jo agents me matter karta hai. Judge align karna investment hai jo enormously pay off karta hai — aligned judge hazaaron traces par expensive human evaluation replace kar sakta hai, jisse agent-wide monitoring feasible ho jata hai.

Data leakage se bacho

Ek aur pitfall hai judge prompt aur evaluation set ke beech data leakage. Leakage tab hoti hai jab teams traces ko judge prompt me few-shot examples ke roop me include karti hain aur unhi traces ko evaluation set me bhi use karke alignment measure karti hain. Metrics contaminate ho jate hain: TPR aur TNR high dikh sakte hain, isliye nahi ki judge achha generalize kar raha hai, balki isliye ki usne specific examples pehle dekh liye hain. Prompt me use hua koi bhi trace evaluation set se exclude karna hi hoga. Kai log apni evaluation ko galat describe bhi karte hain — ya to held-out set use hi nahi karte, ya development set par accuracy report karke use judge ki true performance maan lete hain. Isse highly inflated aur misleading success rate estimates milte hain.

Alignment ek baar ka kaam nahi hai

Alignment ke baad bhi bahut si teams process ko revisit karna bhool jati hain. Production data drift kar sakta hai. Naye failure modes emerge ho sakte hain, LLM updates behaviour shift kar sakte hain, aur evaluation metrics evolve ho sakte hain. Recommendation hai alignment process regularly rerun karo (jaise weekly): handful traces label karna continue karo, TPR aur TNR recompute karo, aur check karo ki confidence intervals acceptably tight rehte hain ya nahi. Agar nahi, to judge ko realign karo. Ye one-off task nahi hai — ye LLM-powered applications ki ongoing lifecycle ka hissa hai, MLOps me monitoring ki tarah. Production me naye failure modes dekhne par unke examples teeno splits (training, dev aur test) me add kar sakte ho.

Ek aur subtlety: LLM-as-judge evaluators khud stochastic hote hain. Same judge ko same trace par do baar chalane se alag labels mil sakte hain, khaas taur par higher temperature settings par. Ise check karne ke liye judge ko temperature 0 se upar rakh kar same trace par teen se paanch baar chalao aur dekho ki reasoning vary karte hue final label stable rehta hai ya nahi. Agar label runs ke beech flip ho, to judge us trace ke baare me uncertain hai, aur rubric me criterion ki definition ko zyada detail ya zyada examples se ambiguity remove karne ki zaroorat hai.

Labeled data kaise badhayein?

Ek practical sawaal hai: error analysis ya collaborative rubric design ke initial traces se train, dev aur test splits ke liye chahiye bada dataset kaise mile? Recommendation hai ki ek single, trusted domain expert failure modes define kare, rubric finalize kare, aur robust splits ke liye chahiye full set (jaise 100-200 traces) label kare. Ye sabse efficient path hai, kyunki inter-annotator agreement measure karne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Lekin agar single expert feasible na ho (badi teams, highly subjective criteria), to pehle chhota collaborative set (jaise 20-50) le kar rubric refine karo jab tak agreement high na ho jaye, phir ek person se baaki traces label karwao. Aur labels par bharosa karna zaroori hai — common mistake hai labeling un logon (ya LLMs) ko outsource kar dena jinke paas application ka context hi nahi hai.

Aage kya?

Automated evaluators ko ongoing maintenance chahiye. Production data drift karta hai, failure modes evolve hote hain, aur model updates judge behaviour shift kar sakte hain. Alignment process regularly rerun karo — fresh traces label karke TPR/TNR recompute karo. Agle teen chapters in evaluators ko specific application types par apply karte hain: multi-turn conversations (Chapter 6), retrieval (Chapter 7), aur tool use (Chapter 8). Wahi techniques wahan naye challenges ke saath wapas aayengi — lekin foundation yehi hai: metric define karo, code ya judge se implement karo, human labels se validate karo, aur uncertainty ke saath report karo.

Yaad rakho: Pipeline hai — metric, phir code ya judge, phir TPR/TNR validation, phir corrected estimate aur confidence interval. Aur ye pipeline living hai: weekly realign karo, naye failure modes ke examples teeno splits me add karo, aur judge ki stochasticity check karte raho. Ek baar align karke bhool jana sabse mehenga shortcut hai.
