06Chapter 6 · Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations

Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations

Ab tak humne un interactions ko evaluate karna seekha jahan user ek message bhejta hai aur agent ek response deta hai — single-turn interaction. Lekin bahut si applications multi-turn conversations hain, jahan user aur agent multiple baar back and forth karte hain. Har exchange (ek user message aur agent ka response) ek turn hai, aur shuru se aakhir tak poori conversation ek session hai. Multi-turn me agent ko turns ke across context maintain karna padta hai, instructions ko time ke saath follow karna padta hai, aur conversation develop hote hue coherently respond karna padta hai — aur ye naye evaluation challenges paida karta hai jo single-turn methods cover nahi karte.

Multi-turn me strong models bhi kyun toot-te hain?

Multi-turn wahi jagah hai jahan otherwise strong models fall apart karte hain. Ek study me 200,000 se zyada simulated conversations leading LLMs (commercial aur open source dono) ke against chalayi gayi, chhe alag tasks par — coding, math word problems aur summarization samet. Har task ke liye do setups compare kiye gaye: single-turn setup, jahan user saari information ek saath deta hai, aur multi-turn setup, jahan user wahi information kai messages me drip karke deta hai. Accuracy multi-turn setup me average 39% drop hui. Interesting finding ye thi ki kyun: drop ko do hisson me split kiya gaya — model ki raw ability me chhoti decline (model single-turn me jitna smart tha, lagbhag utna hi smart raha) aur unreliability me bahut bada increase. Unreliability ka matlab hai ki model pehle user message ke baad early guess kar leta hai, us par commit kar deta hai, aur phir jab user baad ke messages me nayi information deta hai to us guess ko revise karne me fail ho jata hai. Ek baar model galat track par aa gaya, to wahi rehta hai. Ye yaad rakhne layak hai: jab hamare apne agents ki multi-turn conversations break down hoti hain, to aksar wajah ye nahi hoti ki underlying model kharab ho gaya — wajah ye hoti hai ki model ne bahut jaldi answer commit kar diya aur wapas aakar use fix hi nahi kiya.

Analyze-Measure-Improve abhi bhi lagu hai

Core evaluation lifecycle, Analyze-Measure-Improve, abhi bhi apply hota hai, aur pichle chapters ke key principles bhi — qualitative error analysis se shuru karo, simple, aksar binary evaluation criteria favour karo. Lekin multi-turn interactions complexity add karte hain — kya measure karte ho aur meaningful evaluation data kaise collect karte ho, dono me. Is chapter me tum seekhoge: session, turn aur coherence levels par evaluate kaise karein, failures ko single-turn problems se alag kab karein, robustness probe karne ke liye perturbation testing kaise use karein, aur turn-level analysis me invest karne se pehle session-level evaluators kaise banayein.

Teen levels: session, turn, coherence

Multi-turn evaluation teen distinct levels par operate karta hai. Ye levels mutually exclusive nahi hain — ye same conversation par alag-alag lenses hain. Practice me ye ek drill-down workflow banate hain: session level se broad shuru karo, phir failures milne par specific turns aur coherence issues me narrow down karo.

Session level: Poori conversation user ke intended goal achieve karti hai ya nahi? Ye assessment aksar binary (pass ya fail) hoti hai aur system effectiveness ka high-level view deti hai. Example: agar ek peer feedback assistant session end kar de bina user se koi useful feedback liye, to poori session ko failure mark kar sakte hain, chahe individual turns well-formed hon — overall task accomplish nahi hua. Session-level evaluation se shuru karne ki recommendation hai: ye broadest performance signal deti hai, least overhead ke saath, aur seedha woh sawaal answer karti hai jo sabse zyada matter karta hai — kya system ne woh kiya jo user ko chahiye tha?

Turn level: Ye diagnostic tool hai, primary evaluation strategy nahi. Use karte hain pinpoint karne ke liye ki session ke andar kahan galat hua, jab session pehle se failure flag ho chuka ho. Failing session ke individual turns se walk through karo aur wahi sawaal poochho jo single-turn evaluation me poochhte — kya ye response relevant hai, correct hai, tone appropriate hai? Goal hai woh specific turn dhoondhna jahan conversation off track gayi, jo batata hai ki kya fix karna hai.

Conversational coherence aur memory: Teesra level un properties par focus karta hai jo sirf multiple turns me emerge hoti hain. Session ke andar check karte hain ki assistant ko yaad hai ya nahi jo user ne pehle kaha tha. Sessions ke across (applications jo state persist karte hain) examine karte hain ki assistant stored summaries ya memory tools ke through knowledge appropriately retain karta hai ya nahi.

Coherence failures — teen causes, teen fixes

Coherence failures, jahan assistant kuch bhool jata hai jo user ne pehle kaha tha, subtle hote hain. Ye aksar kai turns ke baad hi surface karte hain aur standard single-turn evaluations me catch karna mushkil hota hai. Common examples: stated preferences bhool jana (user conversation ke shuru me constraint specify karta hai, assistant baad ke turn me ignore kar deta hai), pehle ke responses se contradict karna (assistant turns ke across conflicting information deta hai), aur task ka track kho dena (multi-step workflow me assistant bhool jata hai ki kaunse steps complete ho chuke hain).

Jab coherence failure mile, to teen alag causes distinguish karna useful hai, kyunki har ek ka fix alag hai. Anchoring failure: model ne early answer commit kar diya aur update karne se mana kar diya, chahe user ne baad ke turns me nayi information di ho — upar wali study me ye multi-turn degradation ka sabse common cause paya gaya. Context truncation: conversation model ki context window se exceed kar gayi, ya application ne tokens bachane ke liye pehle ke turns truncate kar diye, isliye model pehle ka constraint literally dekh hi nahi sakta. Instruction drift: model ne early turns me system prompt faithfully follow kiya lekin conversation lambi hote hue dheere-dheere use follow karna band kar diya; instructions context me abhi bhi hain, lekin un par model ka attention weaken ho gaya.

Fixes bhi alag hain: anchoring failures ke liye prompting strategies help kar sakti hain (jaise "Before answering, reread all user constraints stated so far"); context truncation ke liye architectural changes chahiye (pehle ke turns ki summarization, ya memory system); instruction drift ke liye conversation ke andar key instructions periodically repeat karna model ko track par rakh sakta hai.

Across sessions: memory ko kaise evaluate karein?

Kuch applications ek conversation ke andar hi nahi, sessions ke across bhi state maintain karte hain. Example: personal assistant ko yaad ho ki user morning meetings prefer karta hai, seafood dislike karta hai, ya uski upcoming deadline hai. Memory systems typically facts ko summaries ya key-value (KV) pairs ke roop me store karte hain aur har naye session ki shuruaat me unhe context me inject karte hain. Memory systems implement karna is chapter ka topic nahi hai, lekin unhe evaluate karne ka tareeka chaar sawaalon me toot-ta hai:

  • Storage: Jab user naya fact bataye (jaise "I prefer morning meetings"), to kya system use save karta hai? Test karne ke liye ek session me preference batao aur check karo ki memory store me woh baad me hai ya nahi.
  • Retrieval: Jab naya session shuru ho, to kya system current context ke liye sahi facts retrieve karta hai? Example: user scheduling ke baare me poochhe to system ko morning-meeting preference retrieve karni chahiye, food preferences ke baare me unrelated facts nahi.
  • Update: Jab user stored fact ko contradict kare (jaise "Actually, afternoons work better now"), to kya system purana fact update karta hai ya dono rakh leta hai? Example: user ne chhe mahine pehle kaha tha woh vegetarian hai aur phir kaha usne fish khana shuru kar diya — use abhi bhi vegetarian recommendations nahi milni chahiye.
  • Staleness: Kya system aise facts apply karta hai jo ab relevant nahi hain? User ke address ke baare me stored fact uske move karne ke baad stale ho sakta hai, aur system ke paas purane facts expire ya reconfirm karne ka tareeka hona chahiye.

Har sawaal ke liye targeted test cases likh sakte ho: ek session me fact set karo, doosri session me use modify ya contradict karo, aur teesri session me system ka behaviour check karo. Evaluation structure retrieval evaluation jaisi hai (Chapter 7), jahan check karte ho ki sahi information sahi time par surface hui ya nahi.

Yaad rakho: Multi-turn me 39% accuracy drop ka sabse bada reason model ka kam smart hona nahi hai — early guess par commit karke use revise na karna hai. Isliye session level se shuru karo (goal mila ya nahi?), phir failing sessions me turn level par drill down karo, aur coherence failures me cause pehchano — anchoring, context truncation, ya instruction drift — kyunki har ek ka fix alag hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations
← Previous05.4 · Evaluator Pipeline banana→ Next06.1 · Multi-Turn Eval — session-level pass/fail
06.1Chapter 6 · Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations

Multi-Turn Eval — session-level pass/fail

Session-level Pass/Fail multi-turn evaluation ka starting point hai: ek label per conversation, jo batata hai ki system kitni baar kaam karta hai. Turn-level analysis uske baad aati hai, sirf un sessions ke liye jo fail hue hon. Ye section batata hai ki traces kaise collect karein, failures ko single-turn problems se kaise alag karein, session-level success ko concretely kaise define karein, aur user simulators se test conversations kaise generate karein.

Traces collect karna

Shuruaat karte hain multi-turn traces ka initial dataset collect karke. Ek lightweight chat interface aksar kaafi hota hai. Team members user behaviour simulate karte hain aur har ek 10 se 15 tasks engage karta hai, alag intents aur personas try karte hue. Sirf kuch participants se jaldi 100 ya zyada diverse traces gather ho jate hain. Phir in conversations ko manually review karte hain, successes aur failures dono ke examples collect karte hain, aur basic sawaal poochhte hain jo kisi bhi trace se poochhte — kya assistant ne user ka goal accomplish kiya, kya usne throughout instructions follow ki, aur agar kuch galat hua to kahan galat hua.

Failures ko isolate karna — kya ye asal me multi-turn hai?

Jab multi-turn traces me failures milein, to critical pehla step ye determine karna hai ki failure asal me multi-turn nature ki hai ya nahi. Conversation ke dauran surface hone wali bahut si failures, core me, single-turn problems hoti hain. Ye distinction draw karna significant debugging effort bachata hai. Technique straightforward hai: failing turn lo aur issue ko single-turn prompt se reproduce karne ki koshish karo jisme saara relevant context include ho.

Example: shopping assistant doosre turn me galat information deta hai. User: "Hi, I want to know about returns." Bot: "Sure, what product are you asking about?" User: "The X1000." Bot: "The return window for X1000 is 15 days." (Incorrect; 30 days hona chahiye.) Ise condense karke single prompt banao: "What is the return window for product X1000?" Agar LLM phir bhi "15 days" jawab de, to failure conversational context ki wajah se nahi hai — ye retrieval ya grounding issue hai, aur use Chapters 3 aur 5 ki single-turn techniques se debug kar sakte ho.

Lekin saari failures aise simplify nahi hoti. Kuch inherently conversational setup se tied hoti hain. Example: user movie dhoondh raha hai, bot genre poochhta hai, user kehta hai "I love sci-fi", bot actors poochhta hai, user kehta hai "Not particularly", aur bot recommend karta hai "The Love Llama, a heartwarming romantic comedy" — sci-fi constraint bilkul bhool kar. Yahan assistant ne "sci-fi" constraint clearly bhool diya. Ise single-turn problem ke roop me reproduce karne ka koi tareeka nahi hai, kyunki failure precisely turns ke across context maintain karne ke baare me hai. Ise systematically study karne ke liye trace ko failing turn se pehle truncate karke LLM ko multiple baar sample kar sakte hain, ye observe karne ke liye ki woh user ki stated preference kitni baar retain karta hai versus drop karta hai. Real conversations se prefixes extract karke ya synthetically generate karke in "N-1 turn" prompts ka dataset bana sakte hain, taaki short-term memory aur consistency ko scale par test kar saken.

Session-level success ko operationalize karna

Session-level Pass/Fail ko concrete definition chahiye, aur sahi definition application par depend karti hai. Customer support bot ke liye success ka matlab ho sakta hai "user ka issue resolve ho gaya aur user ne 48 hours ke andar dobara support contact nahi kiya." Coding assistant ke liye success ho sakta hai "generated code pehli attempt me saare tests pass karta hai." Peer feedback assistant ke liye success ho sakta hai "session ne kam se kam do specific, actionable feedback points produce kiye." Jo bhi definition chuno, use rubric ke roop me likh lo aur Chapter 4 ke collaborative annotation process se validate karo. Agar team agree nahi kar pa rahi ki session pass hui ya nahi, to definition ko zyada detail chahiye.

User simulators se test conversations generate karna

Multi-turn conversations manually simulate karna slow hai, isliye bahut si teams LLM ko user simulator bana kar conversation ka user side automatically generate karti hain. Simplest setup aise kaam karta hai: doosre LLM ke liye system prompt likho jo user persona aur goal describe kare, phir loop chalao jahan simulator LLM user message generate karta hai, tumhara agent respond karta hai, aur simulator agla user message generate karta hai — fixed number of turns tak, ya jab tak simulator decide na kare ki goal meet ho gaya. Example simulator system prompt: "You are playing the role of a first-time home buyer. Your goal: find a 3-bedroom house under $500k near downtown. You are impatient and tend to change your mind. On each turn, respond as this user would. If the assistant has fully addressed your request, respond with [DONE]."

Persona (budget, location, personality, domain knowledge ka level) aur goal (simple lookup, multi-step request, complaint, ambiguous question) vary karke bahut si alag conversations generate kar sakte ho. Diverse behaviour ke liye har run me user ki communication style vary karo: kuch personas terse hone chahiye, kuch verbose, kuch confrontational, aur kuch ko conversation ke beech me apna mind change karna chahiye. Zyada sophisticated approaches persona generation ko bhi automate karte hain — ek pipeline me ek LLM persona-goal pairs generate karta hai, doosra LLM us persona ke saath user role play karta hai, aur teesra LLM resulting conversation evaluate karta hai, jisse manual prompt writing ke bina hazaaron diverse multi-turn interactions produce hoti hain. Ek popular leaderboard dusra approach leta hai: real human conversations ko scale par collect karke use karta hai calibrate karne ke liye ki realistic user behaviour kaisa dikhta hai, jo tumhare synthetic personas design karne me inform karta hai.

Simulators ki ek important limitation hai: LLM-generated user behaviour real user behaviour se zyada consistent aur cooperative hota hai. Real users typos karte hain, bot ke sawaalon ko ignore karte hain, abruptly topics change karte hain, aur frustration aise express karte hain jo simulate karna mushkil hai. Simulators aise conversations bhi produce karte hain jo real sessions se chhoti aur zyada goal-directed hoti hain, matlab woh long-tail failures miss kar sakte hain jo sirf extended, meandering interactions me dikhte hain. Simulators ko initial coverage banane ke liye use karo, lekin jab real user traces available hon to hamesha unke against validate karo.

Conversation length ke hisaab se stratify karna

Failures aksar conversation length se correlate karte hain — agent chhoti conversations me achha kaam karta hai, lekin jaise context accumulate hota hai (jaise 8 ya 10 turns ke baad) kaam karna band kar deta hai. Test set banate time alag-alag lengths ki conversations include karo, buckets me stratify karo (jaise 2 se 4 turns, 5 se 9 turns, 10 ya zyada turns), aur har bucket ke liye success rates alag se report karo. Agar success rates kisi specific length par sharply drop hon, to woh batata hai ki debugging kahan focus karni hai, aur issue context truncation hai, instruction drift hai, ya kuch aur.

Yaad rakho: Har multi-turn failure multi-turn nahi hoti — pehle failing turn ko single-turn prompt me condense karke dekho. Agar failure reproduce ho jaye, to woh retrieval ya grounding issue hai. Agar na ho (jaise sci-fi preference bhool jana), to woh genuinely multi-turn hai, aur use N-1 turn prompts aur length-stratified test sets se study karo.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations
← Previous06 · Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations→ Next06.2 · Transition Failure Heatmap
06.2Chapter 6 · Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations

Transition Failure Heatmap

Passing conversations ko test karna kaafi nahi hai — ye bhi jaanna zaroori hai ki woh kitni aasani se toot-ti hain, aur toot-ti hain to kahan. Perturbation testing passing traces me chhote, deliberate changes karke robustness probe karta hai, brittleness score batata hai ki agent kitna fragile hai, aur transition failure heatmap batata hai ki failure kis state se kis state me jaate hue aati hai. Ye section in teeno ko jod kar multi-turn evaluation ka practical end-to-end workflow deta hai.

Perturbation testing — passing conversation ko tod kar dekho

Jab hamare paas multi-turn traces ka set ho jo pass karte hain (agent unhe correctly handle karta hai), to hum agent ki robustness test kar sakte hain un traces me chhote, deliberate changes karke aur check karke ki agent abhi bhi handle karta hai ya nahi. Ye perturbation testing hai: passing conversation lo, ek cheez modify karo, aur dekho ki agent break hota hai ya nahi. Try karne layak modifications:

  • Conversation ke beech me user ka goal change karna: Sci-fi wale example se shuru karke, user ke sci-fi maangne ke baad insert karo, "Actually, my partner hates sci-fi. Can we do a thriller instead?" Agar agent phir bhi sci-fi recommend kare, to woh apni understanding update karne me fail hua hai.
  • Ambiguity add karna: Clear user message ko vague ya underspecified rephrase karo, aur dekho ki agent clarification maangta hai ya galat guess karta hai.
  • Agent ko contradict karna: Agar agent kuch suggest kare, to user se "no, that's wrong" kehlao aur check karo ki agent course correct karta hai ya double down karta hai.

Perturbation testing useful hai kyunki ye known-good conversations se failing traces generate karta hai, production failures ka wait kiye bina. Ye khaas taur par brittleness catch karne me achha hai: agent jo apne test set ki exact conversations par kaam karta hai, lekin thoda sa change hote hi fail ho jata hai. Philosophically ye ML literature ki adversarial robustness testing jaisa hai, lekin farak hai: adversarial testing worst-case inputs se system todne ki koshish karta hai, jabki perturbation testing passing conversations par naturalistic variations (woh changes jo real users asal me karte hain) apply karta hai. Dono valuable hain, lekin perturbation testing se shuru karna aasan hai kyunki perturbations realistic user behaviour se aate hain, adversarial optimization se nahi.

Brittleness score

Time ke saath track karne layak ek useful metric hai brittleness score: har passing trace ke liye count karo ki agent ko fail karne ke liye kitne perturbations lage, phir traces ke across median report karo. Median brittleness score 1 wala agent (ek chhota change use tod deta hai) score 5 wale agent se bahut zyada fragile hai. Releases ke across brittleness score track karke dekh sakte ho ki agent zyada robust ho raha hai ya kam.

Transition failure heatmap — failure kahan se kahan jaati hai?

Individual failures count karna batata hai ki kya toota, lekin ye nahi batata ki failure kis transition par aayi. Transition failure heatmap iska jawab deta hai: rows represent karti hain "From State" (aakhri successfully completed state) aur columns represent karti hain "In State" (woh state jiske dauran pehli failure hui). Har cell count karta hai kitne traces me failure column wali state me hui, row wali state successfully complete hone ke turant baad. Multi-turn conversations par apply karo to states turns ya stages hote hain — jaise user request parse karna, tool arguments generate karna, tool execute karna, tool output handle karna — aur heatmap dikhata hai ki kaunsi transition sabse zyada fail hoti hai.

Isi idea ka poora worked example Chapter 8 me hai, jahan simplified real estate assistant ke liye chaar states define ki gayi hain — ParseReq (user request parse karna), GenArgs (tool arguments generate karna), ExecTool (tool call execute karna) aur HandleOut (tool output handle karna). Sabse frequent transition jo first failure ki taraf le jati hai, woh hai ExecTool me enter karna, GenArgs complete karne ke turant baad — 12 instances. Ye batata hai ki LLM aise arguments generate kar raha hai jo schema validation pass karte hain lekin execution time par tool ko fail kar dete hain — shayad LLM aise property IDs reference kar raha hai jo exist hi nahi karte, ya aise SQL queries construct kar raha hai jinka syntax database support nahi karta. Column totals sum karke overall sabse zyada failing state pehchante hain: ExecTool ka column total sabse zyada (12), phir GenArgs (8) aur HandleOut (7). GenArgs ka 8 do alag "from" states se aata hai — 3 failures ParseReq se aur 5 HandleOut se — jo batata hai ki argument generation alag contexts me struggle karta hai.

"From State" track karna sirf column totals count karne se behtar kyun hai? Column sums overall sabse error-prone state identify karte hain, lekin ye misleading ho sakta hai. ExecTool jaisi state LLM-generated arguments ke baad frequently fail ho sakti hai, lekin simpler inputs ke baad (jaise jab user query directly specify kare) reliably succeed kar sakti hai. "From State" track karne se finer-grained analysis milti hai jo specific transitions ya contexts pinpoint karti hai jo failure ki taraf le jate hain. Aur yaad rakho: transition pinpoint karna investigation shuru karne ki jagah batata hai, lekin automatically ye imply nahi karta ki preceding state hi sole cause hai. Root issue preceding state me ho sakta hai, ya failing state ke andar khud — example ke liye, database aisa SQL dialect use kar raha ho jiska agent ke prompt me zikr hi nahi tha. Hotspot investigate karte time un specific traces ko isolate karo (jaise woh 12 traces), ExecTool state me kya galat hua analyze karo, aur preceding GenArgs state ke diye context ko critically examine karo. Fixes ke saath heatmap evolve honi chahiye — counts kam hone chahiye, heatmap sparser honi chahiye, aur aakhir me sirf residual errors ya inherently difficult transitions bachne chahiye.

Multi-turn traces ka automated evaluation

Jab manual review se clear failure types identify kar lo, to Chapter 5 ki techniques se automated evaluators bana sakte ho — LLM-as-judge models, programmatic filters, ya dono ka hybrid. Key sawaal hai kis level par evaluate karein. Zyada tar systems ke liye session-level evaluators se shuru karne ki recommendation hai. Session-level LLM-as-judge ko poori conversation milti hai aur woh Pass/Fail verdict deta hai ki user ka goal meet hua ya nahi. Ye sabse pehle banane layak highest-leverage evaluator hai, kyunki ye seedha woh measure karta hai jo matter karta hai.

Turn-level evaluators specific, well-defined failure modes ke liye useful hain. Examples: ek programmatic check jo verify kare ki assistant kabhi us information ko contradict na kare jo usne previous turn me di thi; ek LLM-as-judge jo evaluate kare ki conversation me har tool call preceding user message se justified thi ya nahi; ek coherence check jo user-stated constraints extract kare aur verify kare ki assistant ki final recommendation me woh respected hain ya nahi. Har evaluator ko har turn assess karne ki zaroorat nahi hai — bahut se systems ke liye turn-level analysis sirf tab chahiye jab specific paths debug kar rahe hon. Session-level evaluation broad performance signal deti hai, kam overhead ke saath.

Common pitfalls

Multi-turn evaluation me kuch specific pitfalls hain. Pehla: failures jo conversation length se correlate karte hain — bahut se systems pehle do-teen turns me achha behave karte hain, phir degrade ho jate hain. Woh context bhool sakte hain, instructions ignore kar sakte hain, ya pehle ke responses contradict kar sakte hain. Test sets me alag-alag lengths ki conversations include karni chahiye taaki ye position-dependent failures detect hon. Sirf chhoti conversations test karoge to real users ko lambi sessions me milne wali problems miss kar doge.

Doosra: turn-level evaluation me overinvest karna — har turn ke liye evaluator banana tempting hai, lekin ye jaldi expensive aur noisy ho jata hai. Zyada tar signal session-level evaluation se aata hai. Granular analysis focused debugging ke liye reserve karo: pehle failing sessions identify karo, phir handful representative traces me drill down karke root causes dhoondho.

Teesra: multi-turn failures ko single-turn failures se confuse karna — jaise returns wale example me, conversation ke dauran dikhne wali bahut si failures asal me single-turn problems hoti hain. Multi-turn-specific evaluators banane se pehle hamesha failure ko isolate karne ki koshish karo. Isse un problems ke liye overengineering avoid hoti hai jinke simpler fixes hain.

Putting it together — workflow

Multi-turn conversations evaluate karne ka workflow: pehle, session-level success ko concretely define karo (rubric ke roop me likho). Doosra, traces collect karo — production logs se, manual simulation se, ya user simulators se. Teesra, conversation length ke hisaab se stratify karo aur har bucket ke liye success rates alag se report karo. Chautha, failing sessions ke liye diagnose karo ki failure anchoring hai, context truncation hai, ya instruction drift. Paanchva, har failure ko isolate karo taaki pata chale ki woh truly multi-turn hai ya single-turn problem hai. Chhatha, perturbation testing se passing conversations ki robustness check karo aur brittleness score track karo. Saatva, session-level automated evaluators pehle banao; turn-level evaluators sirf specific, well-defined failure modes ke liye add karo. Agle chapter me ek specific architecture ki baari hai jo apne challenges le kar aati hai: RAG.

Yaad rakho: Pehle session-level Pass/Fail banao — woh sabse zyada signal, sabse kam overhead deta hai. Phir perturbation testing se robustness check karo (brittleness score = fail karne ke liye kitne changes lage, median). Aur jab failures milein, to transition heatmap se dekho ki failure kis state se kis state me jaate hue aayi — hotspot wahi hai jahan fix sabse zyada fayda dega.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Evaluating Multi-Turn Conversations
← Previous06.1 · Multi-Turn Eval — session-level pass/fail→ Next07 · Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
07Chapter 7 · Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Pichle chapters ki evaluation techniques broadly saare LLM applications par apply hoti hain. Ye chapter focus narrow karta hai ek architecture par — RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — jahan retrieval stage apne evaluation questions le kar aata hai. RAG me sirf final answer ki correctness measure karna kaafi nahi hai: pipeline ka har stage (query construction, retrieval, reranking, generation) independently failure modes introduce kar sakta hai, aur stages ke across failures interdependent bhi hote hain.

RAG pipeline kya hai?

Basic RAG pipeline query ke basis par knowledge base (document corpus, structured table, ya web) se context retrieve karta hai, aur use LLM ko generation ke liye feed karta hai. Traditional search se farak ye hai ki is context ka consumer LLM khud hai, jo kai passages simultaneously process kar sakta hai. Isse retrieval objective shift hota hai: high recall critical ho jata hai taaki saare potentially relevant content include ho. Lekin jitne zyada documents retrieve karo, utna behtar nahi hai — LLMs ki limited context windows hoti hain, irrelevant text performance degrade kar sakta hai, aur LLM APIs per token charge karti hain, isliye excess tokens cost badhate hain. Coverage aur quality balance karne ke liye bahut se RAG systems two-stage retrieval approach use karte hain (broadly retrieve karo, phir rerank karo). Zyada recent systems agentic RAG tak jaate hain, jahan model khud apne retrieval queries likhta hai, results examine karta hai, aur initial results insufficient hon to query reformulate karta hai. Agentic RAG me model har step par decide karta hai ki kab aur kya retrieve karna hai, fixed retrieve-then-generate pipeline follow karne ke bajay.

Is chapter me two-stage pattern par focus hai, kyunki evaluation principles same hain: phir bhi measure karna hai ki sahi documents retrieve hue ya nahi aur generated output unke faithful hai ya nahi. Agentic RAG evaluation questions add karta hai — jaise model ne sahi time par retrieve karne ka decision liya ya nahi, aur kya usne achhi query likhi — jo Chapter 8 me cover hote hain.

Retrieval me kya badla hai?

2023 ke baad se retrieval me kai developments ne cheezein reshape ki hain. Hybrid retrieval, keyword search (BM25) ko dense embeddings ke saath RRF (reciprocal rank fusion) se combine karke, bahut se production systems me default ban gaya hai kyunki ye exact-match aur semantic-similarity dono cases cover karta hai. Late-interaction models jaise ColBERT fast embedding-based retrieval (jahan queries aur documents independently encode hote hain) aur expensive reranking (jahan model har query-document pair ko saath score karta hai, jo zyada accurate lekin slower hai) ke beech middle ground offer karte hain. Long-context models (128k+ tokens) ne ye sawaal bhi uthaya hai ki kuch use cases me RAG abhi bhi zaroori hai ya nahi; practice me RAG useful rehta hai kyunki ye attribution deta hai, cost reduce karta hai, aur context ko relevant information par focused rakhta hai.

Two-stage retrieval

Stage 1: first-pass retrieval. Pehla stage poore corpus ko scan karke broad set of candidates return karta hai. Yahan fast, lightweight methods use kar sakte hain jo millions of documents par cheaply chalti hain. Common choices hain embedding-based search approximate nearest neighbor indexes ke saath (jaise FAISS, HNSW, ya hosted vector stores jaise Pinecone ya Weaviate, embeddings models jaise text-embedding-3 ya embed-v3 ke upar), ya sparse retrieval methods jaise BM25 inverted index par. Is stage ka goal hai high recall, precision ki cost par bhi — ye ensure karna ki sahi document candidate set me kahin ho, chahe woh abhi top par na ho.

Stage 2: reranking. Doosra stage Stage 1 ke broad candidate set ko zyada carefully reorder karta hai, sabse relevant ko top par la kar. Reranker, intuitively, ek zyada careful "reader" hai. Jahan Stage 1 ne query ki single embedding ko har document ki single embedding se compare kiya tha, reranker query aur candidate document ko saath dekh kar relevance score produce karta hai jo dono ko account me leta hai. Pair ko jointly consider karne ki wajah se woh nuances catch kar sakta hai jo one-shot embedding similarity miss kar de, lekin per call zyada expensive bhi hai — isiliye use sirf chhote candidate set par chalate hain, poore corpus par nahi. Reranker ke do common implementations hain: cross-encoder models (jaise Cohere Rerank, BGE reranker, ya fine-tuned MiniLM cross-encoder), jo specifically (query, document) pairs score karne ke liye train kiye jate hain, aur LLM-as-reranker setups, jahan general LLM ko retrieved documents ke saath prompt karke nayi ordering ya per-document scores return karne ko kehte hain. Is stage par coverage ke bajay precision aur ranking quality prioritize karte hain.

Pehle retrieval ko alag se evaluate karo

Generated answers ki quality assess karne se pehle verify karo ki system consistently sahi context dhoondh raha hai. Agar retriever relevant documents surface hi nahi kar raha, to generation side par kitni bhi prompt engineering ya model tuning kar lo, output fix nahi hoga. Is chapter me do hisson par focus hai: Analyze aur Measure. Analyze karo ki failures retrieval me aati hain, generation me, ya dono ke interaction me. Measure karo retrieval quality Recall@k, MRR aur NDCG@k jaise metrics se, aur generation evaluate karo faithfulness aur relevance jaise context-sensitive metrics se. Pehle retrieval ke liye evaluation datasets construct karte hain, phir diagnostic metrics aur pipeline ke across failures attribute karne ke methods introduce karte hain.

Yaad rakho: RAG me failure kisi bhi stage par ho sakti hai — aur stages interdependent hain: galat retrieval ka matlab hai generator ke paas sahi answer banane ka koi tareeka nahi. Isliye pehle retrieval ko alag se measure karo (kya sahi documents mile?), phir generation ko (kya answer un documents ke faithful hai?). End-to-end correctness score akele ye kabhi nahi batayega ki dosh kiska hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation
← Previous06.2 · Transition Failure Heatmap→ Next07.1 · RAG Eval — retrieval aur faithfulness
07.1Chapter 7 · Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation

RAG Eval — retrieval aur faithfulness

Retrieval evaluate karne ke liye queries aur unke corresponding relevant document chunks ka dataset chahiye. Manual curation sabse reliable hai lekin expensive hai, isliye synthetic generation se scale karte hain — lekin synthetic questions aksar bahut easy hote hain, isliye unhe harder banana aur filter karna bhi padta hai. Phir retrieval quality ko Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR aur NDCG@k se measure karte hain, aur chunking ko tunable variable ki tarah treat karte hain.

Synthetic query-answer pairs generate karna

Retrieval evaluate karne ke liye queries ka dataset chahiye jisme har query ke saath woh specific document chunks hon jinme correct answers hain. Sabse reliable option hai realistic questions manually curate karna aur har ek ko exact chunk(s) se map karna jinme answer aata hai. Ye high-quality supervision deta hai, lekin aksar expensive aur time-consuming hota hai. Dataset ko aasani se scale karne ke liye LLM se synthetic question-answer-context triples generate kar sakte hain. Documents ko chunks me split karte hain (wahi units jinhe retriever index karta hai, jo retrieval "targets" hain). Har chunk ke liye LLM ek salient fact extract karta hai aur ek question likhta hai jiska jawab woh fact deta hai. Chunk, fact aur question mil kar (question, answer, context) triple banate hain jahan correct retrieval target construction se hi known hota hai.

Prompt kuch aisa hota hai: chunk of text diya jaye, usse ek specific, self-contained fact extract karo, phir ek question likho jo seedha aur unambiguously sirf us fact se answer ho. Output JSON format me return karo, "fact" aur "question" keys ke saath.

Harder synthetic queries — distractors ke saath

Basic synthetic generation approach aise questions produce karta hai jo retriever ke liye easy hote hain, kyunki har question ek hi chunk se bana hota hai aur us chunk ki exact wording use karta hai. Keyword par match karne wala retriever zyada tar sahi chunk dhoondh lega. Production me user queries messy hoti hain — woh alag phrasing use karte hain, aise topics reference karte hain jo multiple documents me aate hain, aur kabhi-kabhi chunks ke across comparisons maangte hain. Retriever ko stress-test karne ke liye synthetic questions generate kar sakte hain jo deliberately multiple chunks ke content jaisi lagti hain lekin sirf ek chunk se correctly answer hoti hain:

  1. Target chunk select karo: Corpus se chunk A chuno jisme clear, fact-based answer ho.
  2. Similar chunks identify karo: Embedding model ya keyword search use karke chunks B, C, etc. dhoondho jo A se similar hon lekin answer contain na karte hon.
  3. Discriminative question generate karo: LLM se aisa question likhwao jo sirf Chunk A se answer ho, lekin B ya C ki terminology ya themes reuse karta ho.

Example: financial news corpus par retrieval system. Step 1, target chunk A: "In April 2020, the company reported a 17% drop in quarterly revenue, its largest decline since 2008." Step 2, similar chunk B: "The company experienced significant losses in 2008 during the financial crisis but rebounded by the end of 2009." Ye chunk same company, same year (2008) aur "financial crisis" phrase mention karta hai, isliye keyword-based retriever use highly score karega. Step 3, generated question: "When did the company experience its largest revenue decline since the 2008 financial crisis?" Sirf Chunk A iska jawab deta hai, lekin Chunk B me overlapping language use ek plausible distractor banati hai jise retriever ko distinguish karna padta hai.

Synthetic questions ko filter karna

Synthetic questions kabhi-kabhi unrealistic ya off-domain ho sakte hain. Unhe filter kar sakte hain, isi tarah jaise Chapter 3 me unrealistic synthetic queries filter karte hain. Subset ko manually review karo aur har question ko realism aur relevance ke liye rate karo, phir un labeled examples ko few-shot prompt me doosre LLM ko de kar baaki ko score karwao. Sirf woh rakho jo realistic mane jayein. Example filtering prompt real estate information retrieval system ke liye: realistic queries ke examples (jaise "What are the property taxes for 123 Main St?" — Rating 5, typical, concise, property-specific; "Show me 3-bedroom houses in the North Berkeley area with a backyard." — Rating 5, natural filter-based query) aur unrealistic queries ke examples (jaise chimney ki teesri brick ke colour ke baare me poochhna — Rating 1, overly specific aur unnatural; ek zip code ke saare houses ka square footage add karna — Rating 2, odd aggregation, real search behaviour represent nahi karta). Phir generated question ko 1 se 5 scale par realism ke liye rate karne ko kaho, brief explanation ke saath.

Note karo ki yahan 1-5 rating sirf filtering ke liye hai: goal hai queries ko realism aur domain relevance ke hisaab se roughly rank karna taaki sabse kamzor discard kar saken, failure rates measure karna nahi. Chapter 4 me evaluation ke liye binary labels recommend kiye gaye the kyunki woh higher inter-annotator agreement dete hain; yahan 1-5 scale appropriate hai kyunki hum synthetic data ko quality ke liye filter kar rahe hain, system outputs evaluate nahi kar rahe. Ye task retrieval pipeline test karna shuru karne ke liye "good enough" dataset banane me support karta hai.

Precision@k aur Recall@k

Queries aur unke corresponding relevant document chunks ka dataset milne ke baad, retriever ko standard ranking metrics se evaluate kar sakte hain. Metric ka chunav is par depend karta hai ki downstream application ke liye kya matter karta hai. Precision@k aur Recall@k sabse basic retrieval metrics hain. Ye query ke response me retrieve kiye gaye top k documents ki quality evaluate karte hain. k ki value query par depend karke vary kar sakti hai. Factoid question jaise "What is the property tax for 123 Main St?" ke liye k = 1 ya 2 kaafi ho sakta hai, jabki synthesis question jaise "Summarize recent market trends for 3-bedroom houses downtown" ke liye k = 5 se 10 chahiye ho sakta hai.

Precision@k measure karta hai top k retrieved documents me se kitna fraction actually relevant hai: (top k results me relevant documents ki sankhya) / k. Recall@k measure karta hai query ke saare relevant documents me se kitna fraction top k results me aata hai: (top k results me relevant documents ki sankhya) / (query ke liye total relevant documents ki sankhya). Dono metrics relevance ko binary treat karte hain: document relevant hai ya nahi. Agar evaluation dataset graded relevance scores use karta hai (jaise 0 se 3), to pehle threshold apply karke binarize karte hain (jaise score 1 se upar ko relevant mano).

Practice me RAG ke first stage ke liye precision se zyada recall ki parwah karte hain. Agar relevant information retrieved set se bilkul missing hai (low recall), to generator ke paas correct answer produce karne ka koi tareeka nahi hai. Relevant content ke saath kuch irrelevant content include karna, relevant content miss karne se kam harmful hai — halanki, jaisa MRR wale section me discuss hai, context me position bhi matter karti hai ("lost in the middle" effect). Early retrieval stages me relevant content include karna ensure karna, noise exclude karne se kahin zyada important hai.

Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) aur hit rate

MRR measure karta hai ki pehla relevant document ranking me kitni jaldi aata hai. Single query ke liye reciprocal rank hai 1 / rank, jahan rank pehle relevant document ki position hai. Agar top k results me koi relevant document nahi aata, to reciprocal rank 0 hai. MRR hai evaluation set ki saari queries Q par average: MRR@k = (1 / |Q|) * sum (1 / rank_q), jahan rank_q query q ke liye pehle relevant document ki position hai (ya infinity, jisse 0 milta hai, agar top k me koi relevant document nahi aata). Ek simpler alternative hai hit rate@k (kuch contexts me Success@k bhi kehte hain): queries ka woh fraction jinme kam se kam ek relevant document top k results me aata hai. Hit rate aksar retrieval ke liye sabse practical starting metric hai, kyunki bahut si applications me ek relevant document correct answer produce karne ke liye kaafi hota hai.

MRR khaas taur par useful hai jab query ka jawab dene ke liye sirf ek key fact chahiye hota hai. LLM multiple retrieved chunks process kar sakta hai, phir bhi correct chunk ko pehle rank karna noise reduce kar sakta hai aur reasoning simplify kar sakta hai. Reason hai ki LLMs apne context par uniformly attend nahi karte. Ek experiment me answer 20 retrieved documents ke beech chhupaya gaya aur accuracy ko answer ki position ke function ke roop me measure kiya gaya. U-shaped curve mili: accuracy sabse zyada thi jab answer position 1 ya position 20 par tha, aur 30 percentage points se zyada drop hui jab answer position 10 (beech) me tha. Ise "lost in the middle" effect kaha gaya. RAG ke liye implication ye hai ki relevant document retrieval order me kahan land karta hai, ye utna hi matter karta hai jitna ki woh retrieve hua ya nahi — isiliye MRR (top position reward karna) tab bhi useful hai jab hamare paas multiple relevant chunks hon. Multi-hop questions ke liye — matlab woh questions jinka jawab do ya zyada retrieved chunks se facts combine karke milta hai (jaise "Which of our West Berkeley listings has the highest property tax?" ke liye West Berkeley listings ki list aur har ek ki tax information, dono chahiye) — Recall@k ya NDCG@k, MRR se zyada informative hai.

NDCG@k — graded relevance

Precision, Recall aur MRR, teeno relevance ko binary treat karte hain. Lekin practice me kuch documents doosron se zyada useful hote hain. Query "Summarize market trends for luxury condos downtown" ke liye recent market analysis report highly relevant hai, general city economic overview somewhat relevant hai, aur restaurant guide irrelevant hai. Graded relevance in distinctions ko capture karti hai — har document ko scale par score de kar, jaise 0 (irrelevant), 1 (marginally relevant), 2 (relevant), ya 3 (highly relevant). NDCG@k isi setting ke liye design kiya gaya hai. Ye sawaal ka jawab deta hai: hamari ranking sabse relevant documents ko pehle rakhne me kitni achhi hai?

Metric do intuitions par bana hai: zyada relevant documents ko score me zyada contribute karna chahiye (relevance 3 wala document relevance 1 wale se zyada matter karta hai), aur position matter karti hai — pehle behtar hai (rank 1 par highly relevant document, rank 5 par same document se zyada valuable hai, kyunki users aur LLMs pehle aane wali cheez par zyada focus karte hain). Formula: top k documents me se har ek ke liye uska relevance score lo aur use log2(i + 1) se divide karo, jahan i uski position hai. Logarithmic discount ka matlab hai pehli kuch positions bahut matter karti hain, baad ki positions ka contribution kam hota jata hai: rank 1 divide hota hai log2(2) = 1 se (koi discount nahi), rank 2 divide hota hai log2(3) ≈ 1.58 se, rank 4 divide hota hai log2(5) ≈ 2.32 se. Rank 1 par document apna poora relevance score contribute karta hai, rank 2 par lagbhag 63%, aur rank 9 par sirf lagbhag 30%.

DCG akele interpret karna mushkil hai kyunki uski value is par depend karti hai ki kitne relevant documents hain aur kitne relevant hain. Normalize karne ke liye Ideal DCG (IDCG@k) compute karte hain: wahi retrieved documents lo, unhe best possible order me re-sort karo (highest relevance pehle), aur us ideal ranking par DCG compute karo. NDCG@k phir ratio hai: DCG@k / IDCG@k. Score 1.0 ka matlab hai system ne documents ko perfectly rank kiya. Score 0.5 ka matlab hai usne better ordering se mil sakne wali value ka lagbhag aadha capture kiya. Ye normalization scores ko queries ke across comparable banati hai, chahe alag queries me relevant documents ki sankhya alag ho.

NDCG@k RAG ke liye kyun matter karta hai? Do reasons: saare chunks equally useful nahi hote — NDCG@k un systems ko reward karta hai jo market report ko pehle rank karte hain; aur context windows finite hote hain — agar retrieved documents ka total size LLM ki context limit se exceed kare, to sirf pehle kuch hi use honge, isliye NDCG@k ensure karta hai ki sabse relevant documents prioritized hon. Ek caveat: NDCG@k counterintuitive scores produce kar sakta hai. Sirf marginally relevant documents retrieve karke unhe perfect order me rank karne wala system high score kar sakta hai, jabki highly relevant document retrieve karke use neeche rank karne wala system worse score kar sakta hai. Hamesha NDCG@k ko recall ke saath interpret karo taaki poori picture mile. Aur jab doubt ho ki kaunsi retrieval metric se shuru karein, to first retrieval stage ke liye Recall@k aur reranking stage ke liye NDCG@k use karo — Recall se check karo ki sahi documents candidate set me aaye ya nahi, NDCG se check karo ki woh top par aaye ya nahi.

Chunking strategies evaluate aur optimize karna

Retriever relevant content search kar sake, usse pehle documents ko chhote pieces me divide karte hain jinhe chunks kehte hain. Chunk text ki woh unit hai jo retriever return kar sakta hai. Agar chunk bahut chhota ho, to ek relevant idea do chunks me split ho sakta hai aur retriever sirf ek aadha dhoondh paye. Agar chunk bahut bada ho, to usme mostly irrelevant text ho sakta hai jo useful content ko dilute karta hai aur LLM ki context window me tokens waste karta hai.

Sabse simple approach hai fixed-size chunking: har document ko fixed number of tokens ke consecutive segments me split karo (jaise 256 tokens har ek). Chunk boundaries par sentences ya ideas aadhe cut na hon, isliye overlap add kar sakte ho, jahan consecutive chunks kuch tokens share karte hain. Example: chunk size 256 aur overlap 128 ke saath, pehla chunk tokens 1-256 cover karta hai, doosra tokens 129-384 cover karta hai, aur aise aage. Overlap ensure karta hai ki boundary ke paas wala content kam se kam do chunks me aaye, jisse retriever ko use dhoondhne ka behtar chance mile.

Sahi chunk size aur overlap documents ki structure aur users ke questions ki kisam par depend karte hain. Koi single best setting nahi hai, isliye alag combinations try karke measure karte hain ki kaunsi best retrieval results deti hai. Practical approach hai grid search: chunk size aur overlap ke liye kuch candidate values pick karo, har combination ke liye document corpus reindex karo, aur evaluation dataset par retrieval metrics measure karo. Ek hypothetical example me: 128 tokens, 0 overlap — Recall@5 0.82, NDCG@5 0.69; 128 tokens, 64 overlap — 0.88 aur 0.75; 256 tokens, 0 overlap — 0.86 aur 0.74; 256 tokens, 128 overlap — 0.89 aur 0.77 (best); 512 tokens, 0 overlap — 0.80 aur 0.72; 512 tokens, 256 overlap — 0.83 aur 0.74. Is example me 256 tokens 50% overlap (128 tokens) ke saath best retrieval performance deta hai. Notice karo ki overlap add karna saare chunk sizes me consistently results improve karta hai, kyunki ye relevant content ke chunk boundaries par split hone ke chance reduce karta hai. Aur ye bhi notice karo ki bahut bade chunks (512 tokens) medium-sized (256 tokens) se actually worse perform karte hain, likely kyunki unme relevant passages ke saath bahut zyada irrelevant content hota hai. Table ki specific values illustrative hain — practice me best configuration tumhare documents aur queries par depend karta hai. Key takeaway ye hai ki chunking ek tunable parameter hai jo retrieval quality ko significantly affect kar sakta hai, aur systematic search bada farak la sakta hai.

Fixed-size chunking simplest strategy hai aur reasonable starting point hai, lekin ye kai options me se ek hai. Sahi approach documents ki structure par depend karta hai, aur common hai kai try karke unhe retrieval metrics se compare karna. Semantic ya structural chunking: fixed token count par split karne ke bajay document me natural boundaries par split karo, jaise section headings, paragraph breaks, ya topic shifts. Isse semantically related content same chunk me rehta hai. Example: agar report me "Market Trends" aur "Pricing" sections hain, to structural chunking strategy har section ko apne chunk me dalti hai, chahe kitne bhi tokens hon. Chunks size me vary karenge, lekin har ek single coherent topic ke baare me hoga. Contextual augmentation: Har chunk ko embed karne se pehle surrounding context se enrich kar sakte ho. Example: "Table 2" wale chunk ke aage document ka title aur section headings prepend kar do. Isse chunk zyada self-contained ban jata hai aur retriever ko stronger signals milte hain ki usme kya hai.

Yaad rakho: Retrieval ke liye Recall@k (coverage) aur NDCG@k (ranking) dono dekho — Recall batata hai sahi documents mile ya nahi, MRR aur NDCG batate hain woh top par aaye ya nahi (lost in the middle effect ki wajah se position bhi matter karti hai). Synthetic questions ko harder aur filtered banao, warna Recall@k artificially achha dikhega. Aur chunking ko variable samjho: grid search se chunk size aur overlap tune karo, kyunki wahi retriever alag chunking par bahut alag perform kar sakta hai.
Synthetic QA-pair generation prompt — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 7)
You are a helpful assistant generating synthetic QA pairs for
retrieval
evaluation.

Given a chunk of text, extract a specific, self-contained fact from
it.
Then write a question that is directly and unambiguously answered by
that
fact alone. Return your output in the following JSON format:

{
    "fact": "...",
    "question": "..."
}

Chunk:
"{text_chunk}"
Synthetic-question filtering prompt (realism rating 1–5) — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 7)
You are an AI assistant helping us curate a high-quality dataset of
questions for evaluating a real estate information retrieval system.

Here are examples of realistic and unrealistic user queries we have
manually rated:

Realistic Queries (Good Examples):
- "What are the property taxes for 123 Main St?"
  Rating: 5 — Typical, concise, property-specific.

- "Show me 3-bedroom houses in the North Berkeley area with a
backyard."
  Rating: 5 — Natural filter-based query.

Unrealistic Queries (Bad Examples):
- "Tell me about the color of the third brick from the left on the
  chimney of the house that was sold yesterday."
  Rating: 1 — Overly specific and unnatural.

- "If I combine the square footage of all houses listed in zip code
  94704, what is the total?"
  Rating: 2 — Odd aggregation, not representative of real search
behavior.

Your Task:
Rate the following generated question for realism on a scale of 1 to
5.
Provide a brief explanation.

Generated Question: "{question_to_evaluate}"

Output Format:
Explanation: [your brief explanation]
Rating: [your 1-5 rating]

07.2Chapter 7 · Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Groundedness aur Citation Quality

Retrieval perfect ho, phir bhi generation step fail ho sakta hai. Is section me generation quality ke do dimensions hain — faithfulness (kya output retrieved context ko accurately reflect karta hai?) aur relevance (kya answer user ke sawaal ka jawab deta hai?) — aur ek debugging technique, context swapping, jo batati hai ki LLM retrieved evidence use kar raha hai ya apni parametric knowledge par bharosa kar raha hai.

Faithfulness — kya answer retrieved context se grounded hai?

RAG applications me expect karte hain ki answer retrieved me grounded ho, LLM ki apni knowledge me nahi. Chahe LLM pretraining data se sahi answer "janta" ho (ise parametric knowledge kehte hain — information jo model ke weights me baked hai), hum chahte hain ki woh apna response diye gaye evidence par base kare. Faithfulness failures teen forms me aate hain:

  • Hallucinations: Output me aisi information hai jo retrieved documents me nahi hai.
  • Omissions: Output retrieved documents me maujood relevant information ko ignore karta hai.
  • Misinterpretations: Output retrieved documents ki information ko distort karta hai ya inaccurately represent karta hai.

Faithfulness ke liye LLM-as-judge achha kaam karta hai: judge ko retrieved context aur generated answer dono milte hain, phir woh check karta hai ki answer ka har claim context se supported hai ya nahi. Ye Chapter 5 ki techniques se banaya jata hai — clear criterion, Pass/Fail definitions, few-shot examples, structured output.

Relevance — kya answer sawaal ka jawab deta hai?

Doosra dimension hai relevance: kya answer woh address karta hai jo user ne asal me poochha? Answer perfectly faithful ho sakta hai context ke liye, phir bhi point miss kar sakta hai. Example: user poochhe "What are the HOA fees for this property?" aur retrieved context me HOA fees aur tax information, dono hon — to taxes discuss karne wala response faithful hai lekin relevant nahi hai. Relevance ke liye simpler checks kabhi-kabhi kaafi hote hain. Programmatic evaluator verify kar sakta hai ki answer query se specific entity ya topic mention karta hai, halanki open-ended queries ke liye LLM-as-judge usually chahiye hota hai.

Context swapping — grounding debug karne ki technique

Faithfulness issues debug karne ki ek useful technique hai context swapping. Retrieved documents ko kisi alag topic ke unrelated documents se replace karo, phir same query ko pipeline se chalao. Agar answer lagbhag same rehta hai, to LLM retrieved context ko ignore kar raha hai aur apni parametric knowledge par bharosa kar raha hai. Ye grounding problem hai, aur ye subtle ho sakti hai kyunki answer phir bhi coincidentally correct ho sakta hai. Risk ye hai ki jab LLM ko answer pehle se nahi pata hoga, to woh retrieved evidence use karne ke bajay hallucinate karega. Context swapping scale par chalane wala metric nahi hai, lekin ye samajhne ke liye valuable debugging tool hai ki pipeline asal me apne retrieval results use kar rahi hai ya nahi. Agar context-swap test dikhaye ki LLM retrieved documents ignore kar raha hai, to fix usually prompt me hota hai, retriever me nahi. "Base your answer only on the provided documents" ya "If the documents do not contain the answer, say so" jaisi explicit instruction add karna aksar grounding problems resolve kar deta hai.

Citation quality — claim ka source dikh raha hai ya nahi?

Groundedness ka practical side hai citation quality: answer ke claims ko retrieved sources se trace kiya ja sakta hai ya nahi? RAG isiliye valuable hai kyunki ye attribution deta hai — user dekh sakta hai ki answer kahan se aaya. Isliye generation evaluate karte time sirf ye mat dekho ki answer sahi lagta hai ya nahi; ye bhi dekho ki har claim retrieved context ke kis chunk se supported hai, koi claim bina support ke to nahi hai, aur answer ne relevant chunks ko ignore to nahi kiya. Faithfulness judge isi ko check karta hai — har claim ko evidence se jodna. Agar answer me claims hain jo kisi retrieved chunk se trace nahi hote, to woh grounded nahi hai, chahe woh factually sahi kyun na ho — kyunki RAG ka poora purpose ye hai ki answer evidence par based ho, model ki yaadon par nahi.

Common pitfalls

RAG pipelines evaluate karte time kai pitfalls recur karte hain. Sirf end-to-end metrics par rely karna: Single correctness score ye nahi batata ki retrieval doshi hai ya generation. Failures isolate karne ke liye har component ko independently measure karo — retrieval ke liye Recall@k, generation ke liye faithfulness. Synthetic evaluation data par overfit karna: Synthetic data bootstrapping ke liye useful hai, lekin woh aksar real user queries ki ambiguity aur diversity capture karne me fail karta hai. Kai generated questions bahut easy hote hain ya source documents ki specific wording se bahut tightly coupled hote hain. Isse bura, designated "gold" chunk unique ya optimal bhi nahi ho sakta. Logs se real queries ya human-curated examples par regularly validate karo. Synthetic data filter karna help karta hai, lekin real-world test sets ko fully substitute nahi karta. Synthetic queries extractive answers ki taraf skew karte hain aur multi-hop ya judgment-based questions miss karte hain. Warning yaad rakho: synthetic QA pairs aksar source chunk ki exact vocabulary mirror karte hain, jisse retrieval artificially easy ho jata hai. Agar Recall@k synthetic data par great dikhe lekin users ko phir bhi kharab answers mil rahe hon, to conclusions nikalne se pehle logs se 20 se 30 real user queries supplement karo.

Galat metric chunna: Agar LLM ko single fact chahiye, to MRR kaafi ho sakta hai. Agar use multiple chunks synthesize karne hain, to Recall@k ya NDCG@k behtar fit hai. Galat metric chunne se hum aise behaviours optimize karte hain jo output quality ko asal me improve nahi karte. Chunking ko variable ki tarah ignore karna: Bahut chhote chunks relevant information scatter kar dete hain. Bahut bade chunks irrelevant noise contain karte hain. Recall@k jaise retrieval metrics chunking ke basis par significantly vary kar sakte hain, chahe retriever model same ho. Grounding check kiye bina generation evaluate karna: Fluency aur reference answer se overlap kaafi nahi hain. Aisa response jo sahi lagta ho lekin retrieved evidence ko contradict karta ho, RAG ka poora purpose undermine karta hai. Context-sensitive metrics chahiye jo verify karein ki generation retrieved cheez se align hai ya nahi. Retrieval correctness ko answer correctness se alag na karna: Ek common aur valuable diagnostic hai check karna ki retrieval succeed hui lekin answer phir bhi galat tha, ya retrieval fail hui lekin answer coincidentally sahi tha. In dono cases ko alag karna batata hai ki bottleneck retrieval me hai ya generation me, jo tay karta hai ki improvement effort kahan invest karna hai.

Putting it together — RAG eval workflow

RAG pipelines evaluate karne ka workflow: pehle, queries ka dataset banao jinme labeled gold chunks hon (woh documents jo har query ke liye retrieve hone chahiye). Doosra, retrieval quality measure karo — coverage ke liye hit rate@k ya Recall@k, aur ranking quality ke liye MRR ya NDCG@k. Teesra, generation ko alag se evaluate karo — faithfulness (kya answer retrieved content se follow karta hai?) aur relevance (kya woh user ke question ko address karta hai?) ke liye. Chautha, failures diagnose karo — retrieval errors ko generation errors se alag karke: kya system ne sahi documents retrieve kiye lekin galat answer produce kiya, ya galat documents retrieve kiye? Paanchva, chunking strategy ko variable treat karo: alag chunk sizes, overlap aur structural boundaries ke saath experiment karo, aur measure karo ki woh retrieval metrics ko kaise affect karte hain. Agle chapter me zyada flexible architectures ki baari hai, jahan LLMs loops me operate karte hain, intermediate reasoning steps construct karte hain, ya tool calls dynamically issue karte hain. Ye agentic systems evaluation ke liye naye challenges le kar aate hain, khaas taur par attribution, planning accuracy aur tool use correctness ke aas-paas.

Yaad rakho: Faithful hone ka matlab hai har claim retrieved evidence se supported ho — hallucination, omission aur misinterpretation, teeno faithfulness failures hain. Context swapping se check karo ki LLM evidence use kar raha hai ya apni yaadon par bharosa kar raha hai. Aur hamesha retrieval errors ko generation errors se alag karo — warna pata hi nahi chalega ki fix retriever me karna hai ya generator me.

08Chapter 8 · Evaluating Tool Use and Complex Agents

Evaluating Tool Use and Complex Agents

Ab tak humne is baare me zyada carefully nahi socha ki hamare agents ko kitni autonomy hai, ya woh kitne tools use karte hain. Pichle chapters ki techniques (error analysis, automated evaluators, CI/CD) apply hoti hain chahe agent 1 LLM call kare ya 20. Lekin jaise agents zyada complex hote jate hain — external functions call karna, multi-step loops chalana, aage kya karna hai ye decide karna — evaluation mushkil hoti jati hai. Errors steps ke across cascade karte hain, aur jab final output me kuch galat ho, to ye batana mushkil ho jata hai ki kis step ne problem cause ki.

Tools kya hain aur LLMs unhe kyun use karte hain?

Apne aap me LLMs sirf text generate kar sakte hain. Woh database me property listing nahi dekh sakte, calendar par time slot available hai ya nahi ye check nahi kar sakte, ya client ko email nahi bhej sakte. Inme se kuch bhi karne ke liye LLM ko external functions tak access chahiye. Tool koi bhi aisa function hai jise LLM invoke kar sakta hai. Tools define karte hain LLM ko function names ki list, har function kya karta hai iski descriptions, aur parameter schemas de kar jo describe karte hain ki har function kaunse arguments expect karta hai. Jab LLM decide karta hai ki use tool chahiye, to woh structured call generate karta hai (typically JSON format me) jisme specify hota hai kaunsa tool invoke karna hai aur kaunse arguments pass karne hain. System phir woh call execute karta hai, result LLM ko wapas deta hai, aur LLM result ko apne response me incorporate karta hai.

Concrete example ke liye wahi real estate assistant lo. Uske paas kai tools hain: query_listings property database search karta hai filters ke saath, send_email clients ko messages draft aur send karta hai, aur check_calendar available showing times lookup karta hai. Jab user kehta hai "Find 3-bedroom houses under $600k and email the top two to my client", to LLM ko multiple steps karne padte hain. Pehle, woh query_listings call karta hai sahi filters ke saath (bedrooms, price cap, shayad location). Phir results padhta hai, top two matches select karta hai, aur send_email call karta hai sahi recipient aur content ke saath. Inme se har step independently fail ho sakta hai.

Tool calling cycle

LLM ko user request milti hai, woh decide karta hai kaunsa tool call karna hai, uske liye arguments generate karta hai, tool execute hone ka wait karta hai, result process karta hai, aur phir ya to user ko respond karta hai ya doosra tool call karne ke liye loop back karta hai. Ye loop final answer produce karne se pehle multiple baar repeat ho sakta hai.

Tools apne potential impact se bhi differ karte hain. Read-only tools jaise query_listings galat results return kar sakte hain (jaise listings jo user ki price range se match nahi karti), lekin outside world me kuch change nahi hota. User kharab data dekhta hai, aur hum query fix kar sakte hain. Write tools alag hain. Agar send_email galat listing details ke saath email client ko bhej de, ya update_listing galat number se price overwrite kar de, to woh actions undo nahi ho sakte. Tool calls evaluate karte time write tools par zyada carefully dhyaan dete hain, isi liye.

Spectrum of agency — kitni autonomy deni hai?

Agentic system evaluate karne se pehle define karna padta hai ki use kitni autonomy honi chahiye. Wahi real estate assistant lo. User kehta hai: "Find 3-bedroom houses under $600k and email the top two to my client." Is assistant ka high-agency version listings search karega, top two pick karega, email draft karega aur bhej dega — bina confirmation maange. Low-agency version listings search karega, results user ko dikhayega, aur poochhega "Should I send these two to your client?" — kuch bhi irreversible karne se pehle.

Na hi behaviour inherently galat hai. Sahi jawab is par depend karta hai ki humne system ko kya karne ke liye design kiya tha. Agar humne high-agency assistant banaya aur woh baar-baar permission maangta rahe, to woh failure hai. Agar humne low-agency assistant banaya aur woh bina confirmation ke emails bhej de, to woh bhi failure hai. Ye spectrum of agency hai, aur evaluation shuru karne se pehle define karne wali pehli cheezon me se ek hai. Bahut se developers is step ko skip kar dete hain. Result ye hota hai ki system aise behave karta hai jo galat lagta hai, lekin clear nahi hota ki issue bug hai ya product specification me gap hai.

Agency level define karne ke baad, agent ki decision making evaluate kar sakte hain. Error analysis ke dauran poochhte hain: kya agent ne har step par reasonable decisions liye? Kya uske actions ka sequence user ke goal ki taraf le gaya? Kya usne sahi level ki initiative ya caution dikhayi? Kya woh loops me phas gaya ya prematurely give up kar diya? Ek pitfall hai final outcomes par over-rely karna. End-to-end success matter karta hai, lekin agent jo sahi answer unreliable path se paaye, woh thode alag inputs par fail hoga. Intermediate steps ko bhi evaluate karte hain.

Yaad rakho: Evaluate karne se pehle agency level define karo — high-agency assistant ka permission maangna bhi failure hai, aur low-agency assistant ka bina confirmation ke email bhej dena bhi. Aur write tools ko read tools se zyada carefully evaluate karo, kyunki bheja hua galat email wapas nahi liya ja sakta, jabki galat query result sirf fix karna hota hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Evaluating Tool Use and Complex Agents
