11.1Chapter 11 · Data Analysis for Traces

Trace Data ka Analysis — patterns dhoondhna

EDA se patterns surface hote hain — par patterns conclusions nahi hote. Is section me outliers flag karne ke rules, aur ek candidate pattern ko confirmed failure mode me badalne ka lightweight protocol hai.

Outliers flag karne ke do rules

  • Interquartile range (IQR): Q1 aur Q3 metric ke 25th aur 75th percentiles hon, aur IQR = Q3 − Q1. Flag karo koi bhi trace jo Q1 − 1.5 × IQR se neeche ya Q3 + 1.5 × IQR se upar ho. Ye rule skew ke against robust hai — trace metrics me aam taur par skew hota hai (kuch bahut slow ya bahut chatty sessions mean ko kheench lete hain, par quartiles ko nahi).
  • Percentile cut: top 1% aur bottom 1% ko flag karo. Ye rule simpler hai aur tumhe padhne ke liye fixed sankhya me traces milti hain.

Outliers ko sirf numbers se judge mat karo — flagged traces ko padho. Ek bahut lamba session loop me phansa agent bhi ho sakta hai, ya ek genuinely complex user request bhi.

Clusters se confirmed hypotheses tak

Clustering aur distribution analysis patterns surface karte hain, par patterns conclusions nahi hote. "Location ambiguity" involve karne wale traces ka ek cluster actually kai unrelated failure modes contain kar sakta hai jo coincidentally similar-looking outputs produce karte hain. Kisi pattern par action lene se pehle use lightweight protocol se confirm karo:

  1. Candidate cluster se 20 traces carefully padho.
  2. Jo observe kiya uske basis par ek testable criterion define karo (jaise "agent neighborhood name ko city name samajh leta hai").
  3. Check karo ki criterion cluster ke 70% se 80% traces par hold karta hai ya nahi. Agar karta hai, to pattern real hai aur tumhari taxonomy me failure mode ban sakta hai. Agar nahi karta, to cluster bahut heterogeneous hai — use split karo ya dobara examine karo.

Jab traces se features extract karne ke liye LLM use kar rahe ho (jaise "har trace se failure type extract karo") taaki un features par clustering kar sako, to pehle extraction quality ko ek chhote manually labeled set par validate karo. Agar validation set par LLM ki extraction accuracy 90% se neeche hai, to un features par bane clusters unreliable honge — to jin features ki matter hai unke liye rule-based feature extraction ya manual labeling par wapas jao.

Confounders ko control karo

Pattern investigate karte waqt ek aur galti hai — confounders ko control kiye bina seedha conclusion par jump karna. Example: agar notice karo ki paanch se zyada tool calls wale traces ki failure rate zyada hai, to wajah tool calls ki sankhya khud nahi bhi ho sakti; ho sakta hai complex queries ko zyada tool calls chahiye hote hain aur wo inherently answer karne me mushkil bhi hoti hain. Conclusion nikaalne se pehle likely confounders se stratify karo (jaise query complexity, user segment, time of day) aur dekho ki pattern har stratum ke andar hold karta hai ya nahi.

Ek poora analysis loop — example

Suppose thumbs-down rate session length se break down karne par dikhta hai ki lambi sessions zyada fail hoti hain. Hypothesis: lambi sessions me agent context bhool jata hai. Ab lambi, thumbs-down sessions ka slice filter karo aur 20 traces back-to-back padho. Agar unme se 15 me agent ne pehle turns me di gayi constraint (jaise budget) ko baad me ignore kiya hai, to criterion banta hai — "agent 5+ turns ke baad pehle di gayi constraint bhool jata hai" — aur ye 70–80% threshold cross karta hai, to ye confirmed failure mode hai. Ab is failure mode ke liye evaluator banao, golden dataset me examples add karo, aur fix (jaise constraints ko har turn summarize karke context me rakhna) ko CI se verify karo.

Yaad rakho: cluster labels ko ground truth mat samjho. Clustering traces ko similarity se group karta hai, par cluster boundaries arbitrary hoti hain, aur tum cluster ko jo labels dete ho wo hypotheses hain jab tak tum unhe traces padh kar confirm na karo. "Tone mismatch" label wala cluster actually wo traces contain kar sakta hai jahan asli issue missing information hai, tone nahi.

11.2Chapter 11 · Data Analysis for Traces

Embeddings se Failure Clusters

Error analysis aksar ek failure mode ke sirf ek-do kharab examples surface karta hai — par hume poori population chahiye: ye kitna common hai, aur kya ye ek user segment ko zyada hit karta hai? Semantic search iska usual jawab hai. Aur AI coding assistants is chapter ke mechanics ko accelerate karte hain — bas unhe analysis karne mat do.

Semantic search — ek failure mode ki poori population dhoondhna

Do query patterns jin par hum rely karte hain:

  • Problematic trace se seed karo: ek aisi trace pick karo jo failure exhibit karti ho (jaise clustering example wala apologetic email) aur embedding se uske nearest neighbors search karo. Ranked list of candidates milti hai — unhe padho.
  • Natural-language description se query karo: likho ki kya dhoondh rahe ho ("email jo koi homes list karne se pehle apology se shuru hota hai") aur us string ko embed karo. Ye useful hai jab pattern ki description hai par canonical example nahi hai.

Semantic search ki ek badi caveat hai: embedding similarity humari similarity ki notion jaisi nahi hoti. Agar failure mode ke liye tumhare paas labeled traces ka chhota set hai, to un labels ke against apni semantic search ki precision aur recall check karo — agar bahut saare irrelevant traces aa rahe hain (low precision) ya bahut saare relevant miss ho rahe hain (low recall), to similarity threshold adjust karo ya alag embedding model try karo. Do traces embedding space me paas ho sakte hain kyunki wo topic words share karte hain (dono "tour scheduling" mention karte hain), chahe jis failure ki hum parwah karte hain wo narrow ho (dono me agent ne showing double-book kar di).

Ek useful workaround: LLM agent se har trace se application-specific features extract karwao (jaise agent ne tour book kiya? conflicting time mention kiya? hedge kiya?) aur raw trace ki jagah un features ko — ya ek chhote summary ko — embed karo. Agent khud features propose kar sakta hai agar use failure mode ke handful examples de do. Feature embeddings se hum apni similarity ki notion ke kareeb pahunchte hain.

AI coding assistants se kaam fast karna

Is chapter ka kaam (traces load karna, distributions plot karna, clustering karna, semantic search chalana) zyada tar wo code hai jo hum scratch se likhna nahi chahte. AI coding assistants (jaise Claude Code, Codex, aur notebook-embedded agents) mechanics ko considerably accelerate karte hain. Typical setup: traces ki file (JSON ya JSONL), application aur har field ka matlab batane wala chhota description, aur jahan relevant ho application code khud — sab ek working directory me daal do, aur us directory ki taraf point karke coding assistant ka session kholo. Context me ye sab aane ke baad hum wahi cheezein maangte hain jo warna khud script karte — distributions ke plots (jaise turns per session ka histogram log y-axis ke saath, phir user segment se split), failure mode ke handful examples se drafted classifier rubric ya regex, paste kiye gaye cluster of traces ka summary, ya traces me pattern ki direct search ("wo traces dhoondho jahan agent ne koi listings dene se pehle apologize kiya").

EDA ke shuru me ek saath bahut saare charts maangna useful hota hai, aur phir sirf wo padhna jo interesting lage — zyada tar uninformative honge, aur ye expected hai. Example: thumbs-down rate ko session length, user segment, agent version, time of day aur tool call count se ek saath break down karwao, aur phir sirf us breakdown ke peeche wale traces padho jahan kuch off dikhe. Phir jab kisi specific pattern ko dhoondh rahe ho, to AI agent se traces ko directly search karwana semantic search ka lightweight alternative hai. Practical constraint hai agent ka context window: agar traces token budget me fit hote hain (kuch hazaar chhote traces aam taur par fit hote hain), to direct search se embedding-index setup skip kar sakte ho. Dataset context window se bada ho jaye (tens of thousands traces, ya lambi traces), to embedding search ya proper index par wapas jana padta hai.

Sabse bada pitfall: AI agent se ye mat poochho ki traces kyun fail ho rahe hain. Agent jo examples dekhe hain unse ek plausible-sounding explanation produce kar dega — par wo explanation galat bhi ho sakti hai, aur pata lagana mushkil hoga kyunki wo confident sound karegi. Har causal claim ko hypothesis samjho, conclusion nahi. Verify karne ke liye ek variable change karo (jaise prompt modify karo, tool swap karo, ya parameter adjust karo) aur results ko golden set ke against pehle aur baad me compare karo. Agar hypothesis sahi hai, to relevant failure mode ki failure rate girni chahiye. Agar nahi girti, to explanation galat thi — chahe kitni convincing lagi ho. AI agent se sirf find, summarize, search ya plot karwao — ye tumhare analysis me help karne wali activities hain, analysis karne wali nahi.

Common pitfalls — data analysis ke

  • Cluster labels ko ground truth samajhna: clustering similarity se group karta hai, boundaries arbitrary hoti hain, labels hypotheses hain jab tak traces padh kar confirm na karo.
  • Confounders ko control kiye bina conclude karna: pattern ko likely confounders (query complexity, user segment, time of day) se stratify karke check karo ki wo har stratum me hold karta hai ya nahi.
  • AI agent ki explanation ko conclusion samajhna: har causal claim ko controlled change se verify karo — ek variable badlo, golden set par pehle-baad compare karo.
  • Sirf unusual cases dekhna: agar tum sirf clusters, outliers aur semantic search results se traces dekhte ho, to system ki view unusual cases ki taraf skewed ho jati hai. Har analysis session me ek random sample include karo taaki overall performance ka sense calibrated rahe.
Putting it together: error analysis traces ko closely padh kar failure modes ki taxonomy deta hai. Data analysis aggregate techniques add karta hai — poore trace set par failures ko ek saath dekhne ke liye. EDA aur clustering se failure modes ke baare me hypotheses surface karte hain, per-trace metrics (distributions, correlations, outliers) se wo patterns spot karte hain jo ek-ek trace padhne me miss ho jayein, aur semantic search se ek known failure mode ko uski poori population tak expand karte hain. AI coding assistants in sabke mechanics ko accelerate karte hain, par unke outputs ko underlying traces ke against check karne wale hypotheses samjho, analysis khud nahi.

12Chapter 12 · Improving LLM Agents

Improving LLM Agents

Humne evaluators banaye, CI setup kiya taaki regressions pakde jayein, aur monitoring deploy ki taaki production quality track ho. Error analysis (Chapter 3) aur data analysis (Chapter 11) se failure modes surface kiye. Ab in sab ka use karke agent ko actually behtar banate hain — accuracy bhi aur cost bhi.

Do fronts — accuracy aur cost

Is chapter me do tarah ke improvements hain: accuracy optimization — prompt refinement, structural changes, aur heavier interventions jaise fine-tuning; aur cost optimization — model selection, token reduction, caching aur model cascades. Dono ke liye reliable measurement zaroori hai: evaluators (Chapter 5) aur monitoring (Chapter 9) ke bina hum bata hi nahi sakte ki koi change help karta hai ya hurt karta hai.

Accuracy techniques effort ke hisaab se organize ki ja sakti hain — low, medium aur high:

  • Low effort — prompt refinement: instructions clarify karna, few-shot examples add karna, explicit personas se model ko steer karna. Fast try karna, CI ke golden test sets se validate karna aasan.
  • Medium effort — agent kaise kaam karta hai, use badalna: task ko chhote steps me todna, RAG retrieval tune karna, tool descriptions fix karna, self-consistency ya verification calls add karna.
  • High effort — model-level changes: fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA, DPO/KTO), automated prompt optimization frameworks. Inke liye high-quality labeled data chahiye hota hai aur serving infrastructure bhi.

Cost side par bhi wahi approach hai jo accuracy me tha: sabse bade cost drivers dhoondho, targeted changes karo, aur evaluators se verify karo ki quality intact hai.

Lifecycle recap — Analyze-Measure-Improve

Ye book Chapter 1 ke Analyze-Measure-Improve lifecycle ko follow karti hai. Humne traces padh kar failure modes identify kiye (Chapter 3), evaluators banaye jo un failures ko scale par quantify karte hain (Chapter 5), un evaluators ko CI me integrate kiya taaki regressions users tak pahunchne se pehle pakde jayein (Chapter 9), aur is chapter me un pehle phases ke evidence ka use karke concrete improvements karte hain — accuracy me bhi aur cost me bhi.

Yaad rakho: har improvement failure distribution ko badal sakta hai. Ek prompt change jo ek class of errors fix karta hai, doosri introduce kar sakta hai. Ek cost optimization jo queries ko saste model par route karta hai, accuracy ko subtle tareekon se degrade kar sakta hai. Isliye loop chalate raho: naye behavior ko analyze karo, impact measure karo, aur dobara improve karo.

12.1Chapter 12 · Improving LLM Agents

Improvement Strategies — prompt, retrieval, finetuning

Jab agent evaluations me fail karta hai ya users ko frustrate karta hai, to accuracy aam taur par pehle fix karne wali cheez hoti hai. Techniques ko effort level se organize karo — sabse saste se shuru karo, aur bhaari interventions tabhi lao jab saste kaam na karein.

Low effort: prompt refinement

Specification errors pehle fix karo. Bahut se failures Gulf of Specification se aate hain: prompt clearly nahi kehta ki hume kya chahiye, to model ek reasonable guess karta hai jo galat nikalta hai. Ye sabse saste failures hain — sirf prompt edit karna hai, model ki generalisation ability improve nahi karni. Example: real estate assistant me user kehta hai "Find me homes near downtown" — model houses, condos aur townhomes ka mix return karta hai, jabki user ko sirf single-family houses chahiye the. Ye specification error hai: prompt kehta hai "Search for listings matching the user's preferences" par kabhi define nahi karta ki "homes" ka matlab kya hai. Fix hai ek clarification add karna: "When the user says 'homes,' default to single-family houses unless they specify otherwise (e.g., 'condos,' 'townhomes')." Specification errors ko evaluator banane se pehle fix karna chahte hain — kyunki koi matlab nahi hai ye measure karne ka ki model aise task par generalize karta hai ya nahi jo humne clearly define hi nahi kiya hai.

Tip: koi evaluator likhne se pehle apne 10 worst traces skim karo aur poochho — "kya prompt ne actually wahi kaha tha jo mujhe chahiye tha?" Humare experience me early failures me se aadhe specification errors hote hain jo ek-line prompt edit se gayab ho jate hain — aur isse evaluator development ke hafton bach jate hain, ek aisi problem par jo kabhi model limitation thi hi nahi.
  • Kuch examples add karo: do-teen representative input/output pairs seedha prompt me include karo. Ye examples error analysis (Chapter 3) ke dauraan observe kiye gaye failure cases ko target karne chahiye — par ye CI me use hone wale test cases se distinct hone chahiye. CI test cases ko few-shot examples ki tarah reuse karne se evaluation scores inflate ho jate hain bina agent ka behavior naye inputs par actually improve hue. Agar achhe examples ki library hai, to dynamically select bhi kar sakte ho — hamesha same fixed examples include karne ki jagah, current query se sabse similar examples retrieve karo (embedding similarity se) aur unhe few-shot examples ki tarah include karo.
  • Role-based guidance use karo: model ko persona dena (jaise "You are a careful tax advisor") tone aur reasoning style guide karne me help karta hai, khaas taur par open-ended tasks me.
  • Step-by-step reasoning maango: logic ya multiple steps wale tasks ke liye model se explicitly apni reasoning explain karne ko kahna correctness aur completeness improve kar sakta hai — ise chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting kehte hain. Par dhyaan rakho: naye reasoning models (jaise OpenAI ke o-series, DeepSeek R1) internally chains of thought generate karte hain, to explicit "think step by step" instructions unke apne reasoning process me interfere karke performance hurt kar sakti hain. Reasoning models ke liye thinking budget parameter adjust karna behtar hai (agar provider expose karta ho) — step-by-step reasoning prompt karne ki jagah.

Medium effort: agent kaise kaam karta hai, use badalna

  • Task ko chhote steps me todo: ek single LLM call jo sab kuch karti hai, uski jagah task ko focused steps ki sequence me decompose karo. Example: research agent jo external data ke corpus me relevant information dhoondh kar report synthesize karta hai — ek call me poori report banane ki jagah: (1) user ki preferences ya constraints extract karo, (2) database ya search tool query karo, (3) results ko filter ya summarize karo, (4) final answer ya message generate karo. Har step ko independently evaluate karna aasan hai — agar report me errors hain, to failure ko specific step tak trace kar sakte hain (jaise kharab retrieval ya galat filtering), ek monolithic call ko debug karne ki jagah.
  • RAG retrieval tune karo: kai agents me retrieval quality overall performance ko generation quality se zyada drive karti hai. Retriever ko bheji jaane wali query rework karke, source documents ki chunking adjust karke, retrieved chunks ki sankhya tune karke, aur LLM ko pass karne se pehle lightweight reranking step add karke retrieval improve kar sakte ho. Retrieval quality measure karna Chapter 7 me detail me hai. Ek real case: ek delivery company ka customer support chatbot dashers (drivers) ke sawalon par hallucinate kar raha tha — jaise refund policies invent karna ya order details misinterpret karna. Engineers ko pata chala ki chatbot ko ek saath bahut zyada raw information dikh rahi thi: delivery history ka har event (pickup time, location pings, chat messages, status changes) prompt me dump ho raha tha aur model volume se confuse ho raha tha. Fix tha ek layer add karna jo relevant delivery history ko clean, structured form me summarize karke chatbot ko pass kare. Koi model change nahi, koi retraining nahi — sirf jo model ke paas pehle se tha use organize karne ka behtar tareeka. Unhone change ko test kiya hazaaron simulated conversations chalakar (har simulated conversation doosre LLM ne dasher ka role play karke generate ki thi) aur hallucination rates measure ki — fix ne simulations me hallucinations lagbhag 90% kam kar diye, aur improvement production me bhi hold hua.
  • Tool descriptions fix karo: agar model baar-baar tool ko galat call karta hai (galat argument formats, missing parameters), to prompt me tool kaise describe hai use revisit karo. Example: calendar check karne wala tool dates YYYY-MM-DD format me expect karta hai, par model "next Saturday" ya "March 10th" jaise strings pass karta rehta hai. Tool description kehti hai date: string par format specify nahi karti. Use date: string in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., "2025-03-10") me badalne se scheduling wali har query ka argument generation error fix ho jata hai.
  • Self-consistency: reasoning ya judgment wale tasks ke liye same prompt multiple times chalao (temperature 0 se zyada par) aur outputs compare karo. Agar zyada tar responses ek answer par agree karte hain, to wo answer likely correct hai. Example: user intent classify karne ke liye teen responses sample karo — do kehte hain "scheduling request", ek kehta hai "listing question" — to "scheduling request" choose karo. Ye per query zyada cost karta hai (multiple LLM calls), to ise high-stakes decisions ke liye reserve karo jahan sahi hona speed se zyada matter karta hai.
  • Verification ke liye doosri LLM call: pehli call ke output ko check karne ke liye alag call add karo. Example: agent email draft karne ke baad doosri call verify karti hai — "kya ye email listing data ko accurately reflect karta hai? kya ye client ke persona se match karta hai?" Isse wo errors pakde jate hain jo pehli call miss kar gayi. Trade-off latency aur cost hai (ek ki jagah do calls), to verification aam taur par sabse important outputs par use karo, har request par nahi.
  • Synchronous checks (guardrails): output user tak pahunchne se pehle chalne wale checks add karo (Chapter 9 me guardrails discussion) — jaise regex jo Social Security number jaisi patterns wale emails pakde, ya SQL parser jo database par hit karne se pehle syntactically invalid queries reject kare. Ye saste aur fast hote hain, aur sabse embarrassing failures ko rokte hain chahe model kabhi-kabhi slip kare.

High effort: model-level changes

  • Fine-tuning: pretrained model ko apne example inputs aur outputs ke set par aage train karna, taaki model tumhare specific task ko specific tareeke se handle karna seekhe. Jab tumhare paas hundreds of high-quality labeled examples hon aur prompting se issue fix na ho raha ho, to fine-tuning ek option hai. Practice me zyada tar teams full fine-tuning ki jagah parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods jaise LoRA ya QLoRA se shuru karti hain. LoRA har parameter ki jagah low-rank adapter matrices ka chhota set update karta hai — isse single GPU (jaise A100 ya H100) par kuch ghanton me fine-tune kar sakte ho, multi-GPU cluster par dinon ki jagah. QLoRA aage jaakar training ke dauraan base model ko 4-bit precision par quantize karta hai, jisse 70B-parameter model ko 48 GB memory wale single GPU par fine-tune kar sakte ho. Aksar narrow task par meaningful improvement ke liye 50–200 high-quality examples kaafi hote hain. Supervised fine-tuning ke aage preference fine-tuning methods hain — jaise direct preference optimization (DPO), jo outputs ke pairs par train karta hai jisme ek preferred hota hai, aur KTO, jise sirf individual outputs chahiye hote hain jo desirable ya undesirable label kiye gaye hon. Preference fine-tuning useful hai jab failure mode style ya quality ke baare me ho (jaise "model ke jawab sahi hain par bahut verbose hain"), correctness ke baare me nahi.
  • Serving cost bhi ginno: fine-tuning ka matlab hai resulting model ko serve bhi karna hai — ye alag infrastructure cost hai. Apne GPUs par chala sakte ho (jaise vLLM ya TGI se), ya inference provider use kar sakte ho jo fine-tuned models host karta hai. Fine-tuning commit karne se pehle cost economics check karo: bade general-purpose model ki jagah chhote fine-tuned model se hone wali bachat ko training, serving aur maintenance ki cost se zyada hona chahiye, time ke saath.
  • Automated prompt optimization: prompts ko thousands of requests me reuse kiya jata hai, to chhoti wording changes ka bhi bada aggregate impact hota hai. Prompt ko tunable artifact ki tarah treat kar sakte ho — variations try karo, held-out golden sets ke against test karo, aur jo accuracy improve kare use rakho. DSPy, TextGrad aur OPRO jaise automated prompt optimization frameworks isse aage jaate hain — Chapter 5 ke evaluation metrics ko optimization objective bana kar prompt variations par systematically search karte hain. Ye tools wo prompt wordings dhoondh sakte hain jo human soch bhi nahi sakta, par inhe well-defined evaluation function aur improvement reliably measure karne ke liye kaafi labeled examples chahiye hote hain. Kuch teams grid search se template variations par ye process formalize karti hain.
  • Human review annotations: high-stakes tasks ya hard-to-detect failure modes ke liye Chapter 10 jaisa lightweight interface banao taaki human reviewers regularly outputs ka chhota sample check aur annotate kar sakein. Annotations fine-tuning datasets me feed ho sakti hain aur wo failure modes reveal kar sakti hain jo automated evaluators miss karte hain.
Usool: prompt optimization ya fine-tuning try karne se pehle quick methods exhaust karo — ye heavier techniques debug aur maintain karne me mushkil hoti hain.
Example 12-1 — Structured output request + response (OpenAI Chat Completions) — Book me chhapa code (Chapter 12)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
  model="gpt-4o-2024-08-06",
  messages=[
      {
             "role": "system",
             "content": (
                 "Evaluate the trace. Return JSON with 'answer' "
                 "(your evaluation) and 'confidence' (0-10, how "
                 "confident you are in your answer)."
             ),
         },
         {"role": "user", "content": trace_text},
      ],
      response_format={
          "type": "json_schema",
          "json_schema": {
              "name": "evaluator_response",
              "strict": True,
              "schema": {
                  "type": "object",
                  "properties": {
                      "answer": {"type": "string"},
                      "confidence": {
                          "type": "integer",
                          "minimum": 0,
                          "maximum": 10,
                      },
                  },
                  "required": ["answer", "confidence"],
                  "additionalProperties": False,
              },
          },
      },
)
  {
    "answer": "The email tone is professional and appropriate for a
  luxury buyer.",
    "confidence": 8
  }

12.2Chapter 12 · Improving LLM Agents

The Improvement Loop — measure, fix, re-measure

Accuracy requirements meet ho jayein to cost kam karna shuru kar sakte hain. Approach accuracy wala hi hai: sabse bade cost drivers dhoondho, targeted changes karo, aur evaluators se verify karo ki quality intact hai.

Model size ko task complexity se match karo

Agent ka har step sabse powerful (aur sabse expensive) LLM nahi mangta. Har task ko us sabse chhote model par map karo jo uski accuracy requirements meet karta hai. Lightweight models simple, high-volume tasks ke liye achhe kaam karte hain — sentiment classification, structured text se fields extract karna, ya basic user intent recognize karna. Sabse bade models un subtasks ke liye reserve karo jinme advanced reasoning chahiye, complex instructions follow karni hain, ya accuracy stakes high hain. Example: real estate assistant me ek chhota model incoming messages ko categories me classify kar sakta hai — "listing question", "scheduling request", "general inquiry" — aur sirf complex queries (jaise property ko recent sales se compare karke customized explanation chahiye) zyada capable model ko route hoti hain.

Token usage kam karo

Zyada tar LLM providers tokens ke hisaab se charge karte hain (input aur output dono), to token count kam karna seedha cost kam karta hai:

  • Instructions concise rakho.
  • RAG-based agents ke liye prompt me retrieved documents ki sankhya tune karo.
  • Agar agent multiple LLM calls me same lambi document analyze karta hai, to pehle ek step add karo jahan sasta model document ko summarize kare — uske baad wali calls chhote summary par operate karti hain, har downstream call ke input tokens kam ho jate hain. Example: lamba legal contract analyze karke clauses extract karna ho, to contract ko ek baar upfront summarize karna poora text har specialized extraction prompt ko feed karne se bahut sasta padta hai.
  • LLM ko explicitly concise rehne ko kaho jahan appropriate ho. Jahan output known structure follow karta hai, wahan natural language prose ya JSON (jisme bahut braces aur brackets hote hain) ki jagah YAML jaisa compact format maangne se generated tokens kam ho sakte hain.

Prompts ko cache-friendly banao

Caching ek cost reduction technique hai jise kai teams overlook karti hain. Kai LLM API providers caching mechanisms use karte hain jo repeated requests ki latency aur cost dono kam karte hain. Jab ek provider ne prompt caching introduce kiya, to usne report kiya ki cache hits ki cost base input token price ka 10% thi (90% reduction) aur lambi prompts par latency 85% tak gir gayi. Ye numbers tabhi apply hote hain jab prompt ka prefix byte-for-byte match kare across requests — isiliye prompts structure karne ka tareeka matter karta hai.

Modern LLMs Transformer architecture par based hain. Har step par Transformer har token ke liye "key" aur "value" vectors ka set compute karta hai — keys lookup signals ki tarah kaam karte hain ye decide karne ke liye ki kaunse past tokens sabse zyada matter karte hain, values actual information carry karte hain jo wo tokens contribute karte hain. Lambi sequences generate karte waqt ya kai similar prompts handle karte waqt saare KV states ko scratch se dobara compute karna expensive hai. LLM inference engines is redundant computation ko KV cache me intermediate states store karke mitigate karte hain — jab naya prompt exact same token sequence (prefix) se shuru hota hai, to engine us prefix ke cached KV states reuse karta hai aur sirf naye suffix ke states compute karta hai. Is reuse se latency aur compute cost dono kam hote hain.

Caching tabhi apply hoti hai jab prefix exactly match kare. Ek token ka change bhi cache ko us point se aage invalidate kar deta hai aur full recomputation force karta hai. Example: task hai "Think of a friendlier way to say: X" jahan X koi bhi text ho. Agar instruction ko varying data se pehle rakhte ho, to har request same lamba prefix (instruction) share karti hai aur provider use cache karke reuse kar sakta hai. Agar instruction data ke baad aati hai, to sirf data ke pehle kuch tokens (jo coincidentally overlap kar sakte hain) shared prefix me rehte hain — cache reuse minimal hota hai. Whitespace differences bhi cache prefix tod dete hain — agar tumhare prompt templates main instructions se pehle variable-length content (jaise username) insert karte hain, to har request scratch se compute hoti hai. Saare static instructions upar rakho aur saara variable data neeche.

  • Constant instructions ko kisi bhi user-provided ya changing data se pehle rakho.
  • Formatting aur phrasing saari requests me consistent rakho.
  • Provider ki documentation check karo — cached vs non-cached tokens ki pricing providers ke beech vary karti hai.

Batching

Agar kuch LLM calls time-sensitive nahi hain, to unhe batch kar sakte ho — ek-ek request bhejne ki jagah multiple requests ko ek API call me group karke saath me process karo. Isse per-request overhead kam hota hai. Kuch providers batched workloads ke liye explicit discounts dete hain — jaise ek provider ki Batch API requests ko 24-hour window me synchronous calls ki aadhi cost par process karti hai. Batching offline tasks ke liye achha kaam karta hai: ek din ke production traces par evaluators chalana, documents ke backlog ke summaries generate karna, ya CI ke liye dataset score karna. Real-time user-facing requests ke liye nahi chalti, jahan latency matter karti hai.

Distillation

Agar bada model kisi task par achha perform karta hai par scale par chalana bahut mehenga hai, to distillation try kar sakte ho. Idea: bade model (teacher) se examples ke set par labeled outputs generate karwao, phir chhote model (student) ko un outputs par fine-tune karo. Student teacher ke behavior ko mimic karna seekhta hai, inference cost ke ek fraction par. Distillation standard fine-tuning se alag hai: standard fine-tuning me human-labeled data par train karte hain, distillation me teacher model ke outputs par train karte hain — iska matlab training data saste me generate kar sakte ho teacher ko unlabeled inputs par chala kar, jisse training set scale karna aasan ho jata hai.

Catch ye hai: student teacher ki quality se aage nahi jayega. Agar teacher kuch inputs par hallucinate karta hai, to student wahi galtiyan seekh lega. Students rare ya distribution-shifted inputs par worse calibration bhi dikhate hain, kyunki wo cases teacher ke outputs me underrepresented hote hain. Distilled model ko wahi rigor se evaluate karo jo kisi bhi change par lagate ho (golden dataset checks, online monitoring), aur uske error profile ko teacher se compare karo taaki wo naye failure modes na pick kar le. Distillation ko fine-tuning jaisi hi serving infrastructure chahiye (dedicated GPUs ya inference provider), to ye high-volume tasks ke liye sabse practical hai jahan per-query cost savings setup cost justify karein. Low query volumes wali teams ke liye economics kaam nahi karte — model cascade behtar fit ho sakta hai kyunki use training ya custom model hosting nahi chahiye.

Model cascades

Suppose production me LLM-as-judge evaluator chala rahe ho aur uski cost $0.02 per trace hai. 10,000 traces per day par ye $200/day hota hai. Hum wahi accuracy rakhna chahte hain par kam kharch karna chahte hain. Model cascade ye karta hai: ek target accuracy set karo — cascade ke output aur expensive model ke output ke beech minimum agreement rate (jaise 95% agreement). Phir har query ko pehle cheap model se guzaro. Agar cheap model apne answer me confident hai, to use accept karo. Agar confident nahi hai, to expensive model par escalate karo. Goal hai target accuracy meet karna, expensive model ko jitni kam queries bhejni padein.

Cascade ko proxy se do cheezein chahiye: ek binary verdict (pass/fail, true/false) aur ek confidence score jise threshold kar sakein. Isi liye LLM-as-judge natural example hai — Chapter 5 me judges ko binary classifiers ki tarah define kiya gaya hai. Agar underlying task open-ended hai, to structured output maango jisme verdict aur score dono hon — sirf free-form paragraph nahi. Expensive model ko oracle kehte hain (best system jo humare paas currently hai) aur cheap model ko proxy. Oracle perfect hone ki zaroorat nahi — wo sirf humara best current system hai. Cascade oracle ke answers ko proxy ki cost ke kareeb reproduce karne ki koshish karta hai.

Confidence kaise mile? LLMs text ek token at a time generate karte hain, har step par vocabulary ke har token ko probability assign karte hue. Jab model classification task me "true" generate karta hai, to usne internally "true" ki probability aur har doosre token (false, maybe, yes) ki probability compute ki hoti hai. Agar true ki probability 0.90 aur false ki 0.10 hai, to model bahut confident hai; agar true 0.55 aur false 0.45 hai, to ye coin flip ke kareeb hai. Isi liye classification tasks (jahan answer ek token hai jaise true ya false) cascades ke liye best case hain — valid answers ki probabilities ko confidence estimates ki tarah use kar sakte hain.

  • Approach 1 — classification tasks ke liye logprobs: zyada tar LLM APIs probabilities directly return nahi karte — log probabilities (logprobs) return karte hain, jo probabilities ka natural logarithm hota hai. Probability 0.90 ka logprob lagbhag −0.10 hota hai; probability 0.01 ka lagbhag −4.60. Logprobs hamesha negative ya zero hote hain, aur zero ke kareeb matlab zyada probability. API se logprobs request karne par providers aam taur par top 5–20 most likely tokens ke logprobs return karte hain. "Answer true or false" se end hone wale prompt me true aur false dono lagbhag hamesha us top list me hote hain. Dono logprobs ko exp() se wapas probabilities me convert karo, normalize karo taaki sum 1 ho, aur zyada wali ko confidence score banao. Open-ended tasks me ye approach kaam nahi karti — answer kai tokens lamba hota hai aur top-token logprobs ek waqt me sirf ek token ke baare me batate hain; poore answer ki probability compare karne ka koi tareeka nahi hai, kyunki API wo deti hi nahi.
  • Approach 2 — open-ended tasks ke liye verbalized confidence (caution ke saath): proxy se structured output return karwao — ek field me open-ended answer, doosri field me verbalized confidence score. Prompt me add kar sakte ho ("0 se 10 ke scale par apne answer me kitne confident ho?") ya provider ke structured output API se JSON schema enforce kar sakte ho. Example: evaluation trace par JSON return karo jisme "answer" (tumhara evaluation) aur "confidence" (0–10) hon. Verbalized confidence calibration improve ho rahi hai aur classification tasks ke liye reasonably achha kaam karti hai — par open-ended outputs ke liye verbalized scores bahut less reliable hote hain. Base models bhi instruction-tuned ya fine-tuned models se behtar calibrated hote hain, kyunki RLHF training models ko confidence express karne ki taraf bias karti hai chahe warranted na ho.

Confidence ko face value par mat lo. Chahe log probabilities se padho ya model se verbalize karwao, confidence ko correctness ka reliable measure samajhna aasan hai — par ye nahi hai. Confidence sirf ek aur signal hai jo model produce karta hai, aur aksar noisy hota hai. Goal ye validate karna nahi hai ki confidence human labels ke against sahi hai — hum proxy aur oracle ko same held-out examples par chalate hain aur simple sawal poochte hain: jab proxy high confidence report karta hai, to kya uska answer usually oracle se match karta hai? Jab match karte hain, to kya proxy usually high confidence report karta hai? Ye correlation batata hai ki threshold kahan set karein — wo cutoff jiske upar hum proxy par bharosa kar sakte hain ki wo oracle ka output reproduce karega bina use call kiye. Chhota proxy deserved se zyada baar confident dikh sakta hai.

Cascade threshold ko offline calibrate karna

Deploy karne se pehle cascade ko offline calibrate karo taaki confidence threshold mil sake:

  1. Held-out evaluation set ke N examples lo aur target agreement rate r tay karo (jaise 0.95).
  2. Proxy ko saare N examples par chalao — har answer aur confidence score record karo.
  3. Oracle ko saare N examples par chalao — har answer record karo (ise ground truth mano).
  4. Har example ke liye mark karo ki proxy ka answer oracle se match karta hai ya nahi.
  5. Examples ko proxy confidence ke hisaab se sort karo, highest pehle.
  6. Sorted list me neeche chalte jao — har position i par examples 1 se i ke beech match rate compute karo. Threshold t ko us confidence score par set karo jo aakhri position par hai jahan match rate kam se kam r hai.

Runtime par har production query pehle proxy ko jati hai. Agar proxy ki confidence t par ya usse upar hai, to proxy ka answer return karo; neeche hai to oracle par escalate karo. Escalated queries slow hoti hain — kyunki wo proxy aur oracle dono se guzarti hain — par ye acceptable hai jab zyada tar queries (70%–80%) proxy se hi handle ho jati hain, kyunki average latency phir bhi girti hai. Agar do se zyada models hain alag cost levels par, to unhe chain kar sakte ho — sabse sasta pehle try karo, confidence low ho to agle par escalate karo, aur aise hi oracle tak. Har model ko apna threshold milta hai, same tareeke se calibrate kiya hua. Threshold-finding process poor calibration ke against robust hai: agar confidence scores correct aur incorrect answers ko separate nahi karte, to calibration step valid threshold dhoondhne me fail ho jayega aur cascade sab kuch oracle ko route karega — jo safe default hai. Humne paise nahi bachaye, par kuch toota bhi nahi. Behtar calibrated proxies zyada bachat karte hain kyunki hum un par zyada queries ke liye bharosa kar sakte hain.

Routing — cascade se alag

Cascade me har query saste model se shuru hoti hai aur confidence low ho to escalate hoti hai. Routing me ek classifier upfront decide karta hai ki har query kis model ko bhejni hai, bina pehle saste model ko try kiye. Example: router simple queries ("listing price kya hai?") seedha fast, saste model ko bhejta hai, aur complex queries ("in teen properties ko school districts, commute times aur price trends me compare karo") seedha zyada capable aur expensive model ko. Routing cascade ki latency penalty avoid karta hai (jahan escalated queries do models se guzarti hain), par use reliable classifier chahiye hota hai aur misrouted queries ko doosra chance nahi milta. Practice me kuch teams dono combine karti hain: router obvious cases handle karta hai, cascade ambiguous middle ko. Off-the-shelf routing solutions bhi available hain — jaise ek open source router jo human preference data par train hua aur MT-Bench par GPT-4 quality ka 95% maintain karte hue 85% cost reduction achieve karta hai, aur managed routing services jo per query complexity aur cost ke basis par models dynamically select karte hain.

Putting it together: cost optimization ka matlab quality sacrifice karna nahi hai — har change ko evaluators aur CI se verify karo. Sabse pehle model size match karo aur tokens kam karo, phir caching aur batching, aur high-volume tasks ke liye distillation ya cascades — hamesha measurement ke saath.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 12 — Improving LLM Agents
← Previous12.1 · Improvement Strategies — prompt, retrieval, finetuning→ Next12.3 · Choosing What to Improve — priority kaise tay karein
12.3Chapter 12 · Improving LLM Agents

Choosing What to Improve — priority kaise tay karein

Itne improvement options ke saath ye decide karna mushkil ho sakta hai ki shuru kahan se karein. Book ka decision framework har strategy ko uske typical effort, data requirements aur best-suited failure type se map karta hai — aur usool simple hai: upar se shuru karo, neeche ki taraf kaam karo. Har row ko usse upar wali se zyada effort aur data chahiye hota hai, to bhaari interventions me invest karne se pehle saste options exhaust karo.

Decision framework — kaunsi strategy kab

  • Prompt refinement — Low effort, kuch failing examples chahiye: specification failures, formatting issues aur missing constraints ke liye best hai. Ek-line clarification se lekar few-shot examples aur persona guidance tak — sabse pehle ye try karo.
  • Architectural changes (task decomposition, retrieval, tools) — Medium effort, failure patterns ki understanding chahiye: multi-step reasoning errors, missing information aur complex workflows ke liye best hai. Task ko steps me todo, RAG tune karo, tool descriptions fix karo.
  • Automated prompt optimization (DSPy, TextGrad, OPRO) — Medium effort, 50+ labeled examples + evaluation function chahiye: systematic quality improvement ke liye best hai jab manual prompt iteration plateau par pahunch jaye. Ye tools prompt variations par systematically search karte hain, evaluation metrics ko objective bana kar.
  • Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA) — High effort, 50–200+ labeled examples chahiye: narrow, well-defined tasks ke liye best hai jahan prompting alone generalisation failures fix nahi kar sakti.
  • Full fine-tuning / preference tuning (DPO) — High effort, 500+ labeled examples ya preference pairs chahiye: style, tone aur format issues ke liye best hai jo kai tasks me fail hote hain — jab PEFT kaafi nahi hota.
  • Distillation + cascade — High effort, bada labeled dataset + oracle model chahiye: high-volume, well-understood tasks par accuracy maintain karte hue cost reduction ke liye best hai.

Priority tay karte waqt sirf effort mat dekho — impact bhi dekho: kaunsa failure mode sabse zyada users ko hit karta hai? Kaunsa failure sabse zyada costly hai (jaise galat email bhejna vs verbose summary)? Error analysis aur data analysis (Chapters 3 aur 11) se pata chalta hai ki kaunse failures frequent hain aur kaunse severe hain. Jo fix low effort me high-frequency failure solve karta hai, wo pehle aata hai; jo high effort me rare failure solve karta hai, wo aakhir me.

Lifecycle continue karta hai

Har improvement failure distribution ko badal sakta hai. Prompt change ek class of errors fix karke doosri introduce kar sakta hai. Cost optimization jo queries ko saste model par route karta hai, accuracy ko subtle tareekon se degrade kar sakta hai. Response hai loop ko chalate rakhna: naye behavior ko analyze karo, impact measure karo, aur dobara improve karo. Evaluation datasets stale ho jate hain jaise products evolve hote hain aur user behavior shift hota hai. Error taxonomies ko periodically revisit karna padta hai. Naye failure modes surface hote hi naye evaluators aate hain. Improvements CI se guzarte hain taaki wo model updates aur code changes ke across persist karein. Ek informal version bhi compound karta hai time ke saath — har hafte kuch traces review karo, golden set update karo, aur sabse kharab prompt fix karo.

Aage kya badal raha hai — aur kya durable hai

Book durable core cover karti hai. Specific models, APIs aur tools badalte rahenge — jab tak tum ye padhoge, kuch examples purane model versions reference kar sakte hain aur naye evaluation platforms aur techniques aa chuke honge. Par systematically ye samajhne ki practice ki tumhara system kaise fail hota hai, un failures ko measure karna, aur unhe fix karna — ye kahi nahi ja rahi. Analyze-Measure-Improve lifecycle ek thinking framework hai, frozen instructions ka set nahi, aur ye agle generation ke models aur tools ke saath adapt hota hai.

Kai areas tezi se evolve ho rahe hain aur likely evaluation kaise kaam karta hai use badal denge: reasoning models jo lambi internal chains of thought produce karte hain, wo naye sawal uthate hain ki intermediate reasoning steps ko kaise evaluate karein, sirf final answers ko nahi. Multi-agent systems, jahan kai agents coordinate karke task complete karte hain, inter-agent communication aur collective behavior ke aas-paas evaluation challenges introduce karte hain jo single-agent evaluation cover nahi karta. Process reward models, jo solution ke har step ko score karte hain sirf final output ki jagah, automated evaluators banane ka tareeka badal sakte hain. Aur jaise-jaise agents lambi-running, zyada autonomous workloads lete hain, evaluation aur monitoring ke beech ki line aur blur hoti jayegi. Ye topics is book me depth me cover nahi hain kyunki community abhi bhi practical guidance par kaam kar rahi hai — par is book ke foundations — traces padhna, taxonomies banana, judges calibrate karna, CI chalana aur outputs review karna — in sab par apply honge.

Ant me yaad rakho: evaluation ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — ye ek loop hai. Analyze karo, measure karo, improve karo — aur phir dobara analyze karo. Jo team ye loop har hafte chalati hai, wo us team se hamesha aage rahegi jo sirf launch ke time evaluation karti hai.
SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 12 — Improving LLM Agents

Error Taxonomy Lab — trace padho, failure mode pehchano

Ek trace padho, guess karo ki failure mode kya hai, aur check karo — error analysis (Chapter 3) ka core skill hai trace se failure mode pehchanana. Galat guess bhi seekhne ka hissa hai.

TRY ITTrace chuno, failure mode guess karo
Trace padho, guess chuno, phir Check karo.
Kya seekha?

  
Usool (Chapter 3): failure mode wahi hai jo root cause batata hai — sirf symptom nahi. Ek trace ko taxonomy me daalne se pehle 20 aisi traces padho, phir criterion define karo jo 70–80% traces par hold kare.

L2Interactive Lab
Cohen's Kappa Lab — agreement measure karo


Do annotators ne 100 traces label kiye. Observed agreement aur chance agreement badlo — dekho Cohen's Kappa kaise badalta hai, aur kab agreement "substantial" kehlata hai.



  
TRY ITSliders ghumao — kappa dekho

  

    
    
  

  

  
Kappa ka matlab

  
Formula (Chapter 4): kappa = (Po − Pe) / (1 − Pe). Kappa 1 = perfect agreement, 0 = sirf chance-level agreement. Raw agreement % dhokha de sakta hai jab ek class dominate kare — kappa chance ko adjust karta hai.




SOURCESource: Evals for AI Engineers, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Implementing Automated Evaluators

TRY ITJudge ki setting badlo — verdict dekho

  

    
    
    
    
  

  

  
Judge ka verdict

  
Usool (Chapter 5): AI judge useful hai par biased ho sakta hai — position swap karke aur length normalize karke bias check karo. Judge ko human labels ke against validate karo (TPR/TNR naapo) aur judge drift ke liye regularly revalidate karo.

F1End Matter · Interview FAQs
Interview FAQs
LLM evals interviews (current era) ke liye — error analysis se lekar CI/CD tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 Evals kya hain — aur LLM apps me ye itne zaroori kyun hain?
Evals wo systematic process hai jisse LLM app ki quality measure karte hain — traces padh kar failure modes dhoondhna, evaluators banana, CI me regression pakadna aur production monitor karna. Bina evals ke tumhe pata hi nahi chalta ki model update ke baad tumhara agent silently degrade ho gaya hai. Evals hi wo safety net hai jo 'ek baar kaam kar gaya' ko 'hamesha kaam karta hai' me badalta hai.
Q02 Analyze-Measure-Improve lifecycle kya hai?
Ye book ka core framework hai: pehle Analyze karo — traces padh kar failure modes identify karo; phir Measure karo — evaluators banao jo un failures ko scale par quantify karein; phir Improve karo — prompt, retrieval ya model changes se fix karo aur dobara measure karo. Har improvement failure distribution badal sakta hai, isliye loop chalta rehta hai — ye ek baar ka kaam nahi hai.
Q03 Error analysis kaise karte hain — trace se failure mode tak ka process kya hai?
Pehle traces ka dataset banao — dimensions aur queries se interesting slices nikalo. Phir traces padh kar open coding karo (free-form notes likho ki kya galat hua), phir axial coding se un notes ko failure modes ki taxonomy me group karo. Ek candidate pattern ko confirm karne ke liye us cluster ki 20 traces padho aur criterion define karo jo 70-80% traces par hold kare. Tabhi wo confirmed failure mode banta hai.
Q04 Golden dataset kya hai aur ye kitna bada hona chahiye?
Golden dataset hand-curated input examples ka set hai, jinke saath reference outputs hote hain — CI me regression pakadne ke liye. Shuruaat me 20-50 examples kaafi hain, mature system me 100-200 hote hain. Ye production data ka random sample nahi hai — ye purpose-built hai: core features, pehle dekhe gaye critical failures aur edge cases cover karne ke liye. Naye failure modes milte hi ise expand karo aur stale examples retire karo.
Q05 CI pass rate ko production quality kyun nahi samajhna chahiye?
Kyunki golden dataset chhota aur curated hai — CI pass hona matlab agent un specific cases ko abhi bhi handle karta hai, production ke hazaaron queries par performance ke baare me ye kuch nahi kehta. CI ek smoke test jaisa hai: fail ho to kuch definitely galat hai; pass ho to humne kuch jaana hua toda nahi, par general quality prove nahi hui. Production quality ke liye online monitoring aur random trace review chahiye.
Q06 Data leakage evals me kya hota hai aur isse kaise bachein?
Jab golden set ke examples galti se agent ke prompts me few-shot examples ban kar ya LLM judge ke prompts me aa jayein, to model ne test cases pehle se dekh liye hote hain aur un par achha perform karta hai bina actually improve hue — CI results meaningless ho jate hain. Bachav: golden set ko prompt content se alag file ya repository me rakho, aur har commit par automated check chalao jo golden inputs ko prompt content se diff kare.
Q07 LLM-as-judge kya hai aur use kaise validate karte hain?
LLM-as-judge me ek LLM dusre LLM ke output ko score karta hai — open-ended tasks ke liye jahan exact match kaam nahi karta. Validate karne ke liye judge ke verdicts ko human labels se compare karo aur TPR (true positive rate) aur TNR (true negative rate) naapo. Judge ke biases check karo — position bias ke liye order swap karo, verbosity bias ke liye length normalize karo. Bina validation ke judge par bharosa mat karo.
Q08 Judge drift kya hai aur isse kaise handle karte hain?
Judge drift tab hota hai jab LLM-as-judge ki accuracy time ke saath degrade ho jaye — ya to provider ne judge ke peeche wala model update kar diya ho, ya team ki 'correct' ki samajh shift ho gayi ho (criteria drift). Handle karne ke teen tareeke: model versions pin karo, har kuch hafte fresh human labels se judge ko revalidate karo, aur judge ka LLM swap karne par poora validation dobara chalao.
Q09 Cohen's Kappa kya hai aur raw agreement se behtar kyun hai?
Cohen's Kappa do annotators ke beech agreement measure karta hai, chance agreement ko adjust karke — formula (Po - Pe) / (1 - Pe), jahan Po observed agreement hai aur Pe chance se expected agreement. Raw agreement % dhokha de sakta hai jab ek class dominate kare — jaise 90% traces pass hon to dono annotators 'pass' keh kar 90% agree kar lenge bina kuch samjhe. Kappa 1 perfect agreement hai, 0 sirf chance-level.
Q10 Rubric kya hai aur evals me iska kya role hai?
Rubric 'achha output kya hota hai' ki likhi hui definition hai — har quality dimension ke liye criteria aur unke levels. Rubric ke bina evaluation subjective ho jata hai: do reviewers alag faisle dete hain. Rubric banane ke liye pehle traces padho, phir criteria likho, phir annotators ko un par align karo aur agreement (kappa) naapo. LLM-as-judge ke prompts me bhi rubric hi hoti hai.
Q11 Exact match, similarity aur LLM-judge metrics me se kaun kab use karein?
Exact match wahan jahan ek sahi jawab ho — classification, structured outputs, unit tests. Similarity metrics (ROUGE, BLEU) text overlap naapte hain, par factual correctness nahi — summary ke liye limited use hai. LLM-as-judge open-ended tasks ke liye hai — writing, reasoning, tone — par use validate karna padta hai. Usool: metric wahi jo task ki asli quality naape, jo naapna aasan ho wo nahi.
Q12 RAG eval me retrieval aur generation ko alag kyun naapte hain?
Kyunki RAG me failure ki do jagah hain — retrieval galat docs laaya ya generation ne sahi docs se galat jawab banaya. Agar sirf final answer naapo to pata nahi chalega ki dosh kiska hai. Retrieval ke liye recall@k aur context precision naapo; generation ke liye faithfulness (claim-by-claim support) aur answer relevance. Component-level eval hi batata hai ki fix kahan lagana hai.
Q13 Faithfulness aur groundedness me kya farak hai?
Faithfulness ka matlab hai generated answer ka har claim retrieved context se supported ho — koi hallucination nahi. Groundedness usi ka broader concept hai: answer source material se kitna grounded hai, citation quality samet — kya citations sahi jagah point karte hain aur claims ko actually support karte hain. Dono ko claim-by-claim check karo; judge ko sirf relevant portion do, poora document nahi.
Q14 Multi-turn eval single-turn eval se kaise alag hai?
Single-turn me ek query aur ek jawab hota hai; multi-turn me poori conversation hoti hai jahan context carry hota hai. Multi-turn eval session-level hota hai — ek turn fail ho to poora session fail. Isme context retention (pehle di gayi constraint yaad rahi?), tool sequencing aur transition failures naapte hain. Transition failure heatmap batata hai ki failure kis turn se kis turn me hota hai — wahi hotspot fix karo.
Q15 Transition failure heatmap kya hai?
Ye ek matrix hai jo dikhati hai ki agent kis state se kis state me jaate waqt fail hota hai — jaise Turn 1 (constraint di) se Turn 3 (constraint use karni thi) tak. Har cell ek transition ki failure rate batata hai. Heatmap se pata chalta hai ki failure ek jagah concentrate ho raha hai ya har jagah fail ho raha hai. Agent evolve hote hi ise periodically regenerate karo — hotspot shift ho sakta hai.
Q16 Tool-use eval me kya-kya check karte hain?
Chaar stages alag-alag: tool selection (sahi tool chuna?), argument generation (arguments sahi format aur range me hain?), execution (tool call chala ya error aaya?), aur output handling (tool ke response ko sahi interpret kiya?). Sirf final answer naapne se root cause pata nahi chalti. Saath me ye bhi check karo ki agent tool call karta bhi hai ya pretrained knowledge se guess kar deta hai.
Q17 Agent eval me adversarial testing kyun zaroori hai?
Kyunki tool access wala agent sirf galat jawab nahi de sakta — use trick karke harmful kaam bhi karwaya ja sakta hai. Teen threat categories test karo: prompt injection (user seedha kehta hai 'instructions ignore karo'), indirect injection (malicious instruction retrieved document ya email me chhupi ho), aur privilege escalation (agent authorized scope se bahar tools call kare). Ye tests CI pipeline me chalao, sirf initial development me nahi — model updates se susceptibility badal sakti hai.
Q18 Production monitoring me kya-kya log karna chahiye?
Har request ka initial input aur metadata, saare intermediate LLM calls (prompts, responses, reasoning), saare tool calls (names, arguments, responses, errors), RAG me retrieved documents, final output, user feedback (thumbs-up/down, edits, follow-ups) aur evaluator outputs. Ye logs poori interaction reconstruct karne dete hain. Traces, spans aur sessions me organize karo aur production traces ka sample daily review karo.
Q19 Guardrails kya hain aur LLM-as-judge se kaise alag hain?
Guardrails execution ke dauraan chalne wale fast, deterministic checks hain — output user tak pahunchne se pehle. Inhe milliseconds me chalna chahiye aur false positive rate 1% se neeche honi chahiye, isliye LLM-as-judge (2-3 second per call) guardrail ke liye suitable nahi hai. Guardrails regex, JSON schema validation, blocklist/allowlist aur lightweight parsers hote hain. Trigger hone par safe fallback, retry ya simpler path use karo.
Q20 Sampling production traces ke liye 1-5% kyun kaafi hai?
Kyunki LLM-as-judge evaluators slow aur expensive hote hain — poore traffic par chalana practical nahi hai. 1-5% sample bhi failure rates ka statistically meaningful estimate deta hai, khaas taur par jab corrected success rate aur 95% confidence interval (bootstrapping se) compute karo. Sampling ke saath failure-driven aur uncertainty-based selection bhi use karo taaki rare failures bhi pakde jayein.
Q21 Human review ke liye traces select karne ki teen strategies kya hain?
Random sampling — unbiased, overall quality ka estimate deta hai, par rare failures miss karta hai. Uncertainty sampling — jahan automated evaluators disagree karte hain, wahan review karo; ambiguous cases se criteria tighten karne ki sabse zyada information milti hai. Failure-driven sampling — guardrails ya thumbs-down se flagged traces review karo; precision high hai par recall low hai, kyunki ye sirf wo pakadta hai jo existing signals dhoondhte hain. Starting split: 50% failure-driven, 30% uncertainty, 20% random.
Q22 Spreadsheet se custom review interface behtar kyun hai?
Kyunki LLM traces rows aur columns me fit nahi hote — ek trace me query, tool calls (JSON blobs), retrieved docs aur final output sab ek row me aa jate hain, aur reviewer ko JSON aankh se parse karna padta hai. Custom interface me query upar, har tool call collapsible panel me, email actual email ki tarah dikhta hai — jo trace spreadsheet me 5 minute leta tha, wo 30 seconds me ho jata hai. Streamlit/Gradio se ya Langfuse, Braintrust, Phoenix jaise platforms se bana sakte ho.
Q23 Review interface me keyboard shortcuts itne important kyun hain?
Kyunki ye review speed ka single highest-leverage feature hai — ek minimal set (Next, Pass, Fail, Defer) bhi throughput double kar sakta hai. Reviewer jo hotkeys se kaam karta hai wo mouse-click wale se 2-3 guna fast hota hai. Iske baad structured failure tagging aur clustering aate hain. Kisi aur enhancement me invest karne se pehle shortcuts add karo.
Q24 Criteria drift kya hai aur review interface isse kaise deal karta hai?
Criteria drift tab hota hai jab reviewers ki 'correct' ki samajh time ke saath badal jaye — jaise-jaise wo zyada examples dekhte hain, 'correctness' ka matlab refine hota hai aur pehle wale labels baad walon se match nahi karte. Agar interface pehle wale labels revise karne nahi deta, to dataset chupchaap corrupt ho jata hai. Interface me labels edit karna, nayi failure categories add karna aur rubrics update karna possible hona chahiye.
Q25 EDA (exploratory data analysis) traces par kaise karte hain?
Dataset ko poke karke hypotheses generate karo: metric distributions plot karo (histogram/box plot — unimodal, bimodal ya long-tailed?), metadata ko outcomes se cross-tabulate karo (thumbs-down rate by session length), metrics ke beech correlations dhoondho, interesting slice filter karke 20 traces back-to-back padho, aur outliers flag karo (IQR rule ya top/bottom 1%). Par yaad rakho: cluster ya correlation conclusion nahi hai — hypothesis hai, traces padh kar confirm karo.
Q26 Cluster ko failure mode samajhna galat kyun hai?
Kyunki clusters similarity se bante hain, failure modes root cause se. Ek cluster me kai unrelated failure modes ho sakte hain jo coincidentally similar-looking outputs dete hain. Confirm karne ka protocol: cluster ki 20 traces padho, testable criterion define karo, aur check karo ki wo 70-80% traces par hold karta hai ya nahi. Agar nahi, to cluster bahut heterogeneous hai — split karo ya dobara examine karo.
Q27 Semantic search se failure mode ki poori population kaise dhoondhte hain?
Do tareeke: problematic trace se seed karo aur uske nearest neighbors (embedding similarity) dhoondho, ya natural-language description likh kar use embed karke search karo. Par dhyaan rakho — embedding similarity humari similarity ki notion jaisi nahi hoti; do traces topic words share karne se paas aa sakte hain jabki failure narrow ho. Labeled traces ke against precision aur recall check karo, aur zaroorat ho to application-specific features extract karke unhe embed karo.
Q28 AI coding assistants ko trace analysis me kaise use karein — aur kya na karein?
Traces ki file (JSON/JSONL), application description aur app code ek directory me daal kar assistant se plots, clustering, rubric drafting aur pattern search karwao — ye mechanics accelerate karta hai. Par assistant se ye mat poochho ki traces kyun fail ho rahe hain — wo plausible-sounding par galat explanation dega. Har causal claim ko hypothesis samjho aur ek variable change karke golden set par pehle-baad compare karke verify karo.
Q29 Prompt refinement me sabse pehle kya fix karna chahiye?
Specification errors — jahan prompt clearly nahi kehta ki kya chahiye, to model reasonable par galat guess karta hai. Apne 10 worst traces skim karo aur poochho 'kya prompt ne actually wahi kaha tha jo mujhe chahiye tha?' — experience me aadhe early failures specification errors hote hain jo ek-line edit se gayab ho jate hain. Iske baad few-shot examples, persona guidance aur chain-of-thought aate hain — par CI test cases ko few-shot examples mat banao, scores inflate ho jayenge.
Q30 RAG retrieval ko improve karne ke tareeke kya hain?
Retriever ko bheji jaane wali query rework karo, source documents ki chunking adjust karo, retrieved chunks ki sankhya tune karo, aur LLM ko pass karne se pehle lightweight reranking add karo. Kai agents me retrieval quality generation quality se zyada overall performance drive karti hai. Ek real case me delivery history ko clean structured summary me badalne se chatbot ke hallucinations lagbhag 90% kam ho gaye — bina model change ke.
Q31 Fine-tuning kab karna chahiye aur kab nahi?
Tab karo jab hundreds of high-quality labeled examples hon aur prompting se issue fix na ho raha ho — khaas taur par narrow, well-defined tasks par. LoRA/QLoRA se shuru karo — 50-200 examples kaafi hote hain aur single GPU par fine-tune ho jata hai. Mat karo jab prompt engineering ya RAG se kaam ho jaye, data kam ho (overfitting hoga), ya serving cost bachat se zyada ho. Style/quality issues ke liye DPO/KTO jaise preference fine-tuning use karo.
Q32 Prompt caching se cost kaise bachta hai?
Providers repeated prompt prefixes ke KV states cache karte hain — cache hit par cost base price ka 10% tak gir sakti hai aur latency 85% tak kam ho sakti hai. Par caching tabhi kaam karti hai jab prefix byte-for-byte match kare — ek token ya whitespace ka farak bhi cache tod deta hai. Isliye saare static instructions upar rakho aur variable data neeche, aur formatting consistent rakho.
Q33 Model cascade kya hai aur threshold kaise tay karte hain?
Cascade me har query pehle cheap model (proxy) ko jati hai; agar proxy confident hai to uska answer accept karo, nahi to expensive model (oracle) par escalate karo. Target agreement rate tay karo (jaise 95%), phir held-out set par dono models chalao, proxy ko confidence se sort karo aur wo threshold dhoondho jahan proxy-oracle match rate target se kam na ho. Confidence logprobs se (classification tasks) ya verbalized score se (open-ended, caution ke saath) milti hai. Agar confidence answers ko separate nahi karta, to cascade sab kuch oracle ko bhejta hai — safe default.
Q34 Routing aur cascade me kya farak hai?
Cascade me har query saste model se shuru hoti hai aur confidence low ho to escalate hoti hai — escalated queries do models se guzarti hain, isliye slow hoti hain. Routing me classifier upfront decide karta hai ki query kis model ko jayegi, bina saste model ko try kiye — latency penalty nahi hai, par misrouted queries ko doosra chance nahi milta. Practice me dono combine karte hain: router obvious cases handle karta hai, cascade ambiguous middle ko.
Q35 Improvement strategy choose karne ka framework kya hai?
Upar se shuru karo, neeche ki taraf kaam karo: prompt refinement (low effort, kuch failing examples) — specification failures ke liye; architectural changes (medium) — multi-step reasoning aur missing information ke liye; automated prompt optimization (medium, 50+ labeled examples) — jab manual iteration plateau ho; PEFT fine-tuning (high, 50-200+ examples) — narrow tasks ke liye; full/preference fine-tuning (high, 500+ examples) — style/tone ke liye; distillation + cascade (high) — high-volume cost reduction ke liye. Priority impact × frequency / effort se tay karo.
Q36 Evaluation datasets stale kyun ho jate hain aur kya karna chahiye?
Kyunki products evolve hote hain aur user behavior shift hota hai — purane golden examples live code paths ko exercise nahi karte, purane failure modes gayab ho jate hain aur naye aa jate hain. Har flywheel cycle me real failures se naye examples add karo, stale examples audit karke retire karo, error taxonomy periodically revisit karo, aur improvements ko CI se guzaro taaki wo model updates ke across persist karein. Ek informal loop bhi compound karta hai — har hafte kuch traces review karo, golden set update karo, sabse kharab prompt fix karo.
